title: Inter-batch delay also runs after the final batch, holding the pull-to-refresh spinner an extra second
detail: `delay(INTER_BATCH_DELAY_MS)` is unconditionally executed at the end of every iteration of `library.chunked(BATCH_SIZE).forEach { ... }`, including the last batch. On Desktop/iOS, LibraryRefreshRepositoryImpl keeps `inlineRefreshing = true` until this use case returns, so the Library pull-to-refresh spinner (and any per-call feedback) is delayed by 1 extra second after all fetch/persist work has already completed. A throttling delay is only needed BETWEEN batches.
evidence: L47-55: `library.chunked(BATCH_SIZE).forEach { batch -> ...; total += counts.sum(); delay(INTER_BATCH_DELAY_MS) }` — no last-batch guard. LibraryRefreshRepositoryImpl.refresh() sets `inlineRefreshing.value = false` only in the `finally` after `refreshAllChapters()` returns.
suggestedFix: Iterate with `forEachIndexed` over the chunked list (captured in a val) and skip the delay on the last index, e.g. `val batches = library.chunked(BATCH_SIZE); batches.forEachIndexed { i, batch -> ...; if (i < batches.lastIndex) delay(INTER_BATCH_DELAY_MS) }`.
verifierNote: delay(INTER_BATCH_DELAY_MS) at L54 runs at the end of every chunked batch including the last; LibraryRefreshRepositoryImpl clears inlineRefreshing only in the finally after refreshAllChapters() returns, so the Desktop/iOS pull-to-refresh spinner is held 1 extra second after all work completes. Suggested forEachIndexed/lastIndex fix compiles and only removes the trailing delay.

title: Total-timeout abort is reported as plain Success with no partial-result signal
detail: If TOTAL_TIMEOUT_MS (15 min) fires mid-run, `withTimeoutOrNull` cancels the remaining batches and the function returns `AppResult.Success(total)` with only the chapters discovered so far — indistinguishable from a complete refresh. On Desktop/iOS a user with a large library (or several slow/timing-out sources at 30s each) gets a success result implying the whole library was checked when later manga were never fetched. Likewise every per-manga failure is coerced to 0 (explicitly by design per the inline comment), so a refresh where every source failed also reports Success(0) ('no new chapters'). The per-manga swallow matches the stated design; the silent total-timeout truncation is the part worth an owner decision (e.g. a partial flag or count of skipped manga in the result).
evidence: L46 `withTimeoutOrNull(TOTAL_TIMEOUT_MS) { ... }` returns null on timeout and the partial `total` accumulated before cancellation is returned at L57 as `AppResult.Success(total)`; nothing records that the run was truncated.
suggestedFix: Capture whether the timeout fired (e.g. `val completed = withTimeoutOrNull(...) { ... } != null`) and surface it — either return a result type carrying (newChapters, completedFully) or at minimum log the truncation via the :core logging SPI so support/QA can distinguish a truncated refresh from a complete one. Owner decision on whether the UI should message partial completion.
verifierNote: Verified: withTimeoutOrNull(TOTAL_TIMEOUT_MS) at L46 returns null on the 15-min timeout, and the partial pre-timeout total is returned as AppResult.Success(total) at L57 with no truncation signal; per-manga failures are coerced to 0 by design (L72), so an all-failed run also reads Success(0). Silent truncation is real; surfacing it changes the result contract, so risky/owner-decision is right.

title: Incognito gate runs a full recursive cache-folder walk on every chapter open / Next / Prev
detail: RecordHistoryUseCase reads the incognito flag via `observeSettings().first()`. `SettingsRepositoryImpl.observeSettings()` is a COLD flow whose snapshot is a `combine(booleans, cbz, cacheSize)`; the first emission cannot happen until the cacheSize source emits, and that source computes `legacy.formatSize(legacy.getCacheFolderSize())` — `AppFileSystem.folderSize()` does an okio `listRecursively` + per-file `metadataOrNull` stat over the ENTIRE cache directory (manga page caches can be thousands of files / GBs). So every chapter open and every Next/Prev navigation (ReaderViewModel L446 and L623 both call `viewModelScope.launch { recordHistory(...) }`) pays a fresh full cache walk plus a fresh subscription to 5 pref flows + 2 DataStore flows, just to read one boolean. Two secondary effects: (1) the history upsert is delayed by the walk duration, and because the call is a fire-and-forget `viewModelScope.launch`, a user who opens a chapter and backs out before the walk completes gets the coroutine cancelled and NO history row recorded (legacy recorded promptly on open); (2) the KDoc claim "the snapshot flow always has a current value; `first()` is the cheapest read of 'incognito right now'" is factually wrong — the flow is cold with no current value at subscription. A narrow incognito read exists in the legacy facade (`SettingsRepository.incognitoFlow`, a single DataStore cell) but is not surfaced through the rework domain interface.
evidence: RecordHistoryUseCase.kt L40: `if (observeSettings().first().incognito) return`. SettingsRepositoryImpl.kt L183-187: `val cacheSize: Flow<String> = cacheRefresh.onStart { emit(Unit) }.map { legacy.formatSize(legacy.getCacheFolderSize()) }`; L188 `combine(booleans, cbz, cacheSize)`. AppFileSystem.kt L111-123: `fs.listRecursively(dir).forEach { ... metadataOrNull ... }`.
suggestedFix: Expose a narrow incognito accessor on the rework domain SettingsRepository (e.g. `fun observeIncognito(): Flow<Boolean>` delegating to the legacy `incognitoFlow`) and have RecordHistoryUseCase depend on that (directly or via a tiny ObserveIncognitoUseCase) instead of the full SettingsSnapshot stream. This removes the cache walk from the chapter-open hot path and makes the history write near-instant.
verifierNote: Chain verified: RecordHistoryUseCase.kt:40 first() on the COLD observeSettings() whose combine cannot emit until cacheSize emits (SettingsRepositoryImpl.kt:183-187), which runs legacy getCacheFolderSize() = fs.folderSize(fs.cacheDir) (shared settings/domain/SettingsRepository.kt:116) = full okio listRecursively + per-file metadata walk (AppFileSystem.kt:111-123); fired per chapter open/next/prev/scroll-crossing (ReaderViewModel.kt:446, 623) as fire-and-forget, so a quick back-out cancels before the upsert and loses the history row. Narrow legacy incognitoFlow exists (SettingsRepositoryImpl.kt:167) but is not surfaced. KDoc 'always has a current value' is false.

title: Cache-first saved-details read bypasses the declared AppResult error contract
detail: The KDoc's error-semantics section (L45-50) promises that all failures "surface as AppResult.Failure", but the cache-first branch added later calls `savedDetails.observeSavedDetails(manga.api, manga.title).first()` — a raw Flow over Room DAO reads (`SavedMangaDetailsRepositoryImpl` does `mangaDao.getIdByApiAndTitle` / `chapterDao.getChaptersByMangaId` inside a plain `flow {}` with no catch). Any SQLite/IO exception there escapes the use case as a thrown exception rather than `AppResult.Failure`; the sole call site (`ReaderViewModel.runListChapters`, `when (val result = listChapters(manga))` inside `viewModelScope.launch` with no try/catch) would then crash the app instead of taking the documented silent-failure branch. Rare in practice (Room read failure), but it is the only path in this use case that violates the typed-error boundary the file itself documents.
evidence: L120: `val saved = savedDetails.observeSavedDetails(manga.api, manga.title).first()` — no exception mapping; contrast with L125 `repository.fetchDetails(manga)` which returns AppResult. ReaderViewModel.kt L786-806 has no try/catch around the call.
suggestedFix: Wrap the saved-details read: `val saved = try { savedDetails.observeSavedDetails(...).first() } catch (e: CancellationException) { throw e } catch (e: Exception) { null }` so a local-cache read failure degrades to the network path instead of escaping the AppResult contract.
verifierNote: SavedMangaDetailsRepositoryImpl.kt:39-52 is a plain flow{} over Room DAO suspend reads with no catch; ListChaptersUseCase.kt:120 .first() lets any SQLite/IO exception escape the AppResult contract the KDoc (L45-50) declares, and ReaderViewModel.runListChapters (L782-806) has no try/catch — uncaught in viewModelScope = crash instead of the documented silent-failure branch.

title: Toggle is documented as 'atomic' but is a non-atomic check-then-act; rapid double-toggle can desync UI from DB
detail: KDoc L10 says "Toggle a manga's library membership atomically", but the implementation is a read-then-write: `repository.get(...)` then branch to `addToLibrary` or `removeFromLibrary` (L65-73). Two concurrent invocations (e.g. double-tap on the heart icon — each intent is launched on a fresh coroutine per MviViewModel.submit) can both observe the same membership snapshot and both take the same branch; both calls then return the same Boolean, so the caller's optimistic UI state can end up inverted relative to the actual DB row (e.g. both observe 'absent' -> both add -> both return true; UI toggled twice shows 'not in library' while the row exists). Outcomes are mostly benign because add is an upsert and remove is idempotent, but the returned membership Boolean — explicitly documented as the way callers "update UI without re-querying" — is unreliable under the race, and the 'atomically' claim is simply not what the code does.
evidence: L65-73: `val existing = repository.get(...); return existing.flatMap { current -> if (current == null) repository.addToLibrary(...) ... else repository.removeFromLibrary(...) }` — no transaction/mutex spanning the read and the write.
suggestedFix: Either push the toggle into a single transactional repository operation (Room transaction doing the membership check + write) and keep the Boolean derived from the actual write, or correct the KDoc to drop 'atomically' and note the benign-race caveat. Doc correction alone is safe; the transactional change is the real fix if double-tap desync is observed.
verifierNote: The 'atomically' KDoc (L10) is genuinely false — L65-73 is an unguarded read-then-write. But the 'UI desync from DB' narrative is overstated: because add is an upsert and remove idempotent, every interleaving leaves the returned Boolean consistent with the final DB state (both-read-absent -> both add -> both return true -> row present). Real residue: stale doc + double-tap collapsing to one toggle. Doc fix is the safe action.

title: Use case is named/documented as an idempotent 'mark as read' but the full chain is a read-state TOGGLE
detail: The KDoc states the upstream flow 're-emits with the entry's isRead = true once the Room transaction commits' and that the per-row button 'vanishes by virtue of the if (!entry.isRead) guard in the :ui composable'. In reality the chain ends at LibraryDeo.markChapterAndNotificationRead -> 'UPDATE notifications SET isRead = NOT isRead WHERE chapterId = :chapterId' (+ the matching saved_chapters flip), i.e. a toggle, not a set-true. The rework UI now deliberately RELIES on toggle semantics: UpdatesScreen.kt:459-464 dispatches OnMarkAsRead from swipe StartToEnd with NO !isRead guard ('drop the guard to restore native's swipe-to-toggle behavior exactly. (The VM's OnMarkAsRead handler has no guard, so this is the only gate.)'), so a read row swiped right is flipped back to UNREAD — the opposite of what this use case's name and KDoc promise. The toggle SQL matches native (parity, not a bug), but the use case's contract documentation is now wrong, and any future caller that assumes invoke() is an idempotent mark-read (e.g. calling it twice, or calling it on an already-read entry) will silently un-read the chapter in both notifications and saved_chapters.

SET isRead = NOT isRead'; ui/.../updates/UpdatesScreen.kt:441 'underlying use case is isRead = NOT isRead', :460-464 unguarded swipe dispatch.
suggestedFix: Rewrite the use case KDoc to document the actual toggle semantics (mark-unread on an already-read entry, swipe-to-toggle parity) and the non-idempotency; optionally rename to ToggleUpdateReadUseCase (rename is an owner decision — the doc correction alone is safe).

title: Rewarded-ad earned-reward signal stored in a weakly-referenced array that GC can collect mid-ad, silently dropping the user's reward
detail: showRewarded() arbitrates the terminal result via `val terminal = WeakReference(arrayOfNulls<AdResult>(1))`. After construction NOTHING holds a strong reference to the 1-element array — both the FullScreenContentCallback and the OnUserEarnedRewardListener capture only the WeakReference object itself. The array is therefore weakly reachable from the moment it is created and is eligible for collection at any GC. A rewarded ad plays for 15-45s of allocation-heavy video, so GC during the ad is the NORM, not the exception. When the array is collected: (a) the reward listener's `terminal.get()?.set(0, EarnedReward)` is a no-op, and (b) onAdDismissedFullScreenContent resumes with `terminal.get()?.get(0) ?: AdResult.Dismissed` = Dismissed — the user watched the full ad, AdMob recorded the reward, but the app reports Dismissed and withholds whatever the reward gates. This binding is LIVE (shared/src/androidMain/.../di/PlatformModule.android.kt:157 binds AndroidAdProvider). The KDoc rationale ('avoids leaking the array through the SDK's callback chain') is unsound: a 1-cell array held only for the duration of one ad show is not a leak, and the callbacks already strongly hold the continuation anyway.
evidence: val terminal = WeakReference(arrayOfNulls<AdResult>(1)) ... ad.show(activity) { _ -> terminal.get()?.set(0, AdResult.EarnedReward) } ... override fun onAdDismissedFullScreenContent() { val result = terminal.get()?.get(0) ?: AdResult.Dismissed; if (cont.isActive) cont.resume(result) }
suggestedFix: Replace the WeakReference with a strongly-referenced holder: `val terminal = arrayOfNulls<AdResult>(1)` (or simply `var earned = false` set in the reward listener and read in onAdDismissedFullScreenContent). The holder's lifetime is naturally bounded by the ad-show callbacks, which AdMob releases on dismissal. Note the legacy :shared twin documents the same 'verbatim' pattern and should get the same fix when touched.
verifierNote: The weak-reachability analysis is correct (AndroidAdProvider.kt:153 — nothing strongly references the 1-cell array, both callbacks capture only the WeakReference, GC mid-ad silently drops EarnedReward) and the binding is live (PlatformModule.android.kt:157). Downgraded to minor: grep across :presentation/:domain/:data/:composeApp/:shared/:app finds ZERO callers of showRewarded/loadRewarded — rewarded ads exist only in native-app. Latent defect on an unused facade today; the one-line strong-holder fix is safe and should land before the parity port wires rewarded ads.

title: No partial-archive cleanup on failure/cancellation — Android leaves a corrupt chapter_N.cbz behind, unlike the iOS/Desktop siblings (fix #28 never reached Android)
detail: Both createCbz (line 44) and createCbzWithSplitting (line 91) open `ZipOutputStream(FileOutputStream(cbzFile))` at the final destination path (`chapterDir/chapter_$chapterId.cbz`). If the write fails partway — cancellation via ensureActive()/yield() (lines 46-47, 93-94), disk-full IOException from putNextEntry, or OOM during decode outside the per-page catch — the exception propagates, `.use{}` closes the stream, and a truncated/corrupt .cbz remains at the canonical path. IosCbzWriter (lines 109-112) and DesktopCbzWriter explicitly delete the partial archive and rethrow (parity fix #28, commit bde51aab); the Android writer — the one actually bound in the live graph (PlatformModule.android.kt:137 `single<CbzWriter> { AndroidCbzWriter(get()) }`) — was skipped. Downstream offline-read code that probes for the file at the canonical path can treat the corrupt partial archive as a completed download. Cancelling an in-flight chapter download is a routine user action, so this is realistically hit.
evidence: ZipOutputStream(FileOutputStream(cbzFile)).use { zipOut -> ... ensureActive() ... } — no try/catch around the archive write; contrast IosCbzWriter.kt:109-112: `catch (t: Throwable) { runCatching { system.delete(cbzPath) }; throw t }`.
suggestedFix: Mirror the iOS/Desktop pattern in both methods: wrap the ZipOutputStream block in try/catch(Throwable), on failure `runCatching { cbzFile.delete() }` then rethrow; only delete the source page files after a fully successful archive.
verifierNote: Missing #28 cleanup is real (AndroidCbzWriter.kt:44/:91 have no try/catch around the archive write vs IosCbzWriter.kt:109-112 / DesktopCbzWriter.kt:108-110; binding live at PlatformModule.android.kt:137). Impact overstated, downgraded: Android chapter downloads do NOT use AndroidCbzWriter — ChapterDownloadService.kt:186/318 calls OptimizedCbzManager.createCbzParallel; the only Android consumer is the Settings bulk CBZ conversion (SettingsRepositoryImpl). On cancellation the DB row is never rewritten and loose pages survive, so the truncated .cbz is inert junk (disk space + cache-size skew), overwritten on re-run; nothing probes the canonical path outside the DB, so 'treated as completed download' does not hold.

title: Dead Build.VERSION check against KITKAT (API 19) — :platform minSdk is 26
detail: `if (Build.VERSION.SDK_INT >= Build.VERSION_CODES.KITKAT)` is always true (platform/build.gradle.kts sets minSdk = 26), so the `@Suppress("DEPRECATION") bitmap.byteCount` else-branch is unreachable dead code. The same file already relies on minSdk 26 elsewhere (chooseWebpFormat only guards against R).
evidence: val byteSize = if (Build.VERSION.SDK_INT >= Build.VERSION_CODES.KITKAT) { bitmap.allocationByteCount.toLong() } else { @Suppress("DEPRECATION") bitmap.byteCount.toLong() }
suggestedFix: Replace with `val byteSize = bitmap.allocationByteCount.toLong()`.
verifierNote: platform/build.gradle.kts:226 sets minSdk=26, so AndroidCbzWriter.kt:107 SDK_INT >= KITKAT (19) is always true and the @Suppress(DEPRECATION) else-branch is unreachable. Replacement with allocationByteCount is behavior-identical.

title: createCbzWithSplitting: a compress failure after putNextEntry leaves pageCounter unincremented, so the next page reuses the same ZipEntry name and every subsequent putNextEntry throws ZipException (duplicate entry)
detail: In both the chunked (lines 120-131) and non-chunked (lines 134-145) branches, `pageCounter++` only happens inside the try after closeEntry(). If putNextEntry succeeds but compress/closeEntry throws (disk-full, encoder error), the entry name `page_NNNN.webp` is already committed to the archive, yet the counter is not advanced — the next iteration calls putNextEntry with the identical name, and java.util.zip.ZipOutputStream throws ZipException 'duplicate entry', which the per-page catch swallows; this repeats for every remaining page, silently producing an archive missing all pages after the first failure. createCbz is immune because it names entries by the loop index.
evidence: try { zipOut.putNextEntry(ZipEntry(pageEntryName(pageCounter))) ... zipOut.closeEntry(); pageCounter++ } catch (e: Exception) { log.e(e) { ... } }
suggestedFix: Move `pageCounter++` into a finally block (or increment immediately after a successful putNextEntry) so a failed page never re-uses a committed entry name.
verifierNote: Verified L118-131/L133-145: pageCounter++ only executes after closeEntry() inside the try; java.util.zip.ZipOutputStream.putNextEntry throws ZipException on a duplicate name (names HashSet), the per-page catch swallows it, so one mid-archive compress failure silently drops every subsequent page. createCbz is immune (index-named). finally/post-putNextEntry increment fixes it.

title: KDoc says 'depth-first walk' but the ArrayDeque is used as a FIFO queue (removeFirst + addLast) — the walk is breadth-first
detail: safeWalkFiles adds children with `stack.add(file)` (addLast) and consumes with `stack.removeFirst()` — that is a queue, i.e. breadth-first traversal. The class KDoc (and the legacy doc it mirrors) claims depth-first. Functionally irrelevant for summing sizes, but the doc contradicts the code.
evidence: KDoc: 'depth-first walk via an `ArrayDeque<File>`' vs code: `val dir = stack.removeFirst()` after `stack.add(root)`/`stack.add(file)`.
suggestedFix: Either fix the KDoc to say breadth-first, or use `removeLast()` to make it genuinely depth-first (LIFO).
verifierNote: AndroidFileSizeFormatter.kt:26-33 — stack.add (addLast) + stack.removeFirst() is a FIFO queue = breadth-first; KDoc L12 (and the postscript) say depth-first. Functionally irrelevant for size summing; doc-only fix.

title: saveBitmapBytesToGallery leaks an orphaned MediaStore row when the write fails after insert
detail: After `resolver.insert(...)` succeeds, three failure paths exit without deleting the inserted row: (a) openOutputStream returns null (line 62-63 returns null directly), (b) `it.write(bytes)` throws into the outer catch, (c) the IS_PENDING=0 update throws. On API 29+ the row is stuck IS_PENDING (system purges it only after ~a week); on API 26-28 (pre-Q branch) an empty 0-byte image stays permanently visible in the user's gallery. The user also gets a null/failure result, so nothing references the row.
evidence: val uri: Uri = resolver.insert(collection, values) ?: return@withContext null; resolver.openOutputStream(uri)?.use { it.write(bytes) } ?: return@withContext null — no resolver.delete(uri, null, null) on any failure path.
suggestedFix: On any failure after a successful insert, call `runCatching { resolver.delete(uri, null, null) }` before returning null (track the uri in a var visible to the catch block).
verifierNote: Verified L59-74: after resolver.insert succeeds, openOutputStream==null returns null directly (L62-63), and write/IS_PENDING-update exceptions hit the outer catch returning null — no resolver.delete on any path. Q+ leaves a stuck IS_PENDING row; API 26-28 leaves a permanent 0-byte gallery image.

title: shareBitmapBytes builds a filename from an unsanitized title — a '/' in a scraped manga title makes the share silently fail
detail: `File(cacheImages, "${title.ifBlank { DEFAULT_FILE_STEM }}.png")` uses the caller-supplied title verbatim as a file name. Titles originate from scraped third-party sites and routinely contain '/', ':' or other separators (e.g. 'Fate/Stay Night'); a '/' makes FileOutputStream throw FileNotFoundException (missing subdirectory), which the catch swallows with only a log — the user taps Share and nothing happens. A crafted title with '../' segments would also escape the images/ subdir (still confined to cacheDir, so impact is low, but FileProvider path mapping can then fail or expose a different cache file).
evidence: val file = File(cacheImages, "${title.ifBlank { DEFAULT_FILE_STEM }}.png"); FileOutputStream(file).use { it.write(bytes) }
suggestedFix: Sanitize the stem before use, e.g. `title.replace(Regex("[^A-Za-z0-9._ -]"), "_").take(64).ifBlank { DEFAULT_FILE_STEM }`.
verifierNote: L81 File(cacheImages, "$title.png") uses scraped titles verbatim; a '/' (e.g. 'Fate/Stay Night') yields FileNotFoundException swallowed at L100-102 — user taps Share, nothing happens. '../' stays confined to cacheDir, so minor + sanitize-stem fix is right.

title: schedulePeriodic ignores job.uniqueWorkName and uses plain enqueue — repeated scheduling stacks duplicate periodic workers
detail: scheduleOneOff was fixed (#8) to use enqueueUniqueWork(REPLACE) when `job.uniqueWorkName != null`, but schedulePeriodic always calls `workManager.enqueue(request)`. WorkManager periodic requests persist across process restarts, so any caller that schedules a periodic job on each app start (the typical pattern) will accumulate N parallel periodic workers, each firing on its own 15-min-clamped cadence. There are currently no production callers of schedulePeriodic (verified by grep), so this is latent, but the asymmetry with the one-off path is a trap for the planned Phase-11 worker port.
evidence: scheduleOneOff: `if (uniqueName != null) workManager.enqueueUniqueWork(uniqueName, ExistingWorkPolicy.REPLACE, request) else workManager.enqueue(request)` vs schedulePeriodic: `workManager.enqueue(request)` with no uniqueWorkName branch.
suggestedFix: Mirror the one-off path: when `job.uniqueWorkName != null`, use `workManager.enqueueUniquePeriodicWork(uniqueName, ExistingPeriodicWorkPolicy.UPDATE, request)`.
verifierNote: Verified: scheduleOneOff branches on uniqueWorkName (L65-70, enqueueUniqueWork REPLACE) while schedulePeriodic always plain-enqueues (L93) — periodic requests persist, so repeat scheduling would stack workers. No production callers today (grep confirms; latent). WorkManager 2.10.1 has ExistingPeriodicWorkPolicy.UPDATE, so the mirrored fix compiles.

title: catch (e: Exception) around Task.await() swallows CancellationException in getDoc/setDoc/deleteDoc/query
detail: All four suspend members wrap a real suspension point (`.await()` from kotlinx-coroutines-play-services) in `catch (e: Exception)`. When the calling coroutine is cancelled while awaiting, await() throws CancellationException, which is an Exception — it gets logged as a spurious 'failed' warning and converted to null/emptyList/no-op instead of propagating. The caller's cancelled coroutine then continues executing with a misleading 'doc absent / empty result' value until its next suspension point. The project contract (CLAUDE.md / contract §9-10) requires CancellationException to always be rethrown. Same pattern at lines 64, 72 and 113.
evidence: return try { val snapshot = resolveDoc(path).get().await() ... } catch (e: Exception) { log.w(e) { "getDoc($path) failed" }; null }
suggestedFix: Add `catch (e: CancellationException) { throw e }` before the generic catch in each of the four methods (or `if (e is CancellationException) throw e` at the top of the catch).
verifierNote: AndroidRemoteDocStore.kt:51-58, 61-67, 69-75, 96-117 — all four suspend members catch Exception around .await(); CancellationException is swallowed into null/emptyList/no-op. The 'verbatim port' KDoc covers swallow-on-failure semantics, not cancellation; rethrowing CancellationException preserves those semantics for real failures.

title: getToken/deleteToken (and observeTokens' initial fetch) swallow CancellationException via catch (e: Exception) around await()
detail: Same contract violation as AndroidRemoteDocStore: `FirebaseMessaging.getInstance().token.await()` is a suspension point; cancellation of the calling coroutine surfaces as CancellationException, which is caught, logged as 'Failed to fetch FCM token', and converted to null — the cancelled caller keeps running with a null token instead of unwinding. Applies to getToken (line 27-32), deleteToken (line 34-40) and the initial fetch inside observeTokens' callbackFlow (line 43-48).
evidence: override suspend fun getToken(): String? = try { FirebaseMessaging.getInstance().token.await() } catch (e: Exception) { log.w(e) { "Failed to fetch FCM token" }; null }
suggestedFix: Rethrow CancellationException before the generic catch in all three sites.
verifierNote: AndroidPushTokenProvider.kt:27-32 (getToken), 34-40 (deleteToken), 43-48 (observeTokens initial fetch) all wrap Task.await() in catch (e: Exception) — kotlinx-coroutines-tasks await rethrows CancellationException on caller cancellation, which gets logged and converted to null, violating the repo-wide rethrow contract.

title: requestReview swallows CancellationException via catch (e: Exception) around the two Play Core await() calls
detail: requestReviewFlow().await() and launchReviewFlow(...).await() are suspension points inside `catch (e: Exception)`. Cancellation of the calling coroutine is logged as 'requestReview failed' and converted to false instead of propagating, violating the project's CancellationException-rethrow contract.
evidence: return try { val reviewInfo = manager.requestReviewFlow().await(); manager.launchReviewFlow(activity, reviewInfo).await(); true } catch (e: Exception) { log.w(e) { "requestReview failed" }; false }
suggestedFix: Add `catch (e: CancellationException) { throw e }` before the generic catch.
verifierNote: AndroidInAppReviewClient.kt:37-44 — both requestReviewFlow().await() and launchReviewFlow(...).await() sit inside catch (e: Exception); cancellation is logged as 'requestReview failed' and converted to false. Same contract violation as the sibling Play Core/Firebase facades.

title: NSAllowsArbitraryLoads=true disables App Transport Security for ALL hosts — far broader than the Android parity config (one cleartext domain)
detail: The Android host scopes cleartext to a single domain (app/src/main/res/xml/network_security_config.xml permits only raijinscan.co); the iOS plist disables ATS globally, allowing unencrypted HTTP and weak-TLS connections to every host. For a scraping app some HTTP sources may be needed, but the blanket opt-out removes MITM protection for all traffic (including Firebase-adjacent and image CDN requests) and requires justification at App Store review. This is also a platform-parity divergence in both directions (iOS allows cleartext everywhere; Android blocks it except one domain).
evidence: <key>NSAppTransportSecurity</key><dict><key>NSAllowsArbitraryLoads</key><true/></dict>
suggestedFix: Replace the blanket flag with NSExceptionDomains entries for the specific hosts that need cleartext/weak TLS (at minimum raijinscan.co, mirroring Android), or inventory which of the ~50 sources are HTTP-only before deciding. Owner decision on source coverage.
verifierNote: Info.plist:47-51 sets NSAllowsArbitraryLoads=true globally; Android's network_security_config.xml permits cleartext only for raijinscan.co. Real two-way platform divergence and a blanket ATS opt-out needing App Store justification. Restricting it could break HTTP-only sources — owner decision, risky.

title: Room version skew: room-runtime/ktx/compiler at 2.8.4 but room-paging pinned at 2.6.1 (paging-room)
detail: `androidx-room-paging` resolves to androidx.room:room-paging:2.6.1 (libs.versions.toml line 56/129) while the rest of Room — runtime, ktx, compiler, gradle plugin — is 2.8.4. Gradle conflict-resolution upgrades room-runtime to 2.8.4 on the Android classpath, so room-paging 2.6.1's binary (compiled against 2.6.x internals like LimitOffsetPagingSource) runs against a runtime two minor versions newer, and the 2.8.4 KSP compiler generates paging code that targets the 2.8.x room-paging API surface. The shared/build.gradle.kts comment justifying the pin ('paging artifact is Android-only at present') is stale — room-paging has shipped KMP artifacts since Room 2.7.0. Risk: NoSuchMethodError/AbstractMethodError on the chapter-downloads PagingSource path at runtime. The app has reportedly smoke-tested downloads, so this may currently work by luck of binary compatibility, but the skew is fragile.
evidence: [versions] room = "2.8.4" ... paging-room = "2.6.1"; androidx-room-paging = { group = "androidx.room", name = "room-paging", version.ref = "paging-room" } — consumed in shared/build.gradle.kts androidMain (line 157).
suggestedFix: Point androidx-room-paging at version.ref = "room" (2.8.4), delete the paging-room version entry, and re-run the compile gate + a downloads-screen smoke test on Android.
verifierNote: Skew is real (libs.versions.toml: room=2.8.4 L19, paging-room=2.6.1 L56, consumed shared/build.gradle.kts:157) and the 'Android-only' comment is stale — but the runtime-failure claim is unfounded: zero Kotlin files import androidx.paging or androidx.room.paging, no DAO returns PagingSource (ChapterDownloadDao.kt:184-189 documents the paged methods were REMOVED), so there is no 'chapter-downloads PagingSource path'. It is an unused dependency; aligning to version.ref="room" or deleting it is safe.

title: catch (e: Exception) swallows CancellationException in all three suspend methods
detail: checkForUpdate (line 47), startFlexibleUpdate (line 69) and completeUpdate (line 79) wrap real suspension points (Play Core Task.await()) in catch (e: Exception). When the calling coroutine is cancelled (e.g. MainActivity destroyed mid-check; this binding IS live via shared/src/androidMain/.../di/PlatformModule.android.kt:158 and consumed by app/MainActivity), the CancellationException thrown by await() is caught, logged as a spurious 'checkForUpdate failed' warning, and converted into the null/false 'no update' result instead of propagating cancellation. This violates the repo-wide contract (CLAUDE.md: 'CancellationException is always re-thrown') and breaks structured concurrency. User-visible impact is bounded (callers are themselves cancelled), hence minor.
evidence: return try { val info = manager.appUpdateInfo.await() ... } catch (e: Exception) { log.w(e) { "checkForUpdate failed" }; null }
suggestedFix: In each of the three methods add `catch (e: CancellationException) { throw e }` before the generic `catch (e: Exception)` (import kotlinx.coroutines.CancellationException).
verifierNote: AndroidAppUpdateClient.kt:36-51, 53-73, 75-83 — all three suspend methods wrap Play Core Task.await() in catch (e: Exception), converting caller cancellation into null/false 'no update' results. The 'return false on any throw' legacy semantics are preserved for real failures by rethrowing CancellationException first.

title: get()/put() can throw on corrupted keyset, violating the SecureStorage interface contract
detail: The SecureStorage interface (platform/.../storage/SecureStorage.kt:72) documents get() as returning 'null if absent / corrupted / cipher-mismatched'. The Android impl does not honor that: EncryptedSharedPreferences.getString throws SecurityException on a value that fails AES-GCM decryption, and the lazy `prefs` initializer rethrows GeneralSecurityException/IOException on a corrupted keyset — a well-known real-world state after Android auto-backup restore (prefs file restored, Keystore master key not). The only current caller (app/MainActivity.startInAppReviewFlow) happens to wrap everything in catch(Throwable), so nothing crashes today, but any future caller written against the documented contract (the KDoc pitches this store for auth tokens) will crash instead of degrading.
evidence: override suspend fun get(key: String): String? = withContext(Dispatchers.IO) { prefs.getString(key, null) } — no guard around lazy keystore init or decryption failure, while the interface promises null on corruption.
suggestedFix: Wrap the body of get() in try/catch returning null on SecurityException/GeneralSecurityException (log via Kermit); consider deleting-and-recreating the prefs file on keyset corruption like Jetpack Security docs recommend. put()/remove() should similarly log rather than propagate, or the interface KDoc must be corrected.
verifierNote: SecureStorage.kt:72 promises 'null if absent / corrupted / cipher-mismatched'; AndroidSecureStorage.kt:29-50 has no guard — the lazy EncryptedSharedPreferences init rethrows GeneralSecurityException/IOException on a corrupted keyset and getString throws SecurityException on decryption failure. Sole caller MainActivity.startInAppReviewFlow:129-145 happens to catch Throwable, so latent today but contract-violating.

title: headersMapFlow is dead and semantically stale after the #12 per-API key change
detail: headersMapFlow observes only the legacy aggregate key StorageKeys.HEADERS_MAP_JSON, but since the #12 change saveHeadersForApi writes exclusively to per-API hashed keys ('headers.' + base36 hash) and never updates the aggregate. So the flow can only ever emit headers persisted before #12 and will never reflect any new Cloudflare/header capture. Repo-wide grep finds zero consumers of headersMapFlow (only the definition and native-app's own separate copy), so nothing is broken today — but it is a loaded trap for the documented 'pure import swap' migration of legacy consumers, and dead weight meanwhile.
evidence: val headersMapFlow = settings.getStringFlow(StorageKeys.HEADERS_MAP_JSON, "").map { parseHeadersMap(it) } vs saveHeadersForApi which does settings.putString(keyForApi(api), encodeSingleHeaders(api, headers)) and never touches HEADERS_MAP_JSON.
suggestedFix: Either delete headersMapFlow (no consumers exist) or reimplement it to merge the per-API keys with the legacy aggregate so it stays truthful. Owner should pick; deletion shrinks the byte-for-byte-preserved API surface the KDoc promises.
verifierNote: Verified: headersMapFlow (L87-89) observes only StorageKeys.HEADERS_MAP_JSON while saveHeadersForApi (L100-107) writes exclusively to per-API hashed keys and never updates the aggregate — the flow can never reflect post-#12 captures. Repo-wide grep finds zero consumers (definition only). Deletion shrinks the byte-for-byte-preserved API surface the KDoc promises, so owner pick / risky stands.

title: addReadMinutes is a non-atomic read-modify-write; concurrent increments lose minutes
detail: addReadMinutes does getInt followed by putInt with no synchronization. multiplatform-settings offers no atomic increment, so two concurrent reading-session ends (e.g. session-end plus a periodic flush, or two windows on Desktop) can interleave and drop one delta, silently undercounting the statistics screen's total reading time. The legacy native implementation used DataStore's transactional edit{} which did not have this race. Probability is low (writes happen at session end), data loss is small — minor.
evidence: suspend fun addReadMinutes(delta: Int) { val current = settings.getInt(StorageKeys.READ_MINUTES, 0); settings.putInt(StorageKeys.READ_MINUTES, current + delta) }
suggestedFix: Guard the read-modify-write with a private kotlinx.coroutines.sync.Mutex (mutex.withLock { ... }) in DataStoreHelper, which serializes all increments in-process.
verifierNote: DataStoreHelper.kt:153-156 — getInt-then-putInt with no synchronization; multiplatform-settings has no atomic increment, so concurrent increments can drop a delta. Single production caller today (legacy StatisticsRepository.kt:101) keeps probability low — minor is honestly calibrated; in-class Mutex fix is safe and behavior-preserving.

title: Blocking ZIP/disk I/O runs on hardcoded Dispatchers.Default instead of an injected IO dispatcher
detail: pageCount, extractImages, deleteCbz and cleanupExtractedCache all do blocking okio file I/O (full-archive extraction can be tens of MB) inside withContext(Dispatchers.Default). The Default pool is sized to CPU core count and is shared with decode/layout work — a large chapter extraction while the reader is decoding pages can starve CPU-bound coroutines. The project already has a DispatcherProvider in :core (and an IoDispatcher expect/actual precedent) exactly for this; on Android/Desktop the IO pool is the correct home. Hardcoding Dispatchers also makes the class untestable with a test dispatcher.
evidence: override suspend fun pageCount(cbzPath: Path): Int = withContext(Dispatchers.Default) { ... zipFs.listRecursively ... } — same pattern at lines 88, 133, 149.
suggestedFix: Inject the :core DispatcherProvider (or a CoroutineDispatcher) through the constructor and use its io dispatcher (mapped to Dispatchers.Default on iOS where IO is unavailable); update the Koin binding accordingly.
verifierNote: Verified withContext(Dispatchers.Default) at L70, 88, 133, 149 around blocking okio zip extraction/deletion; the class is live (injected as CbzReader into ChapterPagesRepositoryImpl, the rework reader path), and :core DispatcherProvider exists precisely for this. Constructor + Koin binding change across three targets keeps the fix risky.

title: formatBytes drops localized byte units on a false premise and truncates instead of rounding
detail: The KDoc justifies hardcoding English unit suffixes with 'the upstream resources bytes_format_* were English-only anyway' — that is factually wrong: native-app localizes them for Arabic ('%.1f ك.بايت', values-ar/strings.xml:778), French ('%.1f Ko') and Russian ('%.1f КБ'). Since Arabic is the app's primary audience, downloaded-chapter/storage sizes now regress to English units, an i18n parity loss the doc actively denies. Additionally, the rounding differs from native: (value * 10).toLong() / 10.0 truncates (1.59 MB renders as '1.5 MB') whereas native's %.1f rounds half-up ('1.6 MB').
evidence: internal fun formatBytes(...): val rounded = (value * 10).toLong() / 10.0; return "$rounded $unit" with unit hardcoded to B/KB/MB/GB/TB; KDoc lines 25-26 and 92-93 claim upstream was English-only.
suggestedFix: At minimum fix the rounding (use kotlin.math.roundToLong on value*10) and correct the KDoc claim. For full parity, have the formatter return (value, unitOrdinal) and let :ui render the localized unit string from compose-resources.
verifierNote: Both sub-claims verified: native-app DOES localize bytes_format_* (values-ar/strings.xml:777-781, values-fr:698-702, values-ru:695-699), so the KDoc's 'English-only anyway' premise is false; and (value*10).toLong()/10.0 (L106) truncates where native %.1f rounds half-up. Adjusted on fixSafety: the minimal fix (roundToLong + KDoc correction — or delegate to :core formatBytes per xcut-dup-5) is safe; only the full localized-unit re-plumb is an owner-level UI change. Overlaps xcut-dup-5 on the truncation half but its i18n-parity claim is distinct.

title: Completed one-off job futures are never evicted from the `futures` map (unbounded growth)
detail: scheduleOneOff/schedulePeriodic put every ScheduledFuture into `futures` keyed by a fresh UUID, but nothing removes the entry when a one-off job completes. Only cancel(jobId)/cancelAll() evict. Over an app session that schedules repeated one-off jobs (this class is the live Desktop binding: PlatformModule.desktop.kt:118 `single<BackgroundJobScheduler> { DesktopBackgroundJobScheduler() }`), the map grows without bound. Entries are small so this is a slow leak, not a crash, but it is a genuine resource leak in a process-lifetime singleton.
evidence: scheduleOneOff: `futures[id] = future; return id` — no completion hook; cancel() is the only `futures.remove(...)` call site.
suggestedFix: Wrap the scheduled runnable so it removes its own entry when done, e.g. `executor.schedule({ try { runJob(job) } finally { futures.remove(id) } }, ...)` for one-off jobs (periodic futures legitimately stay until cancelled).
verifierNote: DesktopBackgroundJobScheduler.kt:43-52 — scheduleOneOff stores every future in `futures` with no completion eviction; only cancel/cancelAll remove (lines 67-74). Binding is live (PlatformModule.desktop.kt:118 single<BackgroundJobScheduler>) and LibraryRefreshRepositoryImpl.kt:115 calls scheduleOneOff per refresh, so the map grows for the process lifetime. Genuine slow leak.

title: runJob catches Exception only — an Error from a runner silently kills the periodic schedule
detail: ScheduledExecutorService.scheduleAtFixedRate suppresses all subsequent executions if a task throws. runJob only catches Exception, so any Error (OOM during a heavy refresh, ExceptionInInitializerError, NoClassDefFoundError from a lazily-loaded runner dependency) propagates into the FutureTask, is swallowed there unobserved (nobody calls future.get(); observeJobState is a stub returning Idle), and the periodic job (e.g. library auto-refresh) silently stops for the rest of the session with zero log output.
evidence: `try { runner.run(job.data) } catch (e: Exception) { log.e(e) { ... } }` — Throwable subclasses other than Exception escape into the executor task.
suggestedFix: Catch Throwable in runJob (logging it), so periodic scheduling survives and the failure is at least visible in logs.
verifierNote: The catch(Exception)-vs-Error semantics at DesktopBackgroundJobScheduler.kt:90-94 are correctly described, but the failure narrative is unreachable today: registerRunner has ZERO callers (runners map always empty, so runner.run never executes) and schedulePeriodic has zero callers repo-wide — no periodic job exists to be killed. Valid latent hardening, impact claim overstated.

title: `safeName` is not sanitized — displayName/title interpolated raw into the output file path
detail: Despite the variable name, `safeName` performs no sanitization: `"${displayName.ifBlank { DEFAULT_FILE_STEM }}.png"` is passed to `File(galleryDir, safeName)`. A displayName containing '/' (realistic for scraped manga titles like "Fate/Grand Order") makes the write target a non-existent subdirectory (silent failure, returns null), and "../" sequences escape galleryDir entirely (path traversal). The same applies to `title` in shareBitmapBytes (line 58). Today the only wired caller passes the constant "Share screenshot" (ChapterImagesReworkScreenRoute), so the bug is latent, but the SPI invites titles as input.
evidence: `val safeName = "${displayName.ifBlank { DEFAULT_FILE_STEM }}.png"; val out = File(galleryDir, safeName)` — no character filtering despite the 'safe' name.
suggestedFix: Sanitize the stem before use, e.g. `displayName.ifBlank { DEFAULT_FILE_STEM }.replace(Regex("[/\\\\:*?\"<>|]"), "_")` (and the same in shareBitmapBytes), so the name truly is safe.

title: Redundant `|| code == 204` — 204 is already inside 200..299
detail: `if (code in 200..299 || code == 204)` — the second disjunct can never change the result since 204 is in the 2xx range. Harmless but dead condition (the file's own audit postscript even acknowledges "204 ... IS in 200..299"). Also note the iOS sibling uses 200..399, so the two polling actuals classify 3xx responses differently; not a bug per se, but the redundancy invites confusion.

suggestedFix: Drop `|| code == 204` (behavior-identical).
verifierNote: DesktopConnectivityObserver.kt:56 — 204 is in 200..299, so `|| code == 204` is mathematically dead. title: Missing/unreadable pages are silently dropped; an all-skipped archive returns a 0-page CBZ as success
detail: archive() skips a page when the source file is missing (line 85-88) or readBytes fails (line 91-95) with only a log line, and still returns the .cbz path as success — including the degenerate case where EVERY page was skipped, producing an empty archive logged as "Created CBZ with 0 pages". The :data caller compressExistingDownloads (SettingsRepositoryImpl.kt:292) treats the returned path as success and rewrites the chapter row's localImagePaths to point only at the archive, so: (a) partially-skipped pages vanish from the reader while their loose files stay orphaned on disk (no longer referenced, never cleaned), and (b) a chapter with stale page paths is converted to a 0-page CBZ that renders empty yet counts as converted/downloaded. A failure path is reported as success in the download/offline core flow.
evidence: lines 85-95 `return@forEachIndexed` on missing/unreadable page; line 113-115 unconditional `filesToDelete.forEach { it.delete() }; log.i { "Created CBZ with $pageCounter pages..." }; cbzPath` — no check that pageCounter > 0 or equals imagePaths.size.
suggestedFix: After the zip loop, if `pageCounter == 0 && imagePaths.isNotEmpty()` delete the cbz and throw (caller's per-chapter runCatching already isolates the failure and keeps loose pages referenced). Consider also failing (or at least surfacing a count) when some pages were skipped, so the DB rewrite doesn't silently lose pages. Check the Android/iOS siblings for the same semantics and keep the 3-actual fan consistent.
verifierNote: Code behaves as described (DesktopCbzWriter.kt:85-95 skip, :113-115 unconditional success; caller rewrites localImagePaths on success at SettingsRepositoryImpl.kt:292-298). Downgraded: warn-and-skip is the deliberate fan/native posture (AndroidCbzWriter has identical skip semantics, documented 'partial archives tolerated by design'), and the degenerate 0-page case only converts an already-broken chapter (its loose paths were already missing) from one broken state to another while claiming success; genuinely new data loss requires a transient read failure (existing file orphaned). Real robustness gap (0-page guard worth adding fan-wide) but edge-case — minor.

title: createCbzWithSplitting silently ignores its maxMemoryBytes parameter
detail: The override accepts `maxMemoryBytes: Long` but archive() never receives it; the memory cap is the fixed 64 MiB MAX_BAND_BYTES inside SkiaWebpEncoder. A caller passing a lower budget (e.g. a low-RAM device-tier heuristic) gets no effect on Desktop, diverging from the interface's implied contract and from the Android actual. The class KDoc documents maxHeight handling but never mentions that maxMemoryBytes is ignored.

suggestedFix: Thread maxMemoryBytes into the band-height computation (min of caller budget and MAX_BAND_BYTES) in SkiaWebpEncoder, or document explicitly on the class KDoc that Desktop applies a fixed 64 MiB cap instead.
verifierNote: DesktopCbzWriter.kt:49-56 passes only maxHeight to archive(); maxMemoryBytes is unused. Interface (CbzWriter.kt:104-112) documents it as a memory hint and AndroidCbzWriter.kt:113 genuinely uses it (`byteSize > maxMemoryBytes`), so the Desktop divergence is real. title: AES master key (and store file) written with default permissions before chmod 600 is applied
detail: loadOrCreateKey writes the raw 32-byte AES key with `Files.write(keyFile, key.encoded)` and only afterwards calls applyRestrictivePermissions — under a typical 022 umask the key file is world-readable during that window. writeStore has the same shape: the tmp file is created with default perms, atomically moved (perms travel with it), and only then restricted (lines 95-99), re-opening the window on every mutation. Low practical impact on single-user machines, but the whole point of the 600 restriction is defeated by applying it after content lands.
evidence: lines 83-84: `Files.write(keyFile, key.encoded); applyRestrictivePermissions(keyFile)`; lines 96-99: tmp write -> ATOMIC_MOVE -> then applyRestrictivePermissions(storeFile).
suggestedFix: Create the files with restrictive permissions atomically: `Files.createFile(path, PosixFilePermissions.asFileAttribute(perms))` (falling back on non-POSIX stores) before writing bytes, or apply permissions to the tmp file before the move.
verifierNote: DesktopSecureStorage.kt:83-84 writes the raw AES key with default-umask perms then chmods; writeStore (95-99) creates the tmp with default perms, ATOMIC_MOVEs (perms travel), then restricts — the world-readable window reopens on every mutation. Create-with-restrictive-attrs fix is standard and behavior-preserving.

detail: The fallback chain (`user.home` -> `java.io.tmpdir` -> ".") only guards against null system properties. `FileSystem.SYSTEM.createDirectories(root)` in the property initializer still throws okio IOException when the resolved home exists but is unwritable (read-only home, disk full, sandboxed CI), which fails the Koin `single<AppFileSystem>` (PlatformModule.desktop.kt:113) and crashes Desktop startup — exactly the 'odd environments' the KDoc says are survived.

title: Per-page catch(Exception) swallows CancellationException and deletes pages that were never written to the CBZ
detail: Inside archive()'s page loop, the encode+writeEntry block is wrapped in `catch (e: Exception)` that logs and CONTINUES, and `filesToDelete += path` (line 105) runs unconditionally after it. Two consequences. (a) SkiaWebpEncoder.encodeToWebpPages deliberately rethrows CancellationException (SkiaWebpEncoder.kt:47), but CancellationException IS an Exception, so a user cancel arriving mid-encode is caught and swallowed here; if it happens on the LAST page, zip.finish() runs, the archive is sealed WITHOUT that page, all source pages (including the never-archived one) are deleted at line 114, and only then does withContext rethrow the cancellation — the page is permanently lost (sealed CBZ on disk is short one page, loose source deleted). This violates the project-wide 'CancellationException is always re-thrown' contract and the file's own #28 comment (lines 72-74: 'if the archive write fails partway (sink/zip error, OOM, cancellation), delete the partial/corrupt .cbz and rethrow — mirrors DesktopCbzWriter'). (b) Any real per-page store failure (okio IOException on a writeEntry flush, etc.) is also skipped-and-deleted: the page is missing from the finished archive yet its source file is still queued for deletion — silent data loss in the core download flow. DesktopCbzWriter deliberately has NO per-page catch for exactly this reason (DesktopCbzWriter.kt:70-76 explains a failed entry must fail the whole archive); the iOS KDoc claim 'Behaviour matches the Desktop actual for cross-platform parity' (line 32) is therefore also wrong. Additionally, a writeEntry that throws mid-header leaves StoreZipWriter.bytesWritten desynced from the sink, so continuing corrupts every subsequent central-directory offset.
evidence: Lines 93-105: `try { ... zip.writeEntry(...) } catch (e: Exception) { log.e(e) { "FAILED STORE: $path" } }\n filesToDelete += path` — vs DesktopCbzWriter which lets the same failure propagate to the outer catch (delete cbz + rethrow). IosCbzWriter is the LIVE iOS binding (shared/src/iosMain/.../di/PlatformModule.ios.kt:114 `single<CbzWriter> { IosCbzWriter(get()) }`) used by CoroutineDownloadRepositoryImpl.createCbzWithSplitting.
suggestedFix: Mirror DesktopCbzWriter: remove the inner try/catch so any encode/write failure (including CancellationException) propagates to the existing outer `catch (t: Throwable)` (partial .cbz deleted, loose pages kept, error rethrown). At minimum: `if (e is CancellationException) throw e` and only add `filesToDelete += path` after a successful write. Also fix the stale 'matches the Desktop actual' wording once aligned.
verifierNote: Defect confirmed and live (IosCbzWriter.kt:93-105 per-page catch(Exception) + unconditional filesToDelete; PlatformModule.ios.kt:114 binding; iOS download pipeline CoroutineDownloadRepositoryImpl.kt:318), but the headline CE-swallow scenario is practically unreachable: cancellation only fires at ensureActive()/yield() (lines 79-80, OUTSIDE the inner try) — SkiaWebpEncoder is non-suspend and returns null instead of throwing (its CE-rethrow at SkiaWebpEncoder.kt:47 is defensive dead code) and StoreZipWriter.writeEntry is non-suspend okio. The reachable harm is a transient mid-writeEntry IOException (okio emitCompleteSegments does real IO): page silently dropped, source still deleted after a clean finish, and a mid-entry throw desyncs bytesWritten corrupting later central-directory offsets. Rare but real data loss in the live iOS download flow — major stands; mirror-Desktop fix is safe.

title: Keychain facade is guaranteed to crash: `NSMutableDictionary as CFDictionaryRef` throws ClassCastException at runtime (verified by K/N repro)
detail: cfDictionaryOf() builds an NSMutableDictionary and returns `dict as CFDictionaryRef` (line 134). In Kotlin/Native an Obj-C object can NOT be cast to a CPointer-based CF type with `as` — toll-free bridging requires CFBridgingRetain/CFBridgingRelease. I reproduced the exact pattern (same dictionary construction, same casts, same Security calls) with the local kotlin-native 2.3.21 compiler on macOS: the compiler warns 'this cast can never succeed' on BOTH casts (line 134 and the `raw as? NSData` in get(), line 97), and at runtime step 1 fails with `ClassCastException: class kotlin.native.internal.NSDictionaryAsKMap cannot be cast to class kotlinx.cinterop.CPointer`. Since put(), get() and remove() all go through cfDictionaryOf()/baseQuery(), EVERY method of this class throws CCE on first call. Secondary issues (relevant once rewritten): the +1 retained CFTypeRef from SecItemCopyMatching is never CFRelease'd, and SecItemAdd/SecItemUpdate OSStatus failures other than errSecItemNotFound are silently ignored, so a failed write would look like success. Currently DORMANT: the class is live-bound (shared/src/iosMain/.../di/PlatformModule.ios.kt:121 `single<SecureStorage> { IosSecureStorage() }`) but SecureStorage has no iOS-side call sites today (only app/MainActivity.kt uses it, Android-only) — the first iOS consumer (e.g. porting MainActivity's session-timestamp persistence) crashes instantly. The KDoc claim that this 'matches the legacy :shared implementation exactly so existing Keychain entries remain accessible' is moot — no entries can ever have been written by this code path.
evidence: Repro (kotlin-native 2.3.21, macos_arm64, same Foundation/Security APIs): compiler emits `warning: this cast can never succeed` at both `dict as CFDictionaryRef` and `raw as? NSData`; runtime output: `step1 FAILED: ClassCastException: class kotlin.native.internal.NSDictionaryAsKMap cannot be cast to class kotlinx.cinterop.CPointer`.
suggestedFix: Rewrite the bridge the way multiplatform-settings' KeychainSettings does: wrap dictionary creation in `CFBridgingRetain(nsDict) as CFDictionaryRef` (CFTypeRef IS a CPointer, so that cast is legal), CFRelease the bridged dictionaries and the SecItemCopyMatching result when done, and convert the result with `CFBridgingRelease(raw) as? NSData`. Check OSStatus on add/update and at least log failures. Verify on an iOS simulator before relying on it (or replace the hand-rolled class with KeychainSettings from the already-bundled multiplatform-settings library).
verifierNote: IosSecureStorage.kt:134 `dict as CFDictionaryRef` casts an ObjC NSMutableDictionary to a CPointer typealias - illegal in K/N without CFBridgingRetain, so every method CCEs on first call; get()'s `raw as? NSData` (L97) is likewise always-null. Binding is live (shared/src/iosMain/.../di/PlatformModule.ios.kt:121) but the only SecureStorage call site is Android-only app/MainActivity.kt:131, so the crash is dormant until the first iOS consumer; major (not critical) for that reason. Suggested CFBridgingRetain/CFBridgingRelease rewrite matches the known-correct multiplatform-settings KeychainSettings pattern; risky stands (needs simulator verification).

title: CGBitmapContextCreate / CGColorSpaceCreateDeviceRGB results are never released — native CF leak per extract() call
detail: Both `CGColorSpaceCreateDeviceRGB()` (line 41) and `CGBitmapContextCreate(...)` (line 45) follow the CoreFoundation Create rule (+1 ownership). Kotlin/Native does not ARC-manage CF pointers, and the code never calls CGContextRelease/CGColorSpaceRelease (no such imports), so every extract() call leaks one CGContext and one CGColorSpace. Per-call magnitude is small (the 1x1 pixel buffer itself is the pinned Kotlin array), but it is unbounded across a session. Currently mitigated by dormancy: DominantColorExtractor is bound in all three PlatformModules but a repo-wide grep finds zero call sites (the audit postscript's 'cover-art-tint consumer resolves it via Koin' claim is stale).
evidence: extract() lines 41-59: `val colorSpace = CGColorSpaceCreateDeviceRGB() ?: return 0L ... val ctx = CGBitmapContextCreate(...) ?: return@usePinned` — no CGContextRelease/CGColorSpaceRelease/CFRelease anywhere in the file.
suggestedFix: Release both Create-rule objects, e.g. wrap the draw in try/finally: `try { CGContextDrawImage(ctx, ...) } finally { CGContextRelease(ctx) }` and `CGColorSpaceRelease(colorSpace)` after the pinned block (or use a single `finally` releasing both, null-safe).
verifierNote: IosDominantColorExtractor.kt:41/45 — CGColorSpaceCreateDeviceRGB and CGBitmapContextCreate follow the CF Create rule (+1); Kotlin/Native does not manage raw CF pointers and the file imports no CGContextRelease/CGColorSpaceRelease — one context + one colorspace leak per extract(). Dormancy verified: zero consumers of DominantColorExtractor outside platform/PlatformModule bindings.

title: No ZIP32 bounds guard: Int byte counter wraps past 2 GiB and entry count past 65535 silently corrupts the archive
detail: `bytesWritten` is an Int used for every local-header offset and the central-directory offset; an archive larger than 2 GiB wraps it negative and the central directory records garbage offsets — the writer keeps going and produces a corrupt-but-'successful' CBZ. Likewise `writeShortLe(entries.size)` truncates above 65535 entries. Neither limit is checked. A single chapter exceeding 2 GiB is unlikely but not impossible (long webtoon chapters with verbatim-fallback pages); failing loudly is strictly better than sealing a corrupt archive that DefaultCbzReader will misread later.
evidence: Line 39 `private var bytesWritten: Int = 0`; line 112-115 write entries.size and centralDirOffset without any range check.
suggestedFix: Track bytesWritten as Long and `check(bytesWritten <= 0xFFFF_FFFFL && offset >= 0)` (practically: fail if > Int.MAX_VALUE) in writeEntry/finish, and `check(entries.size <= 0xFFFF)` in finish(), so an oversized chapter fails the archive (caller already falls back to loose pages) instead of producing silent corruption.
verifierNote: StoreZipWriter.kt:39 — `bytesWritten: Int` feeds every localHeaderOffset and the central-dir offset (lines 54, 82, 102, 115); >2 GiB wraps negative and the writer keeps going, sealing a corrupt-but-successful archive. entries.size written via writeShortLe (112-113) with no 65535 check. Loud check() failure propagates to IosCbzWriter's catch (line 109) which deletes the cbz and rethrows — clean fallback.

title: Each observe() collector runs its own 5s HEAD-probe loop; HttpClient never closed; catch(Throwable) swallows CancellationException
detail: observe() returns a cold callbackFlow, so every concurrent collector spawns an independent polling loop hitting google.com/generate_204 every 5 seconds — N collectors = N network probes (and N wakeups) for the same global state; there is no shareIn/replay. The Darwin HttpClient created per instance (line 39) has no close() path (acknowledged only in the audit postscript). runProbe()'s `catch (_: Throwable)` (line 61) also catches CancellationException when the collector is cancelled mid-request, mapping it to a spurious Status.Unavailable; cancellation still lands at the next delay() so this self-corrects, but it briefly mislabels a cancel as 'offline' and contradicts the repo's CancellationException convention.
evidence: Lines 47-56 (cold callbackFlow + launch per collection), 39-45 (per-instance HttpClient, no close), 58-63 (`catch (_: Throwable) { Status.Unavailable }`).
suggestedFix: Share one upstream loop (`.shareIn(scope, SharingStarted.WhileSubscribed(...), replay = 1)` on a class-owned scope) or document single-collector usage; rethrow CancellationException in runProbe; optionally expose close() for the client.

title: percentEncode leaves '&', '#', '+' unencoded, so shared text containing them corrupts/truncates the mailto body; pre-iOS17 it encodes nothing at all
detail: percentEncode() round-trips the text through `NSURL.URLWithString("https://x/?q=$this")`. NSURL only percent-encodes characters that are INVALID in a query, so query-legal delimiters survive raw: a '#' in the shared text terminates the mailto URL (fragment), '&' splits the body into bogus extra parameters (everything after it is dropped by Mail), and '+' may render as a space. Shared text for a manga app routinely contains URLs with '&' query params and titles with '&'/'#'. Worse, NSURL(string:) only auto-encodes invalid characters on iOS 17+ (RFC 3986 lenient parsing for apps linked against iOS 17); on iOS 16 and earlier URLWithString returns nil for text containing spaces/newlines, percentEncode falls back to the RAW string (`?: this`), and openUrl then fails to parse the mailto URL and silently returns — share does nothing with no user feedback. The mailto degradation itself is documented (TODO Phase 14), but the broken encoding within it is not.
evidence: Line 47-48: `NSURL.URLWithString("https://x/?q=$this")?.absoluteString?.substringAfter("?q=") ?: this` — '&', '#', '+' are valid query characters and pass through unencoded into `mailto:?body=...` (line 44).
suggestedFix: Replace the NSURL trick with a real RFC 3986 component encoder: `NSString.create(string = this).stringByAddingPercentEncodingWithAllowedCharacters(NSCharacterSet.alphanumericCharacterSet)` (or a small manual encoder keeping only unreserved chars), applied to both body and subject.
verifierNote: IosIntentLauncher.kt:47-48 — the NSURL round-trip only encodes query-invalid characters, so '&' (splits mailto params), '#' (URLWithString keeps it as a fragment delimiter; substringAfter("?q=") carries it raw into the mailto body where it truncates) and '+' pass through; pre-iOS-17 strict parsing returns nil for space/newline text, falling back to the raw string (`?: this`) and openUrl's nil-parse silent return. All verified against the code.

title: UIKit main-thread requirement unenforced (siblings hop dispatchers, iOS doesn't) and deprecated keyWindow can be nil — share silently no-ops
detail: shareBitmapBytes presents a UIActivityViewController and saveBitmapBytesToGallery calls UIImageWriteToSavedPhotosAlbum; both are main-thread-only UIKit APIs, but the suspend functions run on the caller's dispatcher with no MainRun/dispatch_async hop and the class KDoc never states the requirement (only the audit postscript does). Today's sole caller (ChapterImagesReworkScreenRoute.kt:156, rememberCoroutineScope = Main) is safe by accident, but Android and Desktop siblings wrap in Dispatchers.IO, so a common-code caller written against those semantics (launching from a background dispatcher) would crash or misbehave only on iOS. Additionally `UIApplication.sharedApplication.keyWindow` (line 55) is deprecated since iOS 13 and returns nil in scene-based setups with no key window, in which case `rootVC?.present...` silently does nothing — the user taps Share and nothing happens, no feedback, no log (the catch only sees thrown exceptions).
evidence: Lines 48-60: no withContext(Main)/dispatch_to_main; `val rootVC = UIApplication.sharedApplication.keyWindow?.rootViewController; rootVC?.presentViewController(...)` — nil window short-circuits silently.
suggestedFix: Hop to the main dispatcher inside both methods (e.g. `withContext(Dispatchers.Main)`), resolve the presenter via `connectedScenes` key window with keyWindow fallback, and log a warning when no root VC is found so the silent no-op is at least diagnosable.
verifierNote: IosScreenshotProvider.kt:48-60 — no main-thread hop for UIActivityViewController/UIImageWriteToSavedPhotosAlbum (Desktop/Android siblings wrap in Dispatchers.IO, so a background-dispatcher common caller misbehaves only on iOS); keyWindow (line 55) is deprecated and nil-prone in scene-based apps, with `rootVC?.present...` silently no-oping. Current caller is Main-scope by accident (ChapterImagesReworkScreenRoute rememberCoroutineScope).

title: Sums NSFileSize of directory entries too — Android sibling counts only files; KDoc parity claim is inaccurate
detail: The enumerator loop accumulates the NSFileSize attribute of EVERY visited path, including subdirectories (a directory's NSFileSize is its metadata/entry size, typically 64-160 bytes). AndroidFileSizeFormatter explicitly excludes directories from the sum (`if (file.isDirectory) stack.add(file) else yield(file)`), so iOS over-reports folder sizes by a small amount whenever subdirectories exist. The KDoc (lines 19-22) claims the behaviour 'matches the Android implementation's behaviour (File.listFiles() returns everything)' — Android lists everything but sums only files, so the claim is wrong as stated. Impact is cosmetic (size labels), and chapter folders are usually flat.
evidence: Lines 33-39 accumulate attrs[NSFileSize] for every nextObject() with no NSFileType check; AndroidFileSizeFormatter.kt:31-33 yields only non-directories.
suggestedFix: Skip directory entries: read `attrs[NSFileType]` and `continue` when it equals NSFileTypeDirectory (and fix the KDoc parity sentence).
verifierNote: IosFileSizeFormatter.kt:33-39 accumulates NSFileSize for every enumerated path with no NSFileType check (directories included); AndroidFileSizeFormatter's safeWalkFiles yields only non-directories (`if (file.isDirectory) stack.add(file) else yield(file)`). KDoc line 19-20 parity claim is wrong as stated — Android lists everything but sums files only.

title: Band height is capped only by memory, not by WebP's 16383px dimension limit — tall pages on the createCbz path silently lose WebP transcoding
detail: effectiveBandHeight() returns min(maxHeight, 64MiB-derived height). WebP has a hard 16383x16383 dimension limit; for narrow pages the memory cap alone allows taller bands (e.g. width 800 -> byMemory ~20971). On the createCbz(...) path (maxHeight = Int.MAX_VALUE in both IosCbzWriter and DesktopCbzWriter) a page taller than 16383px therefore reaches encodeToData(WEBP) which returns null, encodeWebp throws, the runCatching converts the WHOLE page to null, and the caller stores it verbatim — compression silently lost (and the page is decoded again later at read time). The live download pipeline is unaffected (createCbzWithSplitting's DEFAULT_MAX_HEIGHT = 10_000 < 16383), so this only bites future/whole-page callers, but the encoder is the right place for the guard.
evidence: Lines 113-116: `minOf(maxHeight, byMemory)` with no 16383 clamp; encodeWebp errors when Skia returns no data (line 80).
suggestedFix: Clamp: `return minOf(maxHeight, byMemory, WEBP_MAX_DIMENSION).coerceAtLeast(1)` with `private const val WEBP_MAX_DIMENSION = 16383` (also guards width > 16383 is undecodable-by-WebP anyway and will fall back as today).
verifierNote: SkiaWebpEncoder.kt:113-116 — effectiveBandHeight = min(maxHeight, byMemory) with no 16383 WebP-dimension clamp; on the createCbz path (maxHeight=Int.MAX_VALUE in both non-Android writers) a narrow page taller than 16383 reaches encodeToData(WEBP) → null → error → runCatching → verbatim fallback, silently losing transcoding. Live path unaffected (CbzWriter.kt:120 DEFAULT_MAX_HEIGHT=10_000 < 16383); createCbz currently has no production caller, as the finding concedes.

title: allocN32Pixels result unchecked and dst Bitmap not closed on the exception path
detail: decodeEncodedImageWithSkia allocates the destination with `bitmap.allocN32Pixels(outWidth, outHeight)` without checking the Boolean result (sibling SkiaWebpEncoder.encodeBand wraps the same call in `check(...)`); on allocation failure (huge page, native OOM) drawing proceeds against a zero-size bitmap and the decoder returns a blank image instead of failing into Coil's error path (wrong-but-plausible output, which the app's risk profile flags as worse than failure). Separately, if drawImageRect/setImmutable/asImage throws, the freshly allocated Bitmap's native memory is never released — only `image` is closed in the finally; the bitmap leaks (on success, ownership correctly transfers to the returned Coil image, so only the exception path leaks).
evidence: Lines 124-140: `val bitmap = Bitmap(); bitmap.allocN32Pixels(outWidth, outHeight); Canvas(bitmap).skiaUse { ... }; ... return DecodeResult(image = bitmap.asImage(), ...)` inside a try whose finally closes only `image`.
suggestedFix: `check(bitmap.allocN32Pixels(outWidth, outHeight)) { "allocN32Pixels failed for ${outWidth}x$outHeight" }` and wrap the draw/return in try/catch that calls `bitmap.close()` before rethrowing (success path must NOT close).
verifierNote: HighQualitySkiaImageDecoder.kt:124-125 — allocN32Pixels result unchecked (sibling SkiaWebpEncoder.kt:88 wraps the same call in check()); on alloc failure the draw proceeds on a zero-size bitmap producing blank output instead of an error (against the app's wrong-output-worse-than-failure posture). The try's finally (141-143) closes only the source `image`; the dst bitmap is not closed on an exception path, violating the explicit-close discipline the codebase itself documents.

title: AVIF sniff matches only the ftyp MAJOR brand 'avif'/'avis' — AVIF files with e.g. 'mif1' major brand fall through to Skia and fail
detail: isAvif() inspects bytes 8-11, i.e. only the ISO-BMFF major_brand. Valid AVIF files may carry a different major brand (commonly 'mif1') with 'avif' listed in compatible_brands; such files are declined by this Factory, fall through to HighQualitySkiaImageDecoder, and fail to decode there (skiko ships no libavif) — the exact broken-page symptom this decoder (#3-REAL) was added to fix, for a subset of encoders. libavif's default output uses major brand 'avif' so most sources work, but scraped sources are heterogeneous by nature.
evidence: Lines 99-103 check `h[8..10]=='avi'` and `h[11] in {'f','s'}` at the major-brand offset only; no compatible_brands scan.
suggestedFix: Extend the peek to the full ftyp box (read box size from bytes 0-3, bounded e.g. to 64 bytes) and accept when any 4-byte brand in the box equals 'avif'/'avis' (major or compatible). Keep declining on any read error. Needs the same device-smoke the file's NOTE already prescribes.
verifierNote: IosAvifDecoder.kt:99-103 matches only bytes 8-11 (ftyp major_brand) against 'avif'/'avis'; an AVIF with major brand 'mif1' + 'avif' in compatible_brands is declined, falls to HighQualitySkiaImageDecoder, and fails (skiko has no libavif). Android's AvifDecoderCoil additionally claims via Content-Type image/avif, so iOS is strictly narrower. Real but encoder-dependent edge; risky fix needs device smoke per the file's own NOTE.

title: Details 'delete downloaded' actions never delete on-disk files or clear isDownloaded (row-only deleteDownload); per-row delete-chapter permanently orphans files
detail: onDeleteSelectedDownloads (L908), onDeleteAllDownloads (L968) and step 1 of onDeleteChapter (L929) call DeleteDownloadUseCase, whose impl (DownloadsActionRepositoryImpl.deleteDownload, '#10 native-wins') is documented and implemented as a ROW-ONLY delete of the chapter_downloads queue row — on-disk files and saved_chapters.isDownloaded are intentionally left intact (that scope is correct for the Downloads-screen row delete). But these three Details-screen actions are the KMP port of native's deleteAllChapters -> LibraryRepository.deleteDownloadedChapters, which marks chapters NOT downloaded AND deletes the chapter files (native LibraryRepository.kt:139-150). No rework code path calls the full-cleanup deleteDownloadedChapters (grep: only :shared and a comment in :data reference it). Consequences: (a) 'delete downloaded' / multi-select delete frees zero disk space and rows still show the Downloaded badge (Chapter.isDownloaded stays true) — only the size header (derived from chapterDownloads SUCCESS rows) drops, so the UI contradicts itself; (b) onDeleteChapter then deletes the saved_chapters row, leaving the chapter directory on disk with NO referencing row — a permanent storage leak that nothing can clean up. The VM's own comments ('deletes the on-disk download', 'Clean the download (files + chapter_downloads row)', 'deleteDownload reads the chapter row's mangaId to locate the on-disk files', 'so nothing is orphaned') describe a file-deleting impl that does not exist — they were written against a pre-#10 understanding.

The on-disk files and the saved_chapters isDownloaded flag are intentionally LEFT intact'. Native parity target (LibraryRepository.deleteDownloadedChapters) clears the flag and deletes files; no rework caller exists.

verifierNote: Traced end-to-end: DetailsViewModel onDeleteSelectedDownloads/onDeleteChapter/onDeleteAllDownloads -> DeleteDownloadUseCase -> DownloadsActionRepositoryImpl.kt:169-177 (documented '#10 ROW-ONLY delete') -> legacy dao.deleteByChapterId only (DownloadRepositoryImpl.kt:85-87, CoroutineDownloadRepositoryImpl.kt:163-165).
