title: Bare viewModelScope.launch around throwing use cases — an unexpected throw crashes the process (launchSafely exists for exactly this and is used by History/Updates)
detail: DetailsViewModel launches fire-and-forget work with bare viewModelScope.launch in ~14 places. Several of the invoked use cases return plain Unit/Boolean/Long? with NO Result/AppResult wrapping and NO try/runCatching at the repo impl: ToggleChapterReadUseCase (L775), ToggleChapterBookmarkUseCase (L785, L897-898), MarkChaptersReadUseCase (L868, L959), ClearChapterNewUseCase (L646), DeleteChapterUseCase (L937), ResolveChapterIdUseCase (L913, L932, L974). A Room/SQLite throw (disk full, corruption, constraint) from any of these escapes viewModelScope and crashes the app — MviViewModel's own KDoc (L151-157) warns that a bare launch inside a handler bypasses the submit() safety net, and provides launchSafely, which HistoryViewModel (#29) and UpdatesViewModel already adopted. Separately, the silently-discarded returns mean these per-chapter actions give the user no failure feedback even on a clean Result path (inconsistent with the sibling handlers that emit ShowError).
evidence: DetailsViewModel L775: 'viewModelScope.launch { toggleChapterRead(chapter.url) }'. MarkChapterReadRepositoryImpl has no runCatching/try (verified); ChapterDeletionRepositoryImpl.deleteChapter is a bare DAO call. HistoryViewModel L128-133 shows the established fix: '#29: route fire-and-forget deletes through launchSafely so a throw routes to onUnhandledError instead of escaping viewModelScope and crashing the process.'
suggestedFix: Replace every bare viewModelScope.launch in DetailsViewModel with launchSafely (the base-class helper preserves the Job return for cancel-before-relaunch). Same (lower-priority) pattern applies to AboutViewModel.init, ComplaintViewModel and AdminComplaintViewModel (their use cases are Result-wrapped so the residual risk is smaller).
verifierNote: Verified bare viewModelScope.launch at DetailsViewModel L646/775/785/868/897/913/932/937/959/974 around unwrapped use cases: MarkChapterReadRepositoryImpl.kt:38-44 and ChapterDeletionRepositoryImpl.kt:14 are raw DAO calls with no catch, so a SQLite throw escapes the scope (MviViewModel.kt launchSafely KDoc confirms submit()'s net does not cover sibling coroutines). Precedent verified: HistoryViewModel.kt:128-133 and UpdatesViewModel.kt:189-199 already use launchSafely (#29). Major not critical: crash requires an abnormal DB failure, not a normal user path. Mechanical launchSafely swap preserves Job-returning call sites - safe.

title: onSaveToggle has no re-entry guard — a double-tap runs two concurrent toggleInLibrary calls and can silently undo the user's action
detail: onSaveToggle tracks savingKeys for the inline spinner but never checks it: 'if (key in state.value.savingKeys) return' is missing. submit() launches a fresh coroutine per intent, and onSaveToggle suspends (fetchDetails is a network round-trip on ADD; toggleInLibrary is a DB round-trip on REMOVE), so a double-tap delivered before recomposition swaps the button (ADD) — or any time during the REMOVE round-trip (the remove path never shows a spinner, L305-309) — passes the isAdd check twice (savedKeys only flips after the membership flow re-emits) and invokes ToggleInLibraryUseCase twice. Toggle semantics (read-then-write, non-atomic) mean the second call observes the first call's result and toggles BACK: the manga ends up not-saved after the user tapped Save, or re-saved after Remove. DetailsViewModel guards this exact race with isTogglingBookmark + finally (DetailsState KDoc L112-122 documents the failure mode); Home omitted the guard.
evidence: L302-303: 'val key = item.key(); val isAdd = key !in state.value.savedKeys' — no savingKeys check. HomeFeedRow.kt only swaps the button for a spinner via isSaving (recomposition-delayed) and only for ADD.
suggestedFix: Early-return in onSaveToggle when key is already in state.value.savingKeys, and add the key to savingKeys for the REMOVE path too (or at least guard both branches), clearing it in a finally.
verifierNote: HomeViewModel onSaveToggle (L297-323) never checks savingKeys; ToggleInLibraryUseCase.kt:65-72 is read-then-write (get -> add when null / remove when present), so two concurrent invocations undo each other. Worse than described: a double-tap on REMOVE makes the second call's get() return null after the first remove commits, RE-ADDING the manga with an empty chapter list. DetailsViewModel.kt:721-722 guards the identical race with isTogglingBookmark. Early-return + savingKeys on both branches is behavior-preserving - safe.

title: observeMembership creates one Room EXISTS flow per visible feed item (N+1), torn down and rebuilt wholesale on every feed change
detail: observeMembership maps every visible HomeFeedItem to its own observeInLibrary(api, language, title) Room flow and combines them (L285-293). With infinite scroll the visible set grows to 100+ items: that is 100+ concurrently-live Room invalidation observers; every saved_manga write re-runs ALL of the EXISTS queries and re-evaluates the combine; and every pagination append / refresh cancels and recreates the entire set (membershipJob?.cancel() then N fresh subscriptions, each re-querying). Native solved heart-sync with a single observed library list (savedManga) and a contains check. This is the canonical N+1-queries pattern on the app's hottest screen.
evidence: L285-288: 'val flows = items.map { observeInLibrary(api = it.api, ...) }; membershipJob = combine(flows) { ... }' — restarted from fetchHome.onSuccess (L241) and onEndReached.onSuccess (L178) on every page.
suggestedFix: Observe the full library key set once (a single Flow<Set<MangaKey>> use case over the saved_manga table, started in onEnter for the VM lifetime) and intersect it with the visible feed keys in the reducer; drop the per-item flows and the restart-on-append logic.
verifierNote: N-flows claim verified (HomeViewModel.kt:285-293, restarted at fetchHome.onSuccess and onEndReached.onSuccess) but the mechanism is misdescribed: observeIsInLibrary (LibraryRepositoryImpl.kt:109-117) is not a per-item EXISTS query - each of the N flows collects mangaDao.getAllSavedMangaFlow() (the FULL saved_manga table) and scans with .any{}, i.e. N full-table queries + N list scans per library write or pagination append - resource-wise worse than claimed. However all work runs on dispatchers.io, queries are cheap, and there is no incorrectness, so per calibration this is a performance smell, not user-visible incorrectness: minor.

title: In-flight runFetch is never cancelled on identity change and its onSuccess does not validate identity — a stale fetch can land over a newer manga's state
detail: Unlike libraryMembershipJob/savedDetailsJob (explicitly cancelled and restarted 'on every identity change'), the network fetch started by onEnter/onEnterByUrl is an untracked suspend call inside the per-intent coroutine. If OnEnter/OnEnterByUrl for a DIFFERENT manga arrives while a fetch is in flight, the old fetch keeps running and its onSuccess (L536-573) unconditionally writes details and enriches current.manga (language/title/coverUrl/genres) from the OLD manga's payload — corrupting the new identity and showing the wrong manga's chapters (the domain risk profile calls wrong-but-plausible data worse than failure). Today the VM is per-backstack-entry so a same-VM identity change is not reachable through normal navigation, which is why this is minor — but the VM's own job-restart machinery shows same-VM identity changes are an intended supported path, and OnRetry's isLoading guard does not cover this case (the identity check passes for a different manga).
evidence: L168/L176: jobs restarted per identity; runFetch has no Job field; onSuccess L546-551 'current.manga?.copy(language = details.language, title = details.title, ...)' with no check that details corresponds to current.manga.
suggestedFix: Track the fetch in a fetchJob with cancel-before-relaunch (same posture as ReaderViewModel), or capture the target identity at fetch start and no-op the onSuccess/onFailure lambdas when state.value.manga no longer matches it.
verifierNote: Verified: libraryMembershipJob/savedDetailsJob are cancel-before-relaunch per identity (168/176, 454-457, 488-489) but runFetch is an untracked suspend in the per-intent coroutine (submit launches fresh coroutines), and onSuccess (536-573) unconditionally enriches current.manga with the fetched details' language/title/coverUrl/genres with no identity check — a stale fetch corrupts a newer identity. Reachable only via same-VM identity change (the VM's own job machinery treats that as supported), so minor is right.

title: Flow.catch on the four collectors terminates the flow but KDoc claims the collector 'survives transient exceptions'
detail: startObservingLibraryMembership's KDoc (L484-486) says 'The catch swallows so the collector survives transient exceptions; the next emission flips the flag correctly.' That misstates Flow.catch semantics: an upstream exception completes the flow — catch only replaces the crash, there is no retry/resubscribe, so 'the next emission' never arrives. The same one-throw-kills-the-stream posture applies to the downloads collector (L219), connectivity collector (L227) and savedDetails collector (L409): a single transient Room/driver error permanently freezes the download progress map / online flag / saved overlay for the rest of the screen's life, silently. Low likelihood (Room flows rarely throw), but the doc is wrong and the degradation is invisible.
evidence: L497 '.catch { /* See KDoc — secondary affordance... */ }' — no .retry/resubscription; kotlinx.coroutines Flow.catch completes the stream after handling.
suggestedFix: Either correct the KDoc to 'on failure the collector stops; the flag stays at its last value', or add a bounded retry (e.g. .retryWhen with delay) if survive-transient is actually desired.
verifierNote: KDoc at DetailsViewModel.kt:484-485 ('the collector survives transient exceptions; the next emission flips the flag') misstates Flow.catch: an upstream throw completes the flow after catch handles it, no resubscribe. Same one-throw-freezes posture at :219 (downloads), :227 (connectivity), :409 (savedDetails).

title: displayChapters/firstUnreadChapter/isSelectionAllDownloaded are uncached get() properties that re-run full dedup+filter+sort on every access
detail: displayChapters (L285-308) runs distinctBy + filter + sortedBy(+reversed) over the whole chapter list (often hundreds of chapters) on EVERY property read; firstUnreadChapter (L322-324) calls displayChapters again (second full recompute); isSelectionAllDownloaded (L255-264) rebuilds a downloaded-URL set per read; downloadingChapterUrls (L231-232) filters the map per read. The :ui layer reads several of these per recomposition, and the downloads collector ticks state many times per second during an active download (progress updates), so each tick can trigger multiple O(n log n) passes plus allocations on the main thread. Since DetailsState is immutable, the values are constant per instance and trivially cacheable.

title: onNextChapter/onPrevChapter mark the ANCHOR chapter read, not the ACTIVE (viewed) chapter, in a continuous feed
detail: In the #5 continuous reader, after the user scrolls across an appended boundary the chapter on screen (activeChapterUrl) differs from the anchor (state.chapter, set by the last OnEnter). onNextChapter/onPrevChapter compute the navigation target from the ACTIVE chapter (`current.currentChapterIndex` is derived from activeChapterUrl in ReaderState), but mark-read uses `current.chapter?.url` — the anchor. So: read chapter A, scroll into appended chapter B, tap top-bar Next -> navigates to C (correct, active-based) but marks A read again (already read) and never marks B, the chapter actually being left. The VM is deliberately active-chapter-aware everywhere else on this surface (onToggleBookmark line 361 uses activeChapterUrl 'bookmark the chapter the user is CURRENTLY VIEWING'; onPageChanged resume-save line 600 uses the active chapter), so the anchor here is an oversight, and it diverges from native, which marks the chapter being advanced away from.
evidence: ReaderViewModel.kt:469 `val nextIdx = current.currentChapterIndex + 1` (active-based) vs :476 `val leavingUrl = current.chapter?.url` (anchor-based) in the same function; ReaderState.kt:275-276 currentChapterIndex derives from activeChapterUrl.
suggestedFix: In onNextChapter and onPrevChapter use `val leavingUrl = current.activeChapterUrl ?: current.chapter?.url` so the chapter actually on screen is the one marked read.
verifierNote: Verified mismatch inside one function: ReaderViewModel.kt:469 nextIdx derives from currentChapterIndex (active-chapter-based per ReaderState.kt:275-276) while :476/:491 leavingUrl uses the anchor current.chapter?.url. After scrolling into an appended chapter B, Next marks A (already marked at append time, :528) and never marks B. Surrounding code (onToggleBookmark :361, onPageChanged :600) is deliberately active-aware, so the anchor here is an oversight.

title: Extracted-CBZ temp-dir cleanup misses appended chapters in the continuous feed
detail: onEnter clears only the previous ANCHOR chapter's extract dir (`current.chapter?.takeIf { it.url != chapter.url }?.let { clearExtractedPages(it) }`) and onCleared (line 816) clears only `state.value.chapter`. Chapters appended via onAppendNextChapter/appendChapterPages are recorded in state.loadedChapterUrls but never passed to clearExtractedPages, so for downloaded chapters read in continuous mode each appended chapter leaves its full extracted page set in cacheDir/cbz_extract/<mangaId>/<chapterId> (DefaultCbzReader.kt:148-156). A long webtoon session over downloaded chapters accumulates one extracted dir per appended chapter; they are only reclaimed by OS cache pressure, defeating the 'don't accumulate' intent stated in the onEnter comment (lines 384-386).
evidence: ReaderViewModel.kt:387 clears one chapter; appendChapterPages (538-577) adds chapters to loadedChapterUrls but no cleanup path ever iterates that list; onCleared:816 `state.value.chapter?.let { clearExtractedPages(it) }`.
suggestedFix: In onEnter and onCleared, resolve every URL in state.value.loadedChapterUrls against state.value.chapters and call clearExtractedPages for each loaded chapter (excluding, in onEnter, the chapter being entered), falling back to the anchor when the list is empty.
verifierNote: Verified: onEnter (:387) clears only the previous anchor, onCleared (:816) only state.chapter; appendChapterPages (:549-560) grows loadedChapterUrls but no path ever iterates it for cleanup. DefaultCbzReader.cleanupExtractedCache deletes per-(mangaId,chapterId) dir, so each appended downloaded chapter leaks its extracted page set under cacheDir/cbz_extract until OS cache pressure.

title: downloadStatusFor does a linear scan of the downloads list for every visible row on every recomposition
detail: UpdatesScreen.kt:418 calls state.downloadStatusFor(entry.chapterId, ...) inside the LazyColumn items block, and the implementation is downloads.firstOrNull { it.chapterId == chapterId } — an O(downloads) scan per row, i.e. O(rows × downloads) per recomposition pass. The downloads list is the full queue+history projection from Room, which grows with every download the user ever made; on a long updates feed with a large downloads table this is measurable wasted main-thread work during scroll. visibleItems is similarly recomputed (a filterNot pass) at each of its several access sites (UpdatesScreen.kt:309, 321, 388 plus isEmpty/hasUnreadItems), though it early-outs when no delete is pending.
evidence: UpdatesState.kt:134 'val download = downloads.firstOrNull { it.chapterId == chapterId }' invoked per item from UpdatesScreen.kt:418.
suggestedFix: Add a lazily-computed index to UpdatesState (e.g. 'private val downloadsByChapterId by lazy { downloads.associateBy { it.chapterId } }') and look up via the map in downloadStatusFor; data class copy() creates a new instance so the lazy re-computes only when state changes.
verifierNote: UpdatesState.kt:134 downloads.firstOrNull per call, invoked per visible row from UpdatesScreen.kt:418 inside the items{} block → O(rows × downloads) per composition pass over the ever-growing queue+history projection. Real but unmeasured main-thread waste; minor/perf with the lazy associateBy fix is correctly calibrated.

title: handle() wraps use-case calls in bare nested viewModelScope.launch, escaping the MVI crash safety net
detail: Both intent branches do 'viewModelScope.launch { setAppTheme(...) }' / 'viewModelScope.launch { setPureBlack(...) }'. MviViewModel's own launchSafely KDoc warns: 'A bare viewModelScope.launch { … } started inside a handler is a sibling coroutine whose uncaught throw escapes to the scope and crashes the process.' The #29 crash-safety remediation converted UpdatesViewModel/HistoryViewModel mutations to launchSafely but ThemeViewModel was left on bare launch. The write path (legacy sync SharedPreferences-style writes via ThemeRepositoryImpl) is near-infallible so practical risk is low, but the nested launch is also unnecessary: handle() already runs in its own per-intent coroutine under submit()'s try/catch, so calling the suspend use case directly would be both simpler and covered by the safety net.

suggestedFix: Replace the nested 'viewModelScope.launch { ... }' with a direct suspend call (covered by submit's safety net) or with 'launchSafely { ... }' to match the #29 pattern used in Updates/History.

Practical risk low (prefs write), correctly minor.

title: loadFeatures uses a bare viewModelScope.launch with no failure handling — a throw bypasses the safety net and strands isLoading=true forever
detail: loadFeatures() runs 'viewModelScope.launch { updateState(isLoading=true); getWhatsNewFeatures(); updateState(isLoading=false) }'. It is invoked from init{} AND from the OnRetry handler; in the handler case the nested launch escapes submit()'s try/catch (per MviViewModel's launchSafely KDoc), so any throw crashes the process instead of routing to onUnhandledError. Additionally, if the suspend call throws, the second updateState never runs, leaving the screen on an infinite spinner with no recovery affordance (errorMessage is never written anywhere in this VM, so the Retry placeholder can't appear). The repository (WhatsNewRepositoryImpl.getFeatures) is designed to swallow remote failures (Result.fold + runCatchingCancellable + fallbackToDefaults), but fallbackToDefaults' toRework() mapping (MediaType.valueOf) and any future repo change are unguarded — the VM is one :data regression away from a crash + stuck spinner.
evidence: WhatsNewViewModel.kt:160-171; contrast with MviViewModel.kt:151-156 ('Prefer this helper for any such fire-and-forget work').
suggestedFix: Use launchSafely for loadFeatures, and clear isLoading (e.g. in a finally or via an overridden onUnhandledError) so a failed load degrades to the empty/error placeholder instead of an infinite spinner.
verifierNote: WhatsNewViewModel.kt:161 uses bare viewModelScope.launch from init AND the OnRetry handler; MviViewModel.kt:151-156 explicitly documents that such a sibling coroutine escapes submit()'s safety net and says to prefer launchSafely. A throw strands isLoading=true (no finally / no errorMessage write path). Repo today swallows remote failures (WhatsNewRepositoryImpl Result.fold + fallbackToDefaults), so this is defensive hardening, as the finding itself states.

title: OOM fallback is unreachable: `e is OutOfMemoryError` inside `catch (e: Exception)` is always false
detail: Both compression-failure handlers (streaming line 210, batch line 334) test `e is OutOfMemoryError` inside a `catch (e: Exception)` block. OutOfMemoryError extends java.lang.Error, not Exception, so the catch never receives it and the type test is statically always-false. The documented graceful degradation (keep loose page files, mark chapter downloaded) therefore only triggers for exceptions whose message happens to contain "memory". A real OutOfMemoryError thrown by Bitmap work in OptimizedCbzManager.createCbzParallel bypasses both `catch (e: CancellationException)` and `catch (e: Exception)`, skips the `paths.forEach { delete() }` cleanup, and is swallowed by the outer flow `.catch`, which marks the chapter failed and leaves the downloaded loose pages orphaned on disk. Native app has the identical dead test (native ChapterDownloadService.kt:230, :377), so this is a ported parity bug — but it is harmful: low-RAM devices lose the intended fallback for large chapters.
evidence: `} catch (e: Exception) { if (e is OutOfMemoryError || e.message?.contains("memory", ignoreCase = true) == true) { ... fallback ... } else { paths.forEach { File(it).delete() } ... } }` — OutOfMemoryError can never reach a catch typed Exception.
suggestedFix: Catch `Throwable` (rethrowing CancellationException first) around the createCbzParallel call, or add an explicit `catch (e: OutOfMemoryError)` branch that performs the loose-files fallback, in both downloadChapterStreaming and downloadChapterBatch.
verifierNote: Core claim confirmed: ChapterDownloadService.kt:207/210 and :333/334 test `e is OutOfMemoryError` inside `catch (e: Exception)` — statically always false (OOM extends Error), so the documented loose-files fallback only fires on exceptions with 'memory' in the message; a real OOM bypasses both catches and lands in the flow `.catch` → chapter FAILED. Native has the identical dead test (verified in native-app ChapterDownloadService.kt), harmful so it stands. Adjustment: the 'loose pages orphaned on disk' consequence is wrong — DownloadWorkerV2.handleErrorSafely (DownloadWorkerV2.kt:301-309) calls deleteChapterFiles on every DownloadState.Error, so the live worker path cleans them up; impact is lost fallback (failed download on low-RAM devices), not orphaned files.

title: Streaming download marks chapter Complete with silently missing pages
detail: downloadChapterStreaming wraps each image in `try { ... } catch (e: Exception) { log; rethrow only CE }` (lines 160-170) and only fails the chapter when ALL images fail (line 173). If e.g. 5 of 40 pages fail (server hiccup, Cloudflare interstitial served as image, 404), the chapter is compressed and emitted as DownloadState.Complete with those pages permanently absent — no error state, no user feedback, and the chapter is marked downloaded. Per the domain risk profile, wrong-but-plausible results are worse than failures: the user discovers the loss only while reading offline. This matches the native port baseline, so it needs an owner decision (e.g. fail or surface a partial-success warning when paths.size < imageUrls.size).
evidence: `catch (e: Exception) { Log.e(...); if (e is CancellationException) throw e }` per image, then `if (paths.isEmpty()) throw IllegalStateException(...)` — any non-empty subset proceeds to Complete.
suggestedFix: Treat `paths.size < imageUrls.size` as a failure (or emit a distinct partial-success state that the worker maps to FAILED/with-warning) instead of unconditional Complete.
verifierNote: Confirmed at ChapterDownloadService.kt:160-175: per-image catch logs and rethrows only CE; chapter fails only if paths.isEmpty(); any non-empty subset is compressed and emitted Complete with pages silently missing. Native has the identical per-image catch (verified in native-app ChapterDownloadService.kt ~:163-175), so this is exact-parity behavior — but harmful per the domain risk profile (wrong-but-plausible beats failure), so it stands as a finding. Scope note: only the streaming path (MangaSource.PROCHAN.API, downloadChapterC:74); the batch path propagates per-image failures and fails the whole chapter. Fixing it deviates from the native parity spec → owner decision, report-only is the honest label.

title: Pages whose decode fails are silently dropped from the CBZ and their source files deleted
detail: decodeImageSafely / decodeAvifImageSafely / decodeAndSplitBitmaps all return an empty list when BitmapFactory/AvifDecoder fails (corrupt bytes, HTML error page saved with image content-type, unsupported format). createCbzParallel zips whatever chunk lists it got, then unconditionally deletes every original file (`imageFiles.forEach { File(it).delete() }`, line 321) and returns success. A chapter can therefore be archived with pages missing, the only evidence being a Log.w, and the original bytes are gone — unrecoverable silent data loss in the download flow. Combined with code-av-2 the chapter is still surfaced as a successful download.
evidence: decodeImageSafely returns `listOfNotNull(BitmapFactory.decodeFile(...))` (empty on null), createCbzParallel writes `processed.forEach { chunkList -> chunkList.forEach { ... } }` then deletes all inputs without checking any chunkList was empty.
suggestedFix: Fail createCbzParallel (throw) when any page decodes to an empty chunk list, or at minimum skip deleting the originals for failed pages and propagate a partial-failure signal to ChapterDownloadService.
verifierNote: Confirmed at OptimizedCbzManager.kt:347-371/373-403/405-437 (decodeImageSafely returns listOfNotNull(...) — empty on decode failure, the plain BitmapFactory path without even a log) and :306-321 (zip written from whatever chunks exist, then `imageFiles.forEach { File(it).delete() }` unconditionally, success returned). A failed-decode page is silently absent from the CBZ and its source bytes deleted. Byte-identical native port, but harmful (silent data loss in downloads) so it stands per the APP_MAP parity rule. Fix changes behavior → risky.

title: convertFilesToCbz swallows CancellationException and leaves a truncated chapter_<id>.cbz at the canonical path
detail: createCbzFromFilesWithSplitting calls ensureActive()/yield() inside the zip loop, so cancelling the host coroutine (CbzMigrationWorker being stopped by WorkManager) throws CancellationException mid-write. convertFilesToCbz catches it via `catch (e: Exception)` and returns null (CE swallowed; structured-concurrency contract broken — only the enclosing withContext exit re-raises it). Crucially, unlike OptimizedCbzManager.createCbzParallel (lines 324-336 there), nothing deletes the partially written `manga/<id>/chapter_<id>/chapter_<id>.cbz`. The reader path (data ChapterPagesRepositoryImpl:183 `cbzReader.cbzExists(...)`) prefers the canonical CBZ when present, so a truncated archive left by a cancelled/failed migration breaks offline reading of that chapter even though its loose pages are still valid. Live path: app/src/main/java/me/manga/yamiapk/work/CbzMigrationWorker.kt:45.
evidence: `suspend fun convertFilesToCbz(...) = withContext(Dispatchers.Default) { try { createCbzFromFilesWithSplitting(...) } catch (e: Exception) { Log.e(...); null } }` — no CancellationException rethrow, no partial-file cleanup anywhere in CbzManager.
suggestedFix: In createCbzFromFilesWithSplitting wrap the write in try/catch that deletes cbzFile and rethrows (mirroring OptimizedCbzManager), and in convertFilesToCbz rethrow CancellationException before the generic catch.
verifierNote: Code facts confirmed (CbzManager.kt:348-359 catches Exception incl. CE; no partial-file cleanup; live path CbzMigrationWorker.kt:45), but the major consequence is refuted: ChapterPagesRepositoryImpl.localPagesOrNull (data/.../ChapterPagesRepositoryImpl.kt:167-183) only enters the CBZ branch when the DB row's localImagePaths is a SINGLE .cbz entry — after a cancelled/failed migration convertFilesToCbz returns null, the worker never calls updateChapterLocalPaths, so the reader keeps using the still-present loose pages and offline reading is NOT broken; cbzExists:183 is only a stale-path re-derivation inside that branch. CE propagation is also self-healing: the enclosing withContext re-raises cancellation on exit. Remaining real issue: a truncated chapter_<id>.cbz leaks at the canonical path until a later successful migration overwrites it (disk waste) + the CE-in-catch(Exception) anti-pattern. Downgraded to minor; suggested cleanup-and-rethrow fix is safe.

title: Admin.isAdmin defaults to true and is never assigned anywhere — every install gets the admin complaints dashboard
detail: `var isAdmin: Boolean = true` is the sole gate (consulted by SettingsRoute.kt:156 and SettingsReworkScreenRoute.kt:128) that routes users to Screen.ComplaintAdminRework — a dashboard that lists ALL users' complaints and exposes update/delete/bulk actions against the shared Firestore `complaints_v2` collection. A repo-wide grep finds no runtime write to Admin.isAdmin (no auth check, no userId allowlist), so every shipped build exposes the moderation console and client-side mutation of other users' data (server-side Firestore rules are unverifiable from the client and the app's own SDK writes imply they are permissive). The native app has the identical `var isAdmin = true`, so this is parity — but it is harmful and needs an owner decision (real gating or default false).

title: install(HttpCache) with default unlimited in-memory storage on the singleton client that downloads chapter images
detail: Ktor's HttpCache plugin defaults to CacheStorage.Unlimited() — an unbounded in-memory map holding full response bodies for the process lifetime. This client is the Koin singleton (SharedModule.kt:118) used by ChapterDownloadService.downloadImage for every manga page; CDN image responses typically carry `Cache-Control: public, max-age=...`, so full page images accumulate in RAM during chapter downloads and long browse sessions (tens-to-hundreds of MB for big chapters) on top of the bitmap pipeline this app already tier-throttles for memory. The inline comment claims parity with the native OkHttp disk cache, but the native cache was disk-backed and size-bounded; this one is neither — so the /dados 1-day caching also does not survive process restart.
evidence: `// Honors the Cache-Control ... (parity with source's OkHttp disk cache).\n    install(HttpCache)` — no storage argument; Ktor default publicStorage = CacheStorage.Unlimited().
suggestedFix: Provide a bounded storage (e.g. Ktor FileStorage in cacheDir for parity with OkHttp's disk cache, or a size-capped storage), or scope HttpCache away from the image-download path.
verifierNote: Verified against Ktor 3.4.3 sources: HttpCache.Config defaults publicStorageNew/privateStorageNew = CacheStorage.Unlimited() (HttpCache.kt:66-67), and UnlimitedStorage is an unbounded in-memory ConcurrentMap<Url, MutableSet<CachedResponseData>> holding full bodies. The client is the Koin singleton (SharedModule.kt:118) injected into ChapterDownloadService (PlatformModule.android.kt:204-216) whose downloadImage fetches every page, so cacheable CDN image responses accumulate in RAM for the process lifetime with zero benefit (pages are saved to disk and never re-fetched). Minor wording caveat: browse-time images go through Coil's own OkHttp loader, not this client — the growth driver is the download path + ApiClient scraping. Inline parity comment (disk-backed bounded OkHttp cache) is indeed misleading; /dados cache does not survive restart.

title: doWork catch leaves the current row stuck in RUNNING and stalls the rest of the queue; also converts cancellation into Result.failure()
detail: Exceptions that escape the per-state handlers — e.g. `repo.initSite()` thrown from `.onStart` (line 194: site down, Cloudflare wall), provideActiveRepo/DAO failures — hit `catch (e: Exception)` which deletes the chapter files and returns Result.failure() WITHOUT writing FAILED to chapterDownloadDao. The row stays RUNNING in the Downloads UI and the remaining QUEUED rows are not drained until reconcileInterruptedDownloads runs (only on a later Downloads-screen visit/app start), where they are blindly re-QUEUED — a persistent site failure thus loops instead of surfacing as a failed download. The same catch also captures the deliberate `throw CancellationException()` (line 143) and the WorkManager cancellation CE, eating them instead of rethrowing (benign under WorkManager since the result of a stopped worker is ignored, but it makes the cleanup path indistinguishable from a crash).
evidence: `} catch (e: Exception) { currentChapter?.let { chapterDownloadService.deleteChapterFiles(...) }; Log.w(...); Result.failure() }` — no `chapterDownloadDao.updateFailure(...)`/updateStateChId call, no CE rethrow.

title: ForeignKeysOnCallback only applies PRAGMA foreign_keys=ON to the first pooled connection; the writer connection usually runs with FK enforcement OFF
detail: The callback's stated purpose (and inline comment, lines 9-22) is to 're-enable FK enforcement on every connection open to match native' so the onDelete=CASCADE FKs declared on saved_chapters and chapter_downloads (v10) actually fire. But Room KMP 2.8.4 does NOT invoke user RoomDatabase.Callback.onOpen per connection. Verified against room-runtime 2.8.4 sources (BaseRoomConnectionManager in RoomConnectionManager.kt): DriverWrapper.open() routes the FIRST connection through configureDatabase() (which runs migrations then onOpen -> invokeOpenCallback -> user callbacks), but every SUBSEQUENT pooled connection goes through configurationConnection(), which runs only busy-timeout/synchronous PRAGMAs plus openDelegate.onOpen (invalidation-tracker init) and never the user callbacks. BundledSQLiteDriver reports hasConnectionPool=false (verified in sqlite-bundled 2.6.2 sources), so on all three targets Room builds its own multi-connection pool (1 writer + 1 reader for TRUNCATE, 1 writer + 4 readers for WAL). Whichever pool serves the app's first DB operation gets the FK pragma; if the first operation is a read (typical at startup: Home/Library Flow collection), the pragma lands on a reader connection and the writer connection runs with SQLite's default foreign_keys=OFF for the process lifetime - the declared CASCADEs silently never fire, which is exactly the orphaned-saved_chapters bug this callback was added to fix. Conversely if a write happens first, FK child-row validation is enforced on the writer - so constraint behavior is nondeterministic run-to-run. User-visible impact is mitigated because LibraryDeo.removeMangaWithChapters + LibraryRepositoryImpl's removeHistoryByUrl/removeNotificationsByUrl purge children explicitly, but the documented 'belt-and-braces' CASCADE (ChapterDownloadEntity FK, MIGRATION_9_10 rationale) provides no actual guarantee.
evidence: Room 2.8.4 BaseRoomConnectionManager: `if (!isConfigured) { configureDatabase(connection) } else { configurationConnection(connection) }`; configureDatabase ends with `onOpen(connection)` -> `invokeOpenCallback(connection)` (callbacks.forEach { it.onOpen }), while configurationConnection runs only `configureBusyTimeout + configureSynchronousFlag + openDelegate.onOpen(connection)` - no user callbacks. BundledSQLiteDriver.hasConnectionPool == false -> newConnectionPool(maxNumOfReaders=1|4, maxNumOfWriters=1).
suggestedFix: Apply the pragma per physical connection instead of (or in addition to) the callback: wrap the driver passed to .setDriver() in a small decorator - `class ForeignKeysDriver(private val delegate: SQLiteDriver) : SQLiteDriver by delegate { override fun open(fileName: String) = delegate.open(fileName).also { it.execSQL("PRAGMA foreign_keys = ON") } }` - and pass `ForeignKeysDriver(BundledSQLiteDriver())`. Note this turns FK ON during migrations too (the current MIGRATION_9_10 rebuild is already FK-clean since it filters orphans and drops only a child table, but verify the older migrations, or defer enforcement with PRAGMA defer_foreign_keys inside migration-sensitive steps). Add a multi-connection regression test that forces a read before a write and asserts a cascade delete.
verifierNote: Verified line-by-line against room-runtime 2.8.4 sources: BaseRoomConnectionManager.DriverWrapper.openLocked routes only the FIRST connection through configureDatabase() (which ends with onOpen → invokeOpenCallback → user callbacks, RoomConnectionManager.kt:76-86,130,269-273,352-353); every subsequent pooled connection goes through configurationConnection() = busyTimeout + synchronousFlag + openDelegate.onOpen only (:137-140). BundledSQLiteDriver.hasConnectionPool == false (sqlite-bundled 2.6.2, BundledSQLiteDriver.jvmAndroid.kt:42-44) → newConnectionPool(readers=1|4, writers=1) on Android AND jvm/native (RoomConnectionManager.android.kt:95, RoomConnectionManager.jvmNative.kt:43). So the FK pragma lands on whichever physical connection opens first; a read-first startup leaves the writer with foreign_keys=OFF and the declared CASCADEs never fire — nondeterministic enforcement exactly as claimed. Mitigation also as claimed: LibraryDeo.removeMangaWithChapters (LibraryDeo.kt:63-78) purges chapters/downloads/notifications/history explicitly, so current user impact is the broken belt-and-braces, not visible orphans. Driver-decorator fix + migration caveat is correct → risky.

title: getAllComplaints fetches only the first Firestore REST page — admin complaint list silently truncated
detail: getAllComplaints() does a single GET on the collection and maps page.documents. title: Unauthenticated update/delete of arbitrary complaint documents (admin gating is client-side only)
detail: updateComplaint/deleteComplaint PATCH/DELETE any document in complaints_v2 using only the shipped public API key — no auth token, no ownership check. The file's own KDoc states the Firestore rules 'permit unauthenticated reads + writes' for this collection. If that is accurate, anyone who extracts the (public, intentionally shipped) key can read every user's complaints, vandalize them, flip statuses, or wipe the entire collection; the app's admin panel gate is purely client-side. The hardcoded key itself is fine (Firebase keys are identifiers, documented as intentional), the rules posture is the issue. APP_MAP lists complaints as the abuse surface with 'Firestore rules unseen from client', so this needs an owner/server-side decision (e.g. Firebase Auth anonymous UID + rules restricting update/delete to owner or admin claims).

suggestedFix: Server-side: tighten Firestore rules (owner-scoped writes, admin custom-claim for status changes); client: attach an auth identity. Cannot be fixed client-only.
verifierNote: Confirmed and upgraded major->critical per calibration (security + data-loss): updateComplaint/deleteComplaint PATCH/DELETE arbitrary complaints_v2 docs with only the public API key (ComplaintFirestoreRestDataSource.kt:141-168), and the rules demonstrably permit unauthenticated writes -- both the REST impl and the Android SDK impl (ComplaintFirestoreDataSource.kt:158-177, no auth attached) ship working user-edit/admin write features through this path, so any key extractor can vandalize or wipe the collection. title: shouldShowWhatsNew=true is published before isLoading=true, making the LibraryScreenRoute '!isLoading' gate racy; catches also eat CancellationException
detail: checkIfShouldShowWhatsNew sets `_shouldShowWhatsNew.value = true` and then calls loadFeatures(), which only flips `_isLoading.value = true` inside a SEPARATELY LAUNCHED coroutine (line 210-212). title: AasqRepositoryv2.initSite() never hydrates saved headers from DataStore — saved Cloudflare/auth cookies for 3asq are silently dropped every app session
detail: Every other header-bearing source in the family (e.g. sibling AzoraRepositoryv2.kt:85-89, DilarRepository.kt:181-185, and 16+ repos found via getHeadersForApi grep) implements the 'Bug 4' pattern: initSite() loads `dataStore.getHeadersForApi(API)` into `_cachedHeaders` so headers captured by the WebView CF solver survive restarts. title: Search query interpolated into URL without percent-encoding
detail: `buildSearchUrl` builds `"$API_BASE_URL/api/query?searchTerm=$query&perPage=$PER_PAGE"` with the raw user query. A query containing `&`, `#`, `+` or `%` alters or truncates the request (e.g. '#' starts a fragment, '&' injects a bogus parameter), yielding wrong/empty search results. Other repos in the tree handle this (KomikuRepository.kt:77 uses `.encodeURLParameter()`). Matches native verbatim, so this is an inherited defect rather than a port regression.
evidence: private fun buildSearchUrl(query: String): String = "$API_BASE_URL/api/query?searchTerm=$query&perPage=$PER_PAGE"
suggestedFix: Encode the query: `searchTerm=${query.encodeURLParameter()}` (io.ktor.http.encodeURLParameter).
verifierNote: buildSearchUrl (AzoraRepositoryv2.kt:73-74) interpolates the raw query; '&'/'#' are structural URL delimiters for Ktor's parser so they inject params or truncate to a fragment, and '+' decodes server-side as space — wrong/empty results for affected queries. Inherited from native as disclosed; user-visible harm justifies noting despite parity.

title: getSearchResults validates pipe-count on the raw JSON string instead of the encrypted `data.data` field; decode+decrypt sit outside the local try
detail: The `<ciphertext>|<unused>|<iv>|<keyMaterial>` format applies to `data.data`, but the guard checks `string.split("|").size < 4` on the WHOLE response JSON. It only works because the pipes of data.data happen to appear in the raw text; pipes elsewhere in the JSON can satisfy the guard while data.data has fewer than 4 segments, in which case the platform `decrypt()` actuals index enc[2]/enc[3] and throw IndexOutOfBoundsException. The initial `decodeFromString<EncryptedResponse>` and `decrypt(...)` are outside the function's try, so such failures (and non-JSON bodies like CF interstitials) propagate to fetchDataWithHeaders' catch and surface as State.Error — inconsistent with every other Dilar parse path which degrades to an empty list.
suggestedFix: Guard on `data.data.split("|").size < 4` and move decode/decrypt inside the try (or deliberately keep the throw and document it).
verifierNote: Verified at DilarRepository.kt:437-447: pipe guard runs on the raw response string while the `<ct>|<x>|<iv>|<key>` format belongs to data.data, and both decodeFromString<EncryptedResponse> and decrypt() sit outside the try; the decrypt actuals index enc[2]/enc[3] (CryptoUtils.desktop.kt:10-13), so a short data.data or non-JSON CF body throws out to fetchDataWithHeaders — unlike every other Dilar parse path which degrades to emptyList.

title: handelLoadMoreUrl builds a malformed host (missing '/' after dropTrailingSlash) — legacy Mangamello pagination can never load
detail: handelLoadMoreUrl applies .dropTrailingSlash() to the base and then concatenates 'api/v1/mangas?...' with no joining slash. With baseUrl = 'https://plus.mangamello.com/' (the enum default, and any DB-stored value with or without a trailing slash) the result is 'https://plus.mangamello.comapi/v1/mangas?sort_by=updated_at&page=N' — a different, non-existent host. The audit postscript claim (j) rationalizing this as a 'deliberate two-discipline pattern' is wrong.

title: toChapterItems dedupes by chapter number only, ignoring season/volume — can silently drop chapters of multi-season series
detail: DilarChaptersResponse.toChapterItems flatMaps every release of every chapter and then .distinctBy { it.number } where number = 'Chapter <n>'. The intent is to collapse multiple releases of the same chapter (keeps the first release), but DilarChapterDetail carries season and volume fields that are not part of the key — Season 1 Chapter 1 and Season 2 Chapter 1 both map to 'Chapter 1', so the later one is dropped from the chapter list entirely. Parity-inherited (native line 393 identical), but for any Dilar series that restarts numbering per season this loses content.

title: Arabic relative-date parser mishandles dual forms: 'يومين'/'شهرين' parsed as 1 unit, 'ساعتين' matches no branch
detail: Arabic dual forms carry no digit: 'يومين' (2 days) contains 'يوم' so the days branch fires but the digit regex finds nothing and defaults to 1 day; same for 'شهرين' (2 months) and 'أسبوعين' (2 weeks). 'ساعتين' (2 hours) contains neither 'ساعة' nor 'ساعات', so it falls through to parseArabicMonthDate and returns null. Chapter dates are off by a day/week/month or missing, which feeds Updates ordering. Edge-case inaccuracy, likely native-parity.
evidence: normalized.contains("يوم") || normalized.contains("أيام") -> { val days = Regex("\\d+").find(normalized)?.value?.toInt() ?: 1; ... } — dual suffix 'ـين' encodes 2 with no digit present.
suggestedFix: Detect the dual suffix (e.g. normalized.contains("يومين") -> 2) before the digit fallback, and add 'ساعتين' to the hours branch.
verifierNote: parseArabicDate (MangatukRepository.kt:~700-737): dual forms carry no digit so Regex("\\d+") misses and the ?: 1 fallback fires (يومين contains يوم → 1 day; same for شهرين/أسبوعين); ساعتين (ت not ة) matches neither ساعة nor ساعات and falls through to parseArabicMonthDate → null. Verified character-level.

title: Search query interpolated raw into URL without encoding — '&'/'#' in user input truncates or corrupts the query
detail: fetchSearchDataF builds "${apiUrl}series/?search=${searchType.query}&page=1..." with no URL-encoding. A query containing '&' makes the remainder parse as a separate parameter, '#' truncates at the fragment, and '+'/'%' are misinterpreted; Ktor encodes non-ASCII (Arabic works) but treats the string as pre-encoded structure otherwise. Same raw interpolation in ProMangaRepository/ProchanRepository search and in Mangatuk's normalSearchUrl. Native used the same raw string through Retrofit (parity).

suggestedFix: Encode the query component (io.ktor.http.encodeURLParameter()) before interpolation, or build with URLBuilder.parameters.
verifierNote: SwatMangaRepository.kt:182 interpolates searchType.query raw into the URL string; Ktor's URL parser treats '&' as a parameter separator and '#' as a fragment, so such queries silently corrupt the request. Native parity acknowledged, but silently-wrong search results are harmful enough to report.

title: logHeaders() dumps full header values (Cookie/cf_clearance/User-Agent) to logs on every details fetch
detail: fetchMangaChaptersF calls defaultHeaders.logHeaders() (line 100) before every manga-details request. The private logHeaders extension (lines 107-120) logs every header as '$k: $v' at INFO level, chunked so even very long values (i.e. the full Cookie header containing cf_clearance session cookies captured by the WebView solver) are fully emitted. This directly contradicts the security posture stated in BaseManga.kt:168 ('header COUNT, never names/values (must not leak Cookie/cf_clearance/UA)'). On Android these values land in logcat and can leak via bug reports/crash-report log attachments. Verbatim parity with native-app NormalSites.kt:87-107, but harmful: it leaks the exact session secrets the Cloudflare-solver subsystem is built to protect, for every NormalSites-based source.

suggestedFix: Log only header names and counts (or gate value-dumping behind a debug flag), matching the BaseManga diagnostic convention: Logger.withTag(tag).i { "headers: ${keys} count=${size}" }.
verifierNote: Verified NormalSites.kt:100 + 107-120: logHeaders() logs every '$k: $v' at INFO, chunked so arbitrarily long values (Cookie incl. cf_clearance hydrated from DataStore via initSite) are fully emitted on every NormalSites details fetch. Directly contradicts the codebase's own posture at BaseManga.kt:168 ('header COUNT, never names/values (must not leak Cookie/cf_clearance/UA)'). Verbatim native parity (native NormalSites.kt:87-107) but harmful secrets-hygiene leak. Kept major (not critical): leak is to local logcat/bug-report attachments of third-party-site session cookies, low remote exploitability.

title: initSite POSTs to a hardcoded, captured one-time Cloudflare challenge URL (embedded timestamp/nonce)
detail: The URL '.../cdn-cgi/challenge-platform/h/b/jsd/r/0.6438...:1761333314:pZh9.../993bf685d931a630' is a session-specific CF JSD beacon captured once (epoch 1761333314 ≈ Oct 2025) and frozen into source. CF challenge beacon URLs are nonce/time-bound, so this bootstrap cannot mint valid clearance cookies; initSite will persistently return -1/-2 (and, combined with BaseManga's ensureSiteInitialized latch, is never retried in-session). Verbatim parity with native-app BatcaveRepository.kt:85, and the sources map already classifies Batcave as CF-unverifiable legacy — reported so the broken-by-construction bootstrap is on record.

verifierNote: initSite POSTs to a hardcoded cdn-cgi/challenge-platform JSD beacon URL with a frozen nonce and epoch 1761333314 (Oct 2025) — verified at the `val url =` literal in initSite. CF JSD beacons are session/time-bound, so this bootstrap cannot mint fresh clearance; combined with ensureSiteInitialized's latch (code-bb-21) it fails once per session and is never retried. title: Private fetchData swallows CancellationException and surfaces raw response bodies as error messages
detail: ComickRepository bypasses BaseManga.fetchDataWithHeaders with its own fetchData (lines 505-528). Additionally the non-2xx branch (lines 521-523) uses the entire response body as the State.Error message, which can be a full HTML/JSON payload pushed into UI error text.

title: ensureSiteInitialized latches success even when initSite() reports failure via its Int return code
detail: ensureSiteInitialized sets siteInitialized=true whenever initSite() returns without throwing — but initSite implementations signal failure through return codes, not exceptions (BatcaveRepository returns -1 on network error, -2 on missing cookies, -3 on persist failure, all swallowed internally). A failed cookie bootstrap is therefore latched as 'hydrated' and never retried for the whole app session; every subsequent request for that source runs with stale/empty headers. Also note line 41 (override var baseUrl = mangaSource.BASEURL) and lines 49-50 invoke the abstract mangaSource during base-class construction — safe today only because every concrete override is a get() returning an enum constant; a field-backed override would NPE.
evidence: lines 134-138: if (siteInitialized) return; ... initSite(); siteInitialized = true — initSite's Int result is discarded.
suggestedFix: Capture the return code and only latch on success (e.g. >= 0), or document that initSite must throw on failure.
verifierNote: BaseManga ensureSiteInitialized() discards initSite()'s Int and latches siteInitialized=true on any non-throwing return; BatcaveRepository.initSite verifiably returns -1 (network/HTTP fail), -2 (no cookies), -3 (persist fail) without throwing, so a failed bootstrap is latched for the session. The construction-order note (baseUrl/ICON/PRIORITY initializers dereference abstract mangaSource) is also accurate — safe only because all overrides are get()-based.

title: by-lazy URL properties pin the base URL at first access, defeating mid-session domain hot-swap
detail: BASE_URL/homeUrl/popularUrl are `by lazy { baseUrl.ifBlank { mangaSource.BASEURL } }`. Repos are process-lifetime singletons and `baseUrl` is mutated at runtime by getBaseUrl() from SourcesDao (the domain hot-swap mechanism used for moves like lekmanga.net→lek-manga.net). Whatever value `baseUrl` holds at first lazy evaluation is frozen for the session — if the first fetch races ahead of the DB read (or the DB row is updated later), the stale domain is cached until restart. Same pattern in BatcaveRepository (lines 59-60) and BatotoEnRepositoryv2 (lines 53-54). Given how central domain moves are to this app's risk profile, the lazy caching is a footgun even though dead code paths mask it today.
evidence: line 69: override val BASE_URL: String by lazy { baseUrl.ifBlank { mangaSource.BASEURL } }; lines 78-80: homeUrl/popularUrl by lazy on the mutable baseUrl.
suggestedFix: Use custom getters (get() = baseUrl.ifBlank { mangaSource.BASEURL }) instead of lazy so the runtime baseUrl is always honored.
verifierNote: TeamXRepositoryv2.kt:69/78/80, BatcaveRepository.kt:58-59, BatotoEnRepositoryv2.kt:53-54 all declare BASE_URL/homeUrl/popularUrl `by lazy { baseUrl.ifBlank {...} }` over the mutable baseUrl that BaseManga.getBaseUrl() rewrites from SourcesDao on every feed call (HomeFeedRepositoryImpl.kt:140, SearchRepositoryImpl.kt:113, LegacyKotlinSourceClient.kt:45). First lazy access freezes the domain for the process lifetime, defeating mid-session hot-swap.

title: Invalid ksoup pseudo-selector ':containsf(Year)' throws on every MangaBuddy details parse — details page for this source always fails
detail: extractMangaInfo() calls doc.select("div.detail .info span:containsf(Year) + span"). ':containsf' is not a valid ksoup pseudo-class. The in-file KDoc (lines 15-18 and the audit postscript) claims it 'will simply match nothing' — that claim is WRONG. Empirically verified against the project's actual ksoup-jvm 0.2.6 jar: QueryParser.parse("div.detail .info span:containsf(Year) + span") throws Selector$SelectorParseException ("Could not parse query ... unexpected token at '(Year) + span'"). The exception unwinds out of extractMangaInfo before MangaInfo is constructed, is caught by BaseManga.fetchDataWithHeaders' generic catch, and is emitted as State.Error. SeparatedDetailsSites.fetchMangaChaptersF (lines 139-143) forwards any info-flow Error as the terminal state, so EVERY manga-details open on MangaBuddy (an active, DI-registered source — SharedModule.kt:144/249) fails — users can never view details, read, or download from this source. Note jsoup throws the same way, so the vendored native app is equally broken (parity-of-brokenness, but harmful, so reported per APP_MAP ground rules). The sibling dead file MangaBuddyParser.kt:292 already uses the correct ':contains(Year)'.
evidence: val yearOfProduction = doc.select("div.detail .info span:containsf(Year) + span").text()  // verified: ksoup 0.2.6 QueryParser throws SelectorParseException 'Could not parse query ... unexpected token at (Year) + span'; the valid :contains(Year) variant parses fine
suggestedFix: Change ':containsf(Year)' to ':contains(Year)' (one character) — or delete the line entirely, since yearOfProduction is never used in the returned MangaInfo. Either restores the MangaBuddy details flow.
verifierNote: Core claim independently reproduced: ran QueryParser.parse against the project's actual ksoup-jvm-0.2.6 jar — ':containsf(Year)' throws Selector$SelectorParseException ('unexpected token at (Year) + span') while ':contains(Year)' parses fine, so the in-file KDoc 'will simply match nothing' is wrong and extractMangaInfo (line 283) throws on every details parse; BaseManga.fetchDataWithHeaders:191-192 converts it to State.Error and SeparatedDetailsSites.kt:140-142 forwards it as terminal — MangaBuddy (DI-active, SharedModule.kt:144/249) details always fail. Downgraded critical→major per calibration: no crash/data-loss/security (clean error state), one source of ~50, and native is equally broken (jsoup throws the same), so this has been broken since the original app.

title: Local fetchData catches Exception without rethrowing CancellationException (eats cooperative cancellation)
detail: MangaParkRepository bypasses BaseManga.fetchDataWithHeaders with its own private fetchData (lines 537-566) whose catch block swallows ALL Exceptions, including kotlinx.coroutines CancellationException thrown while suspended in api.postJson/api.get/bodyAsText. BaseManga.fetchDataWithHeaders was explicitly fixed to rethrow CancellationException first (with a comment explaining why: cancelled navigation/scroll must not surface as a spurious State.Error and structured concurrency must unwind); this file never got that fix. A user navigating away mid-request can get the cancellation converted into an attempted emit(State.Error(0, ...)), violating the documented contract used everywhere else in sources_repositry. Also note this local fetchData never calls ensureSiteInitialized(), so the Bug-4 header-hydration guarantee documented in BaseManga (saved Cloudflare/auth headers applied even when a ViewModel forgot initSite()) does not hold for MangaPark — first-use requests can go out with empty headers until something else triggers initSite().
suggestedFix: Mirror BaseManga.fetchDataWithHeaders: add ensureSiteInitialized() at the top of the flow and a 'catch (e: CancellationException) { throw e }' clause before the generic catch.
verifierNote: Code facts confirmed: MangaParkRepository's private fetchData (lines 537-566) has only 'catch (e: Exception)' with no CancellationException rethrow, and there is no first-use header hydration (defaultHeaders = _cachedHeaders ?: emptyMap, line 108; note the class extends BaseMangaRepository, not BaseManga, so ensureSiteInitialized doesn't even exist on its parent — the fix must replicate it, not call it). Downgraded major→minor: with kotlinx-coroutines 1.9.0, flow{} emissions are cancellable, so emit(State.Error) on a cancelled collector itself throws CancellationException and structured concurrency unwinds correctly — the spurious-error path is largely neutralized; residual harm is the contract divergence plus the hydration gap on call paths not covered by ViewModel initSite() calls (details/home/downloads do call it before reading).

title: Parse failures swallowed into Success(emptyList()) — reader/search/home show empty results instead of errors on schema drift
detail: extractChapterPages (399-409), extractSearchManga (361-371) and extractChapterList (385-396) catch every parse exception, log it, and return emptyList(). Because fetchData then emits State.Success(parsedData), a MangaPark GraphQL schema change (the APP_MAP's top domain risk) produces: a reader chapter that 'successfully' loads with zero pages, a home feed / search that is 'successfully' empty, and a details page with zero chapters — all with no error state, no retry affordance, and no signal to the user. suggestedFix: Let the parse exception propagate to fetchData's catch (emitting State.Error), or return null and map null to State.Error like extractMangaDetails does, so schema drift surfaces as a retryable error instead of empty content.

title: Non-nullable, non-defaulted fields in MuComics/MuCategories make the whole comick Info decode brittle to API drift
detail: MuComics declares mu_comic_categories and mu_comic_publishers as non-nullable Lists with no defaults, and MuCategories declares slug/title as non-nullable Strings with no defaults. The comick parser Json config (ignoreUnknownKeys + coerceInputValues + explicitNulls=false) only rescues NULLABLE or DEFAULTED properties — if the comick API ever omits or nulls one of these keys inside a present mu_comics object, the ENTIRE Info decode throws MissingFieldException, extractMangaInfo returns null (ComickRepository.kt:403-410), and the details page errors — even though the data lost is only optional tag metadata. Every other model in this tree (Comic, Info, SearchItem, homeV2Item...) is defensively nullable-with-default; these two are the inconsistent brittle spots.

data class MuComics(
    val licensed_in_english: Boolean?,
    val mu_comic_categories: List<MuComicCategory?>,
    val mu_comic_publishers: List<MuComicPublisher?>
)
suggestedFix: Give the fields defaults (= emptyList(), and nullable-with-null-default for MuCategories.slug/title) to match the defensive style of the rest of the comick models.
verifierNote: MuComics.kt:8-9 has non-nullable Lists with no defaults; MuCategories.kt slug/title non-nullable Strings with no defaults. ComickRepository jsonParser (lines 59-66: ignoreUnknownKeys+coerceInputValues+isLenient+explicitNulls=false) cannot rescue non-defaulted non-nullable props — a missing/null key inside a present mu_comics throws, extractMangaInfo (403-410) returns null, and fetchMangaChaptersF emits 'Failed to parse MangaInfo' (line 387). title: Missing pagination total falls back to firing up to 999 page requests, not a sequential walk
detail: In fetchAllChaptersPaginated, when pagination.total or limit is <= 0 but has_next is true, totalPages falls back to MAX_PAGES_SAFETY (1000) and pagesToFetch becomes (2..1000) — 999 HTTP requests are launched (Semaphore-capped at 5 concurrent) with no has-next early exit. Latent request-burst (rate-limit/ban risk) that triggers on Tapas API schema drift — the top domain risk for this app. Identical in native (parity), so report-only.

suggestedFix: On missing total, walk pages sequentially and stop when pagination.has_next is false (or cap the fallback at a small number like 50).

title: ajax/chapters fallback swallows ALL exceptions (incl. CancellationException) — failed fetch silently yields 0 chapters
detail: When the details page has no inline chapter list (common on Madara sites that load chapters via AJAX), the fallback POST to "${baseUrl}ajax/chapters/" is wrapped in 'catch (e: Exception) { /* commented printStackTrace */ }'. Any network failure, Cloudflare 403, or HTTP error silently leaves chapterElements empty, so the user gets a details page with zero chapters and no error state — a wrong-but-plausible result, which the domain risk profile calls out as worse than a failure. The catch also swallows kotlinx.coroutines.CancellationException (api.postForm is a suspend call), violating the project rule that cancellation must be re-thrown (the enclosing fetchDataWithHeaders explicitly re-throws it, but this inner catch defeats that). Native has the identical silent catch, so this is parity-preserved — reported because it is harmful.

suggestedFix: Re-throw CancellationException, and on other failures propagate the error (let the exception escape so fetchDataWithHeaders maps it to State.Error) instead of silently returning an empty chapter list; at minimum log via Kermit.
verifierNote: Verified at MangaOrigineRepository.kt:351-361: the ajax/chapters fallback wraps suspend api.postForm in 'catch (e: Exception)' with a commented-out printStackTrace — swallows CancellationException and silently yields zero chapters on any network/CF failure (wrong-but-plausible result). title: Manhastro details depend on an in-memory home-feed cache; cache miss or search-result URLs make details error out

title: unwrapJsonResponse conflicts with ResultDto's @JsonNames — flat list responses would decode to a silently-empty list
detail: ResultDto (GreenShitModels.kt:17-31) is built to decode the flat GreenShit list shape {"pagina":N,"totalPaginas":M,"resultados":[...]} via @JsonNames("resultado","resultados") on _results. But every list verb (extractHomeMangaItems:147-148, extractMangaList:162-163, getSearchResults:194-195) first runs unwrapJsonResponse(), which extracts jsonElement["resultados"] — a bare JSON array — and then tries to decode ResultDto<List<MangaDto>> from that array. Decoding a class from a JSON array throws JsonDecodingException, which the enclosing catch swallows into an empty list, so if the API serves the flat shape, home/popular/search for Sussytoons are permanently empty with zero error surfaced (the exact 'wrong-but-plausible empty result' failure mode APP_MAP warns about). The two parse paths are mutually exclusive: either the wrapper shape is real (then the @JsonNames alternates 'resultado'/'resultados' on _results are dead), or the flat shape is real (then unwrap breaks all list parsing). Code is parity-identical with native-app/.../pt/sussytoons/SussytoonsRepository.kt, so if broken it is broken in both. Live verification was inconclusive: api2.sussytoons.wtf/obras/atualizacoes now returns 404 (endpoint moved — scraper rot), so a fresh fixture capture is needed to determine which path is dead.
evidence: unwrapJsonResponse(): `val unwrapped = jsonElement["resultado"] ?: jsonElement["resultados"]; return jsonParser.encodeToString(JsonElement.serializer(), unwrapped)` followed by `jsonParser.decodeFromString<ResultDto<List<MangaDto>>>(unwrappedResponse)` at lines 148/163/195 — decoding ResultDto from a bare array throws, caught into `mutableListOf()`.
suggestedFix: Capture a live response fixture for the list endpoints. If the body is flat ({pagina,totalPaginas,resultados:[...]}), stop calling unwrapJsonResponse for the three list verbs and let ResultDto's @JsonNames do the work (keep unwrap only for details/pages which use the {"resultado":{...}} wrapper). If the body is wrapper-shaped, remove the now-dead 'resultado'/'resultados' alternates from _results to make the contract honest. Either way add a parity fixture test.
verifierNote: The structural conflict is real (unwrapJsonResponse at SussytoonsRepository.kt:228-242 strips any top-level 'resultados' to a bare array which ResultDto<List<MangaDto>> cannot decode, caught into empty lists at 148/163/195; the @JsonNames('resultado','resultados') alternates on _results in GreenShitModels.kt:24 are unreachable for list verbs). But ResultDto's primary @SerialName is 'obras' — the most plausible live shape ({pagina,totalPaginas,obras:[...]}) parses fine, making this dead-code/latent fragility rather than proven user-visible breakage; live verification inconclusive (endpoint 404) and code is native-identical. Downgraded major→minor.

title: Required 'scan-id' header is permanently lost after the first Cloudflare header refresh
detail: defaultHeaders falls back to mapOf("scan-id" to "1") only when _cachedHeaders is null (lines 102-105). refreshHeaders (lines 205-208) — invoked by the WebView Cloudflare solver with ONLY the captured cookie/User-Agent map (WebViewViewModel.saveHeaders passes the raw captured headers, shared/.../webview/ui/viewmodel/WebViewViewModel.kt:54) — overwrites _cachedHeaders AND persists newHeaders to DataStore without re-merging the scan-id header. From then on (and across app restarts, because initSite at lines 82-86 reloads the stored map), every API request to api2.sussytoons.wtf is sent without scan-id, the one header the GreenShit API keys on. The sibling MediocretoonsRepository handles this correctly by always re-merging its custom headers (`base + customHeaders` in defaultHeaders, and `newHeaders + customHeaders` in refreshHeaders); Sussytoons does not. The site IS behind Cloudflare (cf-ray observed on live probe), so the solver path is realistic. Parity-identical with the native app, but harmful, hence reported per ground rules.
evidence: override suspend fun refreshHeaders(newHeaders: Map<String, String>) { _cachedHeaders = newHeaders; dataStore.saveHeadersForApi(API, newHeaders) } — no scan-id merge, unlike MediocretoonsRepository.refreshHeaders which does `newHeaders + customHeaders`.

Optionally also make defaultHeaders always overlay scan-id on the cached map.

title: Worker loop dies permanently if a DAO call outside processJob throws (downloads silently stop)
detail: The init comment (lines 130-134) claims 'the loop itself never crashes — it just keeps draining the queue', but only throwables from processJob are caught (inside the per-job launch, lines 235-246). The calls executed directly on the workerLoop coroutine — dao.getNextQueuedChapter() (line 232) and done.await()/mutex ops — are unprotected. A single Room/SQLite read failure (I/O error, disk pressure, transient driver error) propagates out of workerLoop, the applicationScope coroutine completes exceptionally, and the single worker is gone for the process lifetime: every later enqueue inserts a QUEUED row and sends a wake-up that nothing receives. Downloads then hang forever on iOS/Desktop with no user-visible error and no recovery until app restart. The same applies to the init recovery launch (lines 139-145): an exception from dao.getAllQueuedChapterIds().first() is unhandled in applicationScope (on Kotlin/Native an unhandled coroutine exception can terminate the app).
evidence: while (currentCoroutineContext().isActive) { val next = dao.getNextQueuedChapter() ?: break ... } — no try/catch around the drain; init KDoc: 'so the loop itself never crashes'
suggestedFix: Wrap the inner drain iteration (or at least the dao.getNextQueuedChapter() pull) in try/catch: rethrow CancellationException, log other throwables and `break` back to wakeups.receive() (or delay-and-retry) so the worker survives transient DB errors. Similarly wrap the init recovery body in runCatching.
verifierNote: Verified: only processJob is guarded (CoroutineDownloadRepositoryImpl.kt:235-246); dao.getNextQueuedChapter() at line 232 and the init recovery dao.getAllQueuedChapterIds().first() (139-145) run unprotected in applicationScope = CoroutineScope(SupervisorJob() + IODispatcher) with no CoroutineExceptionHandler (SharedModule.kt:207) — a DB throw kills the lone worker for the process lifetime (later enqueues wake nothing) and on Kotlin/Native an unhandled root-coroutine exception terminates the app. Contradicts the init KDoc's 'loop itself never crashes'. File is nonAndroidMain, not a frozen path — 'safe' additive fix stands.

title: Cancelling a QUEUED chapter can be silently undone: processJob unconditionally flips the row to RUNNING
detail: onCancel(chapterId) (line 167-169) marks the row FAILED ('Cancelled by user'). If the user cancels a QUEUED chapter at the same moment the worker pulls it via getNextQueuedChapter(), processJob's first statement dao.updateStateChId(entity.chapterId, DownloadingState.RUNNING) (line 265) overwrites the FAILED state with no state guard, and the chapter downloads to completion despite the cancel. The cooperative per-page check (lines 284-291) only detects state changes made AFTER the RUNNING flip. Window is narrow but real under bursty cancel-all-then-cancel-one UI interactions.
evidence: dao.updateStateChId(entity.chapterId, DownloadingState.RUNNING) — unconditional; cancel path writes FAILED via dao.updateFailure with no fencing
suggestedFix: Make the RUNNING transition conditional (UPDATE ... SET state='RUNNING' WHERE chapterId=? AND state='QUEUED', returning affected-row count) and skip the job when 0 rows were updated; requires a small DAO change.
verifierNote: Race verified: updateStateChId is an unguarded 'UPDATE ... SET state WHERE chapterId' (ChapterDownloadDao.kt:150-151); onCancel writes FAILED with no fencing (CoroutineDownloadRepositoryImpl.kt:167-169); a FAILED write landing between getNextQueuedChapter (:232) and the unconditional RUNNING flip (:265) is overwritten, and the per-page guard (:284-291) only sees post-flip changes — the cancelled chapter downloads to completion. Narrow window, minor is right; fix needs a conditional DAO transition (risky).

title: aesDecrypt guards empty ciphertext but not empty IV — malformed IV crashes via iv.refTo(0)
detail: base64Decode deliberately returns ByteArray(0) on malformed input 'rather than throwing' (its own KDoc), and cipherBytes.isEmpty() is checked (line 95) — but iv is not. A malformed/empty IV from a changed server response reaches iv.refTo(0) (line 112), which throws on a zero-length array, crashing the dilar details/pages path on iOS instead of degrading like the documented defensive intent. The Desktop/Android actuals throw a recoverable crypto exception instead.

title: Missing script-JSON island silently degrades to '{}' — produces empty Success that suppresses legacy fallback
detail: scriptJson() returns the literal string "{}" when the <script id=…> island (default __NEXT_DATA__) is absent or blank. The caller then parses an empty document, listScopes()/rootScope() yield nothing, and the verb returns AppResult.Success(emptyList()/empty fields). FallbackSourceClient only falls back to the legacy parser on Failure for home/featured/search/details (empty Success is treated as legitimate there; only pages() has a non-empty guard). So if a script-json site redesign removes/renames the island — a structural, detectable failure, unlike ordinary selector rot — the generic engine reports wrong-but-Success and the user sees an empty feed/chapterless details with no legacy fallback. This is exactly the 'NEVER ship wrong-but-Success' trap the subsystem's own safety rule warns about. Today the only bundled script-json usage is a pages endpoint (BundledSourcesConfig.kt:437), which the FallbackSourceClient non-empty-pages guard rescues, so the bug is latent rather than user-visible — hence minor, but worth closing before any list/details verb adopts script-json.

suggestedFix: When the island is absent, throw (e.g. IllegalStateException("script island #<id> not found")) instead of returning "{}" — runRequest() already maps non-cancellation throwables to AppError.Unexpected → Failure → legacy fallback. Add a golden test for the missing-island case.

title: refresh() cancelled mid-flight leaves UpdateState stuck at Refreshing forever
detail: refresh() sets `updateState.value = UpdateState.Refreshing` before the try block; CancellationException is correctly rethrown (line 84-85) but nothing resets the state, so a cancelled refresh wedges the observable state machine at Refreshing permanently (next refresh would clear it, but none may come). Stage-0 impact is nil because the state is diagnostic-only and refresh() has no production caller, but any future settings/diagnostics UI consuming `state` would show a perpetual spinner.

title: Documented 'highest revision wins' is not enforced — stale cache outranks newer bundled, and no anti-rollback for remote
detail: SourceUpdateManager's contract (SourceUpdate.kt:15-16, RemoteSourceConfigManager.kt KDoc:23-27) says the verified document 'with the highest revision wins'. ConfigMerger ranks per-source by (priority, precedenceIndex) only; document revision is merely max()'d into the output metadata. Consequences once the dynamic path turns on: (1) after an app update ships a newer bundled config (higher revision, e.g. a fixed domain), a stale-but-valid cached document still overrides it per-source at equal priority because cache has higher precedence; (2) a replayed OLDER validly-signed remote document is accepted, cached, and downgrades sources (no rollback protection). Latent today — remote is null and writeCached is the only cache writer, so no cache ever exists — but it contradicts the written precedence contract and is a security-relevant gap for Stage-1.
evidence: ConfigMerger.Ranked.beats (line 42-43) compares only priority/precedence; RemoteSourceConfigManager.refresh() appends cache/remote unconditionally of revision (lines 62-78); revision used only as `maxOf { it.revision }` (ConfigMerger.kt:36).
suggestedFix: When remote/cache documents are accepted, drop any whose revision is lower than the bundled document's (and refuse to cache a remote doc older than the current cache). Alternatively update the KDocs to state that precedence+priority, not revision, decide per-source wins — but for Stage-1 the anti-rollback check is the safer contract.
verifierNote: Verified: SourceUpdate.kt:14-16 promises 'document with the highest revision wins', but ConfigMerger.Ranked.beats compares only (priority, precedence) with later-doc-wins ties (ConfigMerger.kt:42-43), revision only maxOf'd into metadata (:36); refresh() accepts/caches cache+remote docs with no revision comparison (RemoteSourceConfigManager.kt:62-78). Stale-cache-beats-newer-bundled and remote replay/rollback both real; latent in Stage-0 (remote=null, writeCached unreachable).

title: Validator gaps: FilterSpec.op/mode, EndpointSpec.method/format, and blank endpoint URLs are unchecked
detail: validateSource() checks transforms/date/image strategy names and pagination type, but not: (1) FilterSpec.op — GenericSourceClient.passesFilters treats an unknown op as matched=false (GenericSourceClient.kt:148), so a typo'd op with mode="include" silently drops EVERY list item, yielding an empty Success that list verbs do NOT fall back from (empty Home for that source); (2) FilterSpec.mode (anything ≠ "include" behaves as exclude); (3) EndpointSpec.method — methodOf() maps unknown strings to GET silently (GenericSourceClient.kt:216-220); (4) EndpointSpec.format — unknown values fall into the listSelector heuristic; (5) blank EndpointSpec.url. For bundled configs these are caught by parity tests, but the validator is the only gate for future cached/remote documents, where a typo would pass signature+validation and break a source without tripping fallback.

title: ItemScope.field() re-resolves the primary locator on fall-through (duplicate JsonPath walk / Ksoup attr lookup)
detail: JsonItemScope.field() evaluates `JsonPath.string(node, spec.path)` at line 32 and again, identically, at line 36 as the terminal return — for absent/empty fields (the common case for optional fields like item.rating across every list item) the path is walked twice per field per item. HtmlItemScope.field() has the same shape: `attrOf(target, spec.attr)` computed at line 54 and re-computed at line 62. Behavior is identical to caching the first result; the duplication is pure waste in the per-item hot loop.
evidence: Extractor.kt:32 + 36 (same JsonPath.string call), 54 + 62 (same attrOf call).
suggestedFix: Hoist the first evaluation into a local (`val primary = …`), early-return when non-empty, and return `primary` at the end instead of recomputing.
verifierNote: Verified: JsonItemScope.field evaluates JsonPath.string(node, spec.path) at Extractor.kt:32 and identically again as the terminal return at :36; HtmlItemScope.field computes attrOf(target, spec.attr) at :54 and again at :62. Both locators are pure reads, so hoisting the first result into a local is behavior-identical.

title: pages() reads the header store twice and parses the response body twice; chapter pagination re-parses every page body
detail: pages() calls requestHeaders() for the Page image headers (line 92) and then runRequest() calls requestHeaders() again for the HTTP request (line 176) — two suspend header-store (DataStore) reads per chapter open for every source with usesCapturedHeaders=true. Inside the extractor lambda the same response body is fully parsed twice: Extractor.listScopes (line 95) and Extractor.rootScope (line 99) each run Ksoup.parse/Json.parseToJsonElement over the whole body (script-json sources parse the HTML and the JSON island twice each). Similarly chaptersPaginated() parses each chapters page once in chaptersFrom and again in paginationState (lines 354, 377) — up to 200 pages. None of this is incorrect, but manga page/chapter bodies are large and this is the hottest engine path.
evidence: GenericSourceClient.kt:92 vs 176 (double headersFor read); 95+99 (listScopes + rootScope both parse resp.body); 354+377 (chaptersFrom + locatorValues both parse the same body).
suggestedFix: Pass the already-computed headers into runRequest (or hoist a parsed-document handle): e.g. parse the body once into an internal ParsedBody (Ksoup Document or JsonElement) and derive listScopes/rootScope/locatorValues from it.
verifierNote: Verified: pages() calls requestHeaders() (GenericSourceClient.kt:92) and runRequest calls it again (:176) — two DataStore reads per chapter when usesCapturedHeaders; listScopes (:95) and rootScope (:99) each fully re-parse resp.body (Extractor.kt:103-114, script-json parses HTML+JSON island twice each); chaptersPaginated parses each page body in chaptersFrom and again in paginationState->locatorValues (:354,:377; Extractor.kt:131-141).
