title: Genre blacklist (and recentChapters) ignore per-verb field overrides — a verb with only '<verb>.item.genres' skips blacklist filtering
detail: homeFeedItemFrom/featuredFrom resolve fields through verbKey() so a verb-specific override like 'featured.item.genres' or 'search.item.genres' takes precedence, but isBlacklistedByGenre() reads only the base key: it returns false when config.fields["item.genres"] is null and extracts via the base spec otherwise (lines 163-167). Two consequences: (1) a source that declares genres only as a per-verb override gets no blacklist filtering on that verb despite declaring blacklistGenres; (2) when the base spec targets the wrong format for an overridden verb (e.g. Tapas: base item.genres is a JSON listPath but search is HTML), the filter silently extracts nothing. recentChaptersFrom (line 268) has the same base-key-only shape. Today's bundled configs happen not to define <verb>.item.genres, so impact is latent — but the asymmetry between mapping (override-aware) and filtering (base-only) is an authoring trap.
evidence: GenericSourceClient.kt:163-166 uses literal "item.genres"; homeFeedItemFrom:249 uses verbKey(verb, "item.genres") for the same data.
suggestedFix: Thread the verb into isBlacklistedByGenre and resolve the spec via verbKey(verb, "item.genres") (and likewise consider verbKey for "item.recentChapters"), keeping the null-spec short-circuit.
verifierNote: Asymmetry verified: isBlacklistedByGenre reads literal "item.genres" (GenericSourceClient.kt:164-165) while mapping resolves via verbKey (:249); recentChaptersFrom likewise base-only (:268). Tapas demonstrates the trap shape today (blacklistGenres :507, base item.genres is JSON listPath :521, search verb is HTML with overrides :523-525 and no search.item.genres -> HtmlItemScope.fieldList with empty selectors returns emptyList -> no filtering on search); no bundled <verb>.item.genres exists, so user impact stays latent.

title: Duplicate LazyColumn keys ('admin' x2) from the two static pinned FAQ entries crash the rework Feedback Manager list
detail: items(key = { it.id.ifEmpty { it.subject + it.createdAt } }) assumes ids are unique. But ComplaintListRepositoryImpl.loadUserComplaints() prepends PINNED_COMPLAINTS (data/src/commonMain/kotlin/me/manga/yamiapk/data/repository/PinnedComplaints.kt) — BOTH entries have id = "admin" (non-empty, so the ifEmpty fallback never fires). state.filtered therefore always contains two items with key "admin" when no filter is active, and LazyColumn throws IllegalArgumentException ("Key admin was already used") on first composition of the list. Every successful load of the rework user Complaint screen crashes. Today only the dark-launched Screen.ComplaintRework route reaches this screen (nothing calls navigate(Screen.ComplaintRework) yet — the live Settings path still uses the legacy Screen.Complaint), so it is not yet user-reachable; it becomes a guaranteed launch-blocking crash the moment the rework route is wired. The same key lambda exists in AdminComplaintScreen.kt:420, but the admin list is Firestore-only (unique doc ids, no pinned prepend) so it is not currently affected.
evidence: ComplaintScreen.kt:339 `items(items = state.filtered, key = { it.id.ifEmpty { it.subject + it.createdAt } })`; PinnedComplaints.kt:94 and :111 both declare `id = "admin"`; ComplaintListRepositoryImpl.kt:133 `PINNED_COMPLAINTS + legacy(userId).map { it.toSummary() }`; ComplaintViewModel derives filtered=applyFilter(all,...) with no dedupe.
suggestedFix: Make the key collision-proof, e.g. key = { c -> if (c.id.isNotEmpty() && c.id != "admin") c.id else "${c.id}|${c.subject}" } — or simpler and robust: key = { "${it.id}|${it.subject}|${it.createdAt}" }. Alternatively give each PINNED_COMPLAINTS entry a distinct synthetic id (e.g. "admin-pinned-1"/"admin-pinned-2") in :data.
verifierNote: Crash mechanics fully verified (ComplaintScreen.kt:339 key lambda; PinnedComplaints.kt:94+:111 both id="admin"; ComplaintListRepositoryImpl.kt:133 prepends both; applyFilter has no dedupe and default filters pass both) — duplicate LazyColumn keys at indices 0-1 throw on first composition. But the finding's reachability claim is WRONG: the live Settings feedback destination routes to Screen.ComplaintRework for non-admins (SettingsRoute.kt:156, registered for the live Screen.Setting at App.kt:650-652), and the legacy Screen.Complaint route (App.kt:728-730) renders the SAME rework ComplaintScreen (ComplaintScreenRoute.kt). Every successful load of the user feedback list crashes today -> upgraded major to critical.

title: Complaint card body swallows taps (combinedClickable onClick = {}), so tapping most of the card does not open the action dialog
detail: The body Text (up to 10 lines — usually the largest area of the card) is wrapped in Modifier.combinedClickable(onClick = {}, onLongClick = copy). The empty inner onClick consumes plain taps before they reach the Card's clickable(onClick = OnRowClick), so tapping the complaint body does nothing while tapping the title/padding opens the Reply/Edit/Delete dialog. Native user-side ComplaintCard (native-app .../complaint/ui/components/ComplaintCard.kt) has NO click handler on the body — taps anywhere on the card open the dialog — so this is a parity regression introduced when the admin-side long-press-copy affordance was lifted to the user row. (The admin row's identical pattern at AdminComplaintScreen.kt:849 DOES match native admin behavior and is not a finding.)
evidence: ComplaintScreen.kt:513-519 `modifier = Modifier.combinedClickable(onClick = {}, onLongClick = { clipboardManager.setText(...); onLongClickBody() })` vs native ComplaintCard body Text with no clickable; card-level clickable at ComplaintScreen.kt:440.
suggestedFix: Forward the row click: `combinedClickable(onClick = onClick, onLongClick = {...})` (pass the row's onClick into ComplaintRow's body modifier). Long-press copy is preserved; plain taps open the dialog as native does.
verifierNote: Verified: ComplaintScreen.kt:513-519 body Text wraps combinedClickable(onClick = {}, onLongClick = copy) — the inner clickable consumes plain taps so the Card-level clickable (ComplaintScreen.kt:440) never fires for body taps. title: Adaptive-mode trigger fires for ordinary inline parents: badge expands to fill the row and a second sibling badge collapses to ~1dp
detail: The adaptive branch is gated on `maxWidth.isSpecified && maxWidth.value.isFinite()`, intended to distinguish 'bounded width (weighted cell)' from 'unbounded inline'. But in Compose a non-weighted Row child is measured with a FINITE max width (the parent's remaining width), so virtually every call site takes the adaptive branch. Consequences at the real inline call sites (LibraryScreen.kt:1331/1348, the below-cover download/bookmark badges inside a plain Row): (1) the adaptive branch's Row(Modifier.fillMaxWidth(), Center) makes the first badge consume ALL remaining row width with a 24dp icon (clamp ceiling) centered mid-card, instead of the intended compact 14dp right-aligned form; (2) the second badge is then measured with ~0 remaining width, so iconDp coerces to 1.dp and the font to 1.sp — the bookmark badge is effectively invisible whenever a manga has both downloaded and bookmarked chapters with showDetails enabled; (3) the leading Spacer(weight(1f)) receives 0 width so right-alignment is lost. The fixed 'inline fallback' (iconSize=14dp/labelSmall/2dp spacing) is dead code — no real parent supplies infinite max width.
evidence: YamiCountBadge.kt:68 `val adaptive = maxWidth.isSpecified && maxWidth.value.isFinite()` + :80 `Row(modifier = Modifier.fillMaxWidth(), ... Center)`; inline call sites LibraryScreen.kt:1331/1348 pass only `Modifier.padding(start = spacing.xs)` inside `Row { Spacer(Modifier.weight(1f)); ... }` — Row children get finite max-width constraints, so adaptive is always true.
suggestedFix: Make adaptive scaling opt-in: add `adaptive: Boolean = false` to YamiCountBadge and pass adaptive = true only from the on-cover LibraryCardDetailBadges (weighted) call sites; keep the compact fixed-size branch as the default. (Constraint inspection cannot distinguish the two cases — the weighted cells also have finite bounded width.)
verifierNote: Verified against Compose Row measurement semantics: non-weighted Row children are measured with finite maxWidth (remaining width), so at LibraryScreen.kt:1331/1348 (plain Row inside a finite grid cell) BoxWithConstraints.maxWidth is finite and the adaptive branch (YamiCountBadge.kt:68) always fires; its fillMaxWidth Row (line 80) makes the first badge consume all remaining width (icon clamped to 24dp, centered), the second badge then gets ~0 maxWidth (icon coerced to 1.dp, font 1sp — effectively invisible), and the weighted leading Spacer collapses to 0 so right-alignment is lost. The fixed inline fallback is unreachable from any current call site. Opt-in adaptive param is the correct fix; rendering-behavior change -> risky stands.

title: availableAppVersions comparator is not a consistent total order (mixes numeric and lexicographic comparison per pair)
detail: sortedWith compares numerically when BOTH versions parse to numeric parts, but falls back to string comparison when either side has none — so for a list mixing parseable and unparseable versions ('1.2', '10.0', 'beta'), transitivity can be violated (a<b numeric, b<c string, c<a string). Kotlin's sort (TimSort) can throw 'Comparison method violates its general contract!' once the list exceeds ~32 elements; below that the order is merely arbitrary. Also note 'mapNotNull { toIntOrNull() }' silently drops suffixes ('1.2-beta' compares as 1.2). Realistic impact is low (few distinct versions, mostly numeric), but the comparator is incorrect as written.
evidence: AdminComplaintScreen.kt:354-372: `if (aParts.isNotEmpty() && bParts.isNotEmpty()) { ...numeric... } else { b.compareTo(a) }` — the comparison strategy depends on the pair, not on a per-element key.
suggestedFix: Sort by a per-element key instead, e.g. compareByDescending<String> { it.split('.').firstOrNull()?.toIntOrNull() ?: Int.MIN_VALUE } chained across parts, or partition parseable/unparseable versions and sort each group independently before concatenating.
verifierNote: Verified at AdminComplaintScreen.kt:354-372: comparison strategy is chosen per pair, and a concrete cycle exists (descending: '2' before '1x' by string, '1x' before '10' by string, but '10' before '2' numerically), violating transitivity — JVM TimSort can throw IllegalArgumentException on larger inputs; realistic impact low as stated.

title: Grid columnCount is remembered once and never recomputed when constraints change (window resize / adaptive columns)
detail: `val columnCount = remember { slotSizesSums(constraints).size }` has no keys, so the column count computed on first composition is reused even after the available width changes. With GridCells.Adaptive on Desktop (window resize) the actual column count changes while the remembered value stays stale, corrupting the thumb-drag-to-item mapping math (columnNum/offsetRatio at lines 355-358) until the scroller happens to be recreated. On Android the composition is rebuilt on rotation so the impact is Desktop/window-resize only.
evidence: VerticalFastScroller.kt:341 `val columnCount = remember { slotSizesSums(constraints).size }` inside the subcompose lambda — constraints is a fresh measure-pass value but is not a remember key.
suggestedFix: Key the remember on the relevant inputs: `remember(constraints.maxWidth, slotSizesSums) { slotSizesSums(constraints).size }`.
verifierNote: Verified: VerticalFastScroller.kt:341 remember{} has no keys so columnCount goes stale when constraints change; LibraryScreen.kt:1114 uses GridCells.Adaptive, so Desktop window resize changes the real column count while the thumb-drag math (:355-358) keeps the stale one. The identical pattern exists in native (LazyVerticalScrollerWithScrollBar.kt:278) but native is Android-only where recreation masks it — on the Desktop target it is a live defect, so parity does not refute.

title: Unreachable over-limit error states: onValueChange caps input at maxChars, so isError / error-colored counter / length guards can never trigger
detail: ReplyContent caps input at 500 chars in onValueChange (line 433: `if (it.length <= maxChars) replyText = it`), so `isError = replyText.length > maxChars` (line 440), the red counter color (line 454), and the `trimmed.length <= maxChars` submit/enabled guards (lines 474/484) are all dead conditions. suggestedFix: Either drop the unreachable isError/length-guard branches, or (closer to typical Material UX) allow typing past the cap and rely on the isError + disabled-submit path to communicate the limit.

Both EditContents initialize from existing data (ComplaintActionDialog.kt:508 and AdminComplaintActionDialog.kt:601 editedBody = complaint.body), so a pre-existing body over the 1000-char cap makes isError/submit-guard reachable and load-bearing there — deleting those branches would change behavior. title: Zero-size Spacer(Modifier.height(0.dp)) between title and status chip is a no-op (likely meant a width gap)

title: lastChapterDateLabel renders 'Today' for future-dated chapters
detail: The header's last-chapter date label uses `days <= 0L -> Today`, so a chapter whose source-supplied date is in the future (timezone skew or sloppy scraped dates — a known domain risk) renders as 'Today'. The sibling chapterRelativeDate in the same file deliberately routes negative day-deltas to the absolute date format instead (line 2296 comment). The two formatters handle the same edge inconsistently.
evidence: return when { days <= 0L -> stringResource(Res.string.np_details_today); ... } vs chapterRelativeDate's `when (days) { 0L -> today; 1L -> yesterday; else -> absolute }`.
suggestedFix: Use `days == 0L -> Today` and let negative deltas fall through to the ISO/absolute fallback, matching chapterRelativeDate.
verifierNote: Verified: DetailsScreen.kt:1368 'days <= 0L -> Today' renders future-dated chapters as Today, while the sibling chapterRelativeDate (:2296-2297) deliberately routes negative deltas to the absolute format, and native HeaderSection.kt:121-126 uses exact when(days) matching (0L/1L/else) so it never clamps future to Today either — the inconsistency is real on both axes.

title: LibraryCard tap/long-press uses raw pointerInput — no click semantics, no ripple
detail: The card uses Modifier.pointerInput { detectTapGestures(onTap/onLongPress) } instead of combinedClickable. This means: (1) no ripple/indication feedback on tap; (2) no semantics — TalkBack/VoiceOver users cannot activate the card to open Details or long-press to enter selection mode (the inner action IconButtons are reachable, but opening a manga from the library — a core flow — is not exposed to screen readers). Also note the pointerInput is keyed on (item.manga.title, isInSelectionMode) rather than the unique url used as the lazy-grid key.
evidence: .pointerInput(item.manga.title, isInSelectionMode) { detectTapGestures(onTap = { onIntent(OnItemClick...) }, onLongPress = { onIntent(OnItemLongClick...) }) }
suggestedFix: Replace with Modifier.combinedClickable(onClick = ..., onLongClick = ...) which provides ripple + click/long-click semantics, keying captured state via rememberUpdatedState if needed.
verifierNote: LibraryScreen.kt:1180-1185 raw pointerInput/detectTapGestures has no click semantics or indication, so screen readers cannot open Details from the library card. Native MangaCard.kt:124 used .clickable (semantics + ripple), so this is a regression, not parity; multi-select long-press is a rework addition, making combinedClickable the right fix.

title: Bulk-remove snackbar formats the localized template with a manual String.replace of '%1$d'
detail: The ShowBulkRemoveSuccess collector does `bulkRemovedTemplate.replace("%1\$d", effect.count.toString())` instead of resource formatting. This silently breaks (shows the raw '%1$d' literal) if any locale's translation uses a different placeholder form (e.g. '%d', positional reorder, or Arabic-script digit variants added later). All 11 current translations happen to use %1$d, so it works today, but it's a fragile contract that the resource formatter would handle for free.
evidence: snackbarHostState.showSnackbar(bulkRemovedTemplate.replace("%1\$d", effect.count.toString()))
suggestedFix: Hoist the count formatting into composable scope is impossible (dynamic), but stringResource(Res.string.library_bulk_removed, count) can be pre-resolved per-effect by holding the effect in a state variable rendered by a composable, or keep the replace but add a fallback when the placeholder is absent. Minimal fix: document and assert the placeholder, or restructure like UpdatesScreen does for its parameterized strings.
verifierNote: Claim verified: LibraryScreen.kt:306 manual replace("%1$d") and all 11 locale strings currently use %1$d (works today, fragile contract). Suggested fix is muddled; the clean option the finding misses is compose-resources' suspend getString(Res.string.library_bulk_removed, effect.count) callable directly in the collector, though it diverges from the project's pre-resolve convention - keep risky.

title: No BackHandler for selection mode — system back exits the screen/app instead of clearing the selection
detail: LibraryTopBar registers a BackHandler only for the search bar (line 530). When the user is in multi-select mode (isInSelectionMode), pressing system back does not clear the selection — Library is the root bottom-tab on Android, so back backgrounds/exits the app while a selection is active. DetailsScreen implements exactly this pattern for its chapter selection (DetailsScreen.kt:482 BackHandler(enabled = state.isInChapterSelectionMode) { OnSelectionClear }), so the Library surface is inconsistent with the sibling screen.
evidence: Only `BackHandler(enabled = showSearchBar) {...}` exists; no handler gated on state.isInSelectionMode.
suggestedFix: Add BackHandler(enabled = state.isInSelectionMode) { onIntent(LibraryIntent.OnSelectionClear) } in LibraryScreenContent or LibraryTopBar.
verifierNote: Only BackHandler in LibraryScreen.kt is :530 gated on showSearchBar; nothing for isInSelectionMode. DetailsScreen.kt:482 implements the pattern for chapter selection. Native Library had no selection mode at all (no parity shield), so the inconsistency and Android back-exits-app behavior are real.

title: Items-per-row Slider truncates instead of rounding the slider value
detail: onValueChange = { onCountChange(it.toInt()) } truncates toward zero. Material3 Slider with steps snaps via float lerp, which can produce values an epsilon below the integer tick (e.g. 2.9999998), truncating to the previous step — the caption and persisted value can lag one notch behind the thumb. The KDoc itself says 'onCountChange receives the rounded slider position'.
evidence: Slider(value = count.toFloat(), onValueChange = { onCountChange(it.toInt()) }, valueRange = 0f..8f, steps = 7)
suggestedFix: Use kotlin.math.roundToInt(): onCountChange(it.roundToInt()).
verifierNote: LibraryOptionsSheet.kt:389 `onCountChange(it.toInt())` truncates; M3 stepped Slider snaps in px space and the px->user-value lerp round-trip can return ticks an epsilon below the integer, mapping to the previous step. KDoc at :374 promises 'rounded'. roundToInt() fix compiles and preserves behavior.

title: Page scrubber truncates the slider value instead of rounding
detail: ReaderPageScrubber's onValueChange computes `newValue.toInt().coerceIn(0, lastIndex)`. With steps-based snapping the float tick value can be an epsilon below the integer, so toInt() maps the thumb to page N-1; the `if (newRel != positionInChapter)` guard then dispatches a one-off page jump. Rounding removes the epsilon sensitivity.
evidence: val newRel = newValue.toInt().coerceIn(0, lastIndex); if (newRel != positionInChapter) onSeekToChapterPage(newRel)
suggestedFix: Use newValue.roundToInt().coerceIn(0, lastIndex).
verifierNote: ReaderScreen.kt:1244-1248 same stepped-Slider toInt() truncation (steps = pageCount-2 at :1251); an epsilon-low tick maps the thumb to page N-1 and the inequality guard then dispatches a spurious one-page jump. roundToInt fix valid. Same pattern as code-bj-9 but a distinct widget/file needing its own fix - not a duplicate.

title: Grid-mode next-page spinner occupies a single grid cell instead of spanning the row
detail: In HomeGrid the isLoadingNextPage spinner is added via `item { NextPageSpinner() }` with no span, so it renders inside one adaptive cell at the tail of the grid (off-center, easily mistaken for a broken cover). List mode's spinner is full-width. It also lacks a key, unlike the list-mode counterpart ("__nextpage__").

title: Carousel per-item scale recomposes every visible card on every scroll frame
detail: The continuous parallax scale is computed in a derivedStateOf and read in composition via `Modifier.scale(scale)`. Because the derived value changes continuously while scrolling, every visible card recomposes on every scroll frame (derivedStateOf only dedupes equal values). The idiomatic fix keeps the read in the draw phase: `Modifier.graphicsLayer { val s = listState.itemCenterScale(index); scaleX = s; scaleY = s }`, which skips recomposition entirely. The in-code comment acknowledges the recompose-per-frame behavior.
evidence: val scale by remember(index) { derivedStateOf { listState.itemCenterScale(index) } } ... Modifier.width(150.dp).scale(scale)
suggestedFix: Replace .scale(scale) with .graphicsLayer { val s = listState.itemCenterScale(index); scaleX = s; scaleY = s } and drop the derivedStateOf.
verifierNote: FeaturedCarousel.kt:87-95 reads the continuously-changing derivedStateOf value in composition (`Modifier.scale(scale)`), so every visible card's item scope recomposes per scroll frame; the in-file comment admits it. graphicsLayer-block read defers to layer update phase and compiles (itemCenterScale is file-private, accessible).

The user gets no clue why conversion failed.

title: formatRelativeDate renders negative day counts ('-1 days ago') for future timestamps
detail: For a lastReadDate in the future (device clock rolled back, or timezone-skewed writes), days is negative; the `days == 0L`/`== 1L` arms fail and `days < 7` matches, producing 'days_ago' with a negative number. formatGroupLabel in the same file is safe (negative falls to the absolute-date branch), so only the per-row subtitle is affected.
evidence: val days = date.date.daysUntil(today).toLong(); ... days < 7 -> stringResource(Res.string.days_ago, days.toInt()) — no lower bound.
suggestedFix: Clamp first: `val days = date.date.daysUntil(today).toLong().coerceAtLeast(0L)`.
verifierNote: Verified: HistoryScreen.kt:399-404 has no lower bound — negative days skip ==0L/==1L and match days < 7, rendering 'days_ago' with a negative count; formatGroupLabel (:384-392, days in 2..6) is safe as stated, and native Date.kt explicitly guards futures (timeAgo: seconds < 0 -> ""; toRelativeString: exact equality), so this is not native parity.

title: Stale KDoc: RequestSourceDialog claims SendComplaintUseCase rejects bodies under 8 chars
detail: The RequestSourceDialog KDoc states bodies in the 5-7 char range 'will reach the legacy SendComplaintUseCase's require(body.length >= 8) block and surface a snackbar error' and that a Phase 10 lift 'will reconcile the UI gate (5) with the use case gate (8)'. The use case was already reconciled to MIN_BODY_LENGTH = 5 (shared/.../complaint/usecase/SendComplaintUseCase.kt:20), as the SettingsScreen FeedbackDialog KDoc (GAP-SET-11) documents. The doc contradicts current behavior — 5-7 char submissions succeed.
evidence: SendComplaintUseCase.kt: `const val MIN_BODY_LENGTH = 5` vs SourcesScreen.kt KDoc: "require(body.length >= 8)".
suggestedFix: Update the KDoc paragraph to state the gates now match at 5 (mirroring the SettingsScreen FeedbackDialog KDoc).
verifierNote: SourcesScreen.kt:972-977 KDoc claims the use-case gate is require(body.length >= 8) pending a Phase 10 reconcile; shared SendComplaintUseCase.kt:14,20 already enforces MIN_BODY_LENGTH = 5. Stale-KDoc-contradicting-code is a sanctioned minor finding per APP_MAP; doc-only fix.

title: New NSNumberFormatter allocated on every formatGroupedNumber call (called per stat row in composition)
detail: formatGroupedNumber constructs a fresh NSNumberFormatter on every invocation. Apple's documentation explicitly flags NSNumberFormatter creation as expensive and recommends caching instances. The function is called from StatisticsScreen's formatCount (StatisticsScreen.kt:323, :336, :452 — one call per stat row) inside composition, so every recomposition of the Statistics screen allocates several formatters. The Desktop/Android actuals use NumberFormat.getIntegerInstance, which is much cheaper. Low absolute impact (Statistics is not a hot scrolling list), but it is the textbook cache-your-formatter case.
suggestedFix: Hoist the formatter to a file-level cached instance, e.g. `private val groupedFormatter = NSNumberFormatter().apply { numberStyle = NSNumberFormatterDecimalStyle }` and use it in the actual. Safe because all call sites are main-thread composition (NSNumberFormatter is not thread-safe, so keep it UI-only), and iOS app-language changes require a relaunch (IosLocaleSwitcher writes AppleLanguages, picked up on next launch), so a process-lifetime formatter can never hold a stale locale.
verifierNote: NumberFormatting.ios.kt:9 allocates a fresh NSNumberFormatter per call; call sites verified at StatisticsScreen.kt:323/336/452 via formatCount (composition scope, main thread). File-level cached instance is sound: main-thread-only use and iOS locale switch requires relaunch, as the finding itself argues.

title: Stray attribute pasted as text content inside <shape> (app:tint=... as a text node)
detail: Line 8 contains the literal text `app:tint="?attr/colorOnBackground"` between the <solid> and <stroke> child elements, i.e. an attribute accidentally pasted into the element body. It is well-formed XML (a text node) and Android's GradientDrawable inflater silently ignores character data, so it never tints anything - the author's intent (tinting the thumb) was silently lost. Note the byte-identical defect exists in the compose-resources twin composeApp/src/commonMain/composeResources/drawable/custom_seekbar_thumb.xml (other shard); the compose-resources copy is the one actually shipped to users. The :app copy itself is unused (see res-aa-1).
evidence:
<solid android:color="?attr/colorOnBackground"/>
    app:tint="?attr/colorOnBackground"
    <stroke ...
suggestedFix: Delete the stray text line (the <solid> already provides the color, making the lost tint redundant); apply the same removal to the composeApp composeResources twin.
verifierNote: Verified line 8 of app/.../custom_seekbar_thumb.xml is the literal text node app:tint="?attr/colorOnBackground" between <solid> and <stroke>; GradientDrawable inflation ignores character data. The composeApp composeResources twin is byte-identical (diff verified).

title: Invalid <selector> structure: bare <solid> child, no <item> entries
detail: A StateListDrawable (<selector>) may only contain <item> children; this file puts a <solid> directly inside the selector. StateListDrawable inflation skips unknown non-item elements, producing a selector with zero states that draws nothing. It only "works" because drawing nothing looks transparent. The compose-resources twin (composeApp/src/commonMain/composeResources/drawable/transparent_background.xml, other shard) is byte-identical, and compose-resources' stricter vector/XML loader cannot parse a <selector> at all, so any future Res.drawable.transparent_background use would fail at runtime. The :app copy is unused (see res-aa-1).
evidence:
<selector xmlns:android="...">
    <solid android:color="@android:color/transparent" />
</selector>
suggestedFix: Delete the file (unused), or if a transparent drawable is ever needed, replace with <shape><solid android:color="@android:color/transparent"/></shape> or reference @android:color/transparent directly.
verifierNote: Verified: <selector> containing a bare <solid>, no <item>; StateListDrawable inflation skips non-item children, yielding a zero-state drawable that draws nothing. composeApp twin exists and compose-resources cannot parse <selector> (vector-only). Accurate.

title: Progress layer-list would render incorrectly if ever used: no <clip>/<scale> wrappers, oval track layers
detail: A SeekBar/ProgressBar progressDrawable layer-list must wrap the @android:id/progress and @android:id/secondaryProgress layers in <clip> (or <scale>) so they are clipped to the current level; here they are plain <shape>s, so the "filled" layer would always draw at full width regardless of progress. Additionally the background and secondaryProgress layers use android:shape="oval" with a 1dp height plus a <corners> element (meaningless on an oval) while the progress layer is a rectangle - the track and fill would not even have matching geometry. File is currently unused in :app (res-aa-1) and has a compose-resources twin, so this is latent, not live.
evidence: <item android:id="@android:id/progress"><shape android:shape="rectangle">... (no <clip>); background/secondaryProgress: <shape android:shape="oval"><size android:height="1dp"/><corners android:radius="2dp"/>
suggestedFix: Delete with res-aa-1; if ever revived, wrap progress layers in <clip> and use shape="rectangle" (or "line") for all three layers.
verifierNote: custom_seekbar_progress.xml verified: plain <shape> items with no <clip>/<scale>, so the progress layer ignores level (GradientDrawable does not respond to setLevel) and would draw full-width; background/secondaryProgress are oval+1dp+corners vs rectangle progress. Latent (file unused per res-aa-1) but the defect description is accurate Android semantics.

title: Notification small icon declares 240dp x 240dp intrinsic size
detail: ic_message.xml is the Firebase default notification small icon (manifest meta-data) and the FCM setSmallIcon drawable, but its root <vector> declares android:width/height="240dp" for a 24x24 viewport. Status-bar icons are rendered at ~24dp; the 10x intrinsic size means any code path that rasterizes the drawable at intrinsic bounds (e.g. Drawable.toBitmap(), some OEM notification renderers, or future reuse in an ImageView without explicit size) allocates a ~960x960 px bitmap for a tiny glyph. Functionally the system notification pipeline scales it down, so impact today is cosmetic/defensive.
evidence: <vector ... android:height="240dp" android:viewportHeight="24" android:viewportWidth="24" android:width="240dp">
suggestedFix: Change android:width/android:height to 24dp (viewport already 24).
verifierNote: ic_message.xml root <vector> declares android:width/height=240dp with a 24x24 viewport (verified), and it IS the live FCM small icon (manifest:98-100 + MyFirebaseMessagingService.kt:63). Impact correctly framed as defensive/cosmetic -> minor.

title: Dark-mode Theme.YamiManga sets android:windowBackground to white, causing white flashes in dark mode (parity inversion vs native)
detail: The night-qualified Theme.YamiManga sets android:windowBackground=@color/white. In native, the night themes.xml defines a DIFFERENT style name (Theme.YamiManga.Dark) that is never applied: the native manifest uses Theme.App.Starting -> postSplashScreenTheme Theme.YamiManga, and no setTheme() call references the .Dark style (verified by grep over native-app/app/src/main/java). So natively, in night mode, the values/ definition of Theme.YamiManga wins and the effective dark windowBackground is @color/black. The KMP port renamed the dormant .Dark style to Theme.YamiManga in values-night, which ACTIVATES its windowBackground=@color/white in dark mode. Result: dark-mode users get a white window background visible between splash dismissal and Compose's first frame, and on every activity recreation (rotation, in-app theme/locale switch) — the exact white-flash problem the splash-theme comment in values/themes.xml (L43-47) says was fixed. The in-file comment ('Mirrors native ... verbatim from native L102') is accurate about the copied value but wrong about the effect, since native never applies that style.
evidence: values-night/themes.xml L23: <item name="android:windowBackground">@color/white</item> — vs native effective night windowBackground @color/black (values/themes.xml Theme.YamiManga, the only definition native ever applies). Native night style is named Theme.YamiManga.Dark; KMP renamed it to Theme.YamiManga, activating it.
suggestedFix: In app/src/main/res/values-night/themes.xml change <item name="android:windowBackground">@color/white</item> to @color/black (restores native's effective dark-mode behavior), or better @color/yami_manga_background to track the M3 dark surface. Also update the file comment to note that native's .Dark style was dormant.
verifierNote: app/values-night/themes.xml:23 sets windowBackground=@color/white (#FFFFFFFF, not redefined in values-night/colors.xml) on the style name the app actually applies (manifest Theme.App.Starting -> postSplashScreenTheme Theme.YamiManga). Grep over native-app source shows zero setTheme/.Dark references, so native's night-mode effective windowBackground is values/themes.xml Theme.YamiManga = @color/black (L102); the KMP rename of the dormant .Dark style activated the white background — parity inversion confirmed, white flash in dark mode on launch and every activity recreation.

title: 44 of the 78 shard drawables in composeApp/composeResources are unreferenced and shipped on all three platforms (~244 KB), 6 of them shadowing live same-named copies in :ui
detail: Exhaustive reference check: the only consumers of composeApp's generated Res.drawable accessors are RepoIconResolver.kt (40 source-brand icons) and Plus18memes.kt (anti_horny_*). There are no Res.allDrawableResources / Res.getUri / Res.readBytes or string-keyed lookups anywhere in composeApp/:ui/:sources, :shared has no composeResources at all, and the only other grep hits are inside comments (e.g. MangaSource.kt '/* R.drawable.ic_xxx */') or KDoc. That leaves 44 of this shard's 78 composeApp drawables dead: bg_dialog_reading_mode, bg_reading_mode_item, cache_cleaner, custom_seekbar_progress, custom_seekbar_thumb, dots, earth_svgrepo_com, gradient_overlay, ic_adult, ic_back_, ic_bookmark, ic_bookmark_bold, ic_cancel, ic_check_24dp, ic_comick, ic_complaint, ic_day_night, ic_done_down_arrow, ic_download, ic_edit_sur, ic_glasses, ic_image_broken, ic_instagram, ic_launcher_background, ic_launcher_foreground, ic_message, ic_new, ic_next, ic_open_ad, ic_panal_shera, ic_plus_18, ic_pluss18, ic_previous, ic_readcomiconline, ic_reader_continuous_vertical_24dp, ic_reader_horizontal_, ic_reader_ltr, ic_reader_ltr_24dp, ic_reader_rtl, ic_reader_rtl_24dp, ic_reader_setting, ic_reader_vertical_24dp, ic_reader_webtoon_24dp, ic_share_24dp (~244 KB raw; compose-resources has no shrinker, so all are packed into the Android APK, iOS framework and Desktop jar). Six of these (cache_cleaner, ic_complaint, ic_day_night, ic_launcher_foreground, ic_pluss18, ic_reader_setting) duplicate same-named files in ui/src/commonMain/composeResources/drawable — the :ui copies are the live ones (ui code imports me.manga.yamiapk.ui.generated.resources), so editing the composeApp copy silently does nothing; three of the pairs (cache_cleaner, ic_complaint, ic_day_night, ic_reader_setting) have already drifted in content. Rot examples among the dead files: ic_message.xml declares a 240dp x 240dp intrinsic size for a 24x24 viewport; ic_comick is a stale lower-res duplicate of the used ic_comickio; dots.xml carries a UTF-8 BOM.
evidence: grep -rE 'drawable\.<name>\b' over all module sources (build/ excluded) yields 0 hits for each of the 44 names from composeApp's Res; RepoIconResolver.kt L130-176 enumerates the 34 used shard icons; ui/.../composeResources/drawable contains the 6 shadowed names and ui screens import me.manga.yamiapk.ui.generated.resources.Res.

If any are anticipated for upcoming reader-UI ports, move them to :ui (where the live copies of the shadowed six already are) instead of keeping dual copies.

title: Five non-vector Android drawables (shape/selector/layer-list) in composeResources can never render via compose-resources; custom_seekbar_thumb.xml additionally contains stray junk text
detail: compose-resources only supports VectorDrawable XML (plus bitmap files) for DrawableResource; bg_dialog_reading_mode.xml (<shape>), bg_reading_mode_item.xml (<selector>), custom_seekbar_progress.xml (<layer-list>), custom_seekbar_thumb.xml (<shape>) and gradient_overlay.xml (<shape>) were copied verbatim from native's Android res/drawable but are unparseable as vectors — any future painterResource(Res.drawable.bg_reading_mode_item) etc. (e.g. when the reading-mode dialog or reader seekbar port lands) will throw at runtime on every platform, even though the generated accessors exist and compile. custom_seekbar_thumb.xml is broken even by Android standards: line 8 is stray character data ('app:tint="?attr/colorOnBackground"' floating between elements, not an attribute), and line 7 references ?attr/colorOnBackground which cannot resolve outside an Android themed context. All five are currently unreferenced (see res-ab-2), so this is latent, not live.
evidence: xmllint root elements: bg_dialog_reading_mode=shape, bg_reading_mode_item=selector, custom_seekbar_progress=layer-list, custom_seekbar_thumb=shape, gradient_overlay=shape. custom_seekbar_thumb.xml L7-8: <solid android:color="?attr/colorOnBackground"/> followed by stray text 'app:tint="?attr/colorOnBackground"'.
suggestedFix: Delete the five files (they are dead and unusable). When the reading-mode dialog / reader seekbar UI is ported, implement these as Compose shapes/brushes (RoundedCornerShape + Brush.verticalGradient) rather than drawable XML.
verifierNote: Root elements verified: bg_dialog_reading_mode=<shape>, bg_reading_mode_item=<selector>, custom_seekbar_progress=<layer-list>, custom_seekbar_thumb=<shape>, gradient_overlay=<shape>; compose-resources DrawableResource XML parsing is vector-only, so painterResource on any of these throws at runtime. Stray text node in custom_seekbar_thumb.xml line 8 verified. All five unreferenced (res-ab-2), latent as stated.

title: backup_rules.xml / data_extraction_rules.xml are unedited IDE templates, so allowBackup=true backs up everything including cf_clearance cookies
detail: Both files are the untouched Android Studio templates (all rules commented out) while the manifest sets android:allowBackup="true", android:fullBackupContent="@xml/backup_rules" and android:dataExtractionRules="@xml/data_extraction_rules". An empty rule set means the entire app data dir is eligible for Google cloud backup and device-to-device transfer: the Room DB (library/history) plus DataStore preferences, which per the app map include captured Cloudflare cf_clearance cookies and user-agent strings. Restoring stale CF cookies onto a new device is also functionally useless (IP/UA-bound) and can resurrect solved-challenge state that immediately 403s. This is byte-identical to native (parity), so changing it is an owner decision; flagged because backup of session tokens is the kind of default worth a deliberate choice rather than a leftover template.
evidence: backup_rules.xml L8-13: <full-backup-content> with only commented-out sample rules; data_extraction_rules.xml likewise; app/src/main/AndroidManifest.xml L24-26 wires both with allowBackup=true. Identical files exist in native-app (diff confirms).
suggestedFix: Owner decision: either exclude the DataStore/prefs files holding cf_clearance cookies from cloud-backup/device-transfer rules, or document that full backup is intended. Keep behavior identical to native if strict parity is preferred.
verifierNote: Verified: both XMLs are untouched IDE templates (all rules commented out) and byte-identical to native-app's copies (diff), while manifest:24-26 wires allowBackup=true + both rule files. Empty rules = full app-data backup incl. DataStore-held cf_clearance/UA per APP_MAP. Parity-bound owner decision -> report-only correct.

title: Android-style \' and \" escapes render as literal backslashes in compose-resources strings (multiple locales, live screens)
detail: Many string values across both modules' composeResources catalogs use Android-aapt escaping (\' and \"). Compose Multiplatform resources 1.11.0 does NOT unescape these: the Gradle converter (PrepareComposeResources.kt handleSpecialCharacters) only handles \n, \t, \uXXXX and \\, and the runtime formatter only substitutes %N$s/%N$d. The backslash therefore ships to screen. Confirmed in the built artifact: ui/build/.../values/strings.commonMain.cvr packs what_s_new as base64 of "What\'s new". Live, user-visible examples: EN default what_s_new (Settings row + About row -> shows "What\'s new"; ui values/strings.xml:24 and composeApp values/strings.xml:300), np_p3_whats_new_title + np_p3_whats_new_loading (What's New screen title), languages_coming_soon_description, request_language_prompt, please_don_t_close_the_app_until_conversion_is_complete; np_admin_active_filter_search shows literal \"...\" in ALL 11 locales (used at AdminComplaintScreen.kt:584); French catalog is worst hit (~25 used keys: time_just_now "A l\'instant" History timestamps, error_occurred, failed_to_load_image, grant_permission, notification_permission, details_more_options, library_delete_selected_message, language_restart_hint, ...); Italian (~8 used keys) and Turkish (~10 used keys: welcome_title "Yami Manga\'ya...", action_open_in_browser, error_network_forbidden, library_empty_message_format, ...) similarly affected. composeApp locale catalogs carry the same defect for legacy-routed strings.
evidence: compose-gradle-plugin 1.11.0 handleSpecialCharacters handles only \n/\t/\uXXXX/\\; runtime SimpleStringFormatRegex = %(\d+)\$[ds]. Built CVR: string|what_s_new|V2hhdFwncyBuZXc= -> 'What\'s new'.
suggestedFix: Mechanical sweep over composeApp/src/commonMain/composeResources/values*/*.xml and ui/src/commonMain/composeResources/values*/*.xml replacing \' with ' and \" with " (compose-resources needs no apostrophe/quote escaping). Do not touch \n/\t/\u escapes.
verifierNote: Verified end-to-end: compose-gradle-plugin 1.11.0 handleSpecialCharacters (extracted from sources jar) only converts \n, \t, \uXXXX and \\; the built CVR artifact base64-decodes what_s_new to literal `What\'s new`; \' escapes present in live keys across modules/locales (composeApp values/strings.xml:300, ui values-fr/strings.xml:171 time_just_now, np_admin_active_filter_search with \" in base + fr). Mechanical unescape sweep is safe and behavior-preserving except for the bug.

title: np_reply_to_complaint_id uses bare %s in every locale - argument is never substituted, users see literal '%s'
detail: The key np_reply_to_complaint_id is defined with a non-positional %s in the default catalog (ui values/strings_np_complaint_etc.xml:32 'Reply to Complaint ID: %s') and in all 10 locale catalogs (shard files: values-ar/strings_backfill_parity.xml:91, values-tr/strings_backfill_parity.xml:135, etc.). Both consumers are live (Settings routes to the rework complaint screens via SettingsRoute.kt:156; legacy admin route renders the rework admin screen).

title: Indonesian locale (values-in) is unreachable on Desktop (JDK 17+) and iOS - falls back to English
detail: The app stores Indonesian as code 'in' (LanguageRepositoryImpl.SUPPORTED_LANGUAGES) and all Indonesian resources live in values-in/ dirs (composeApp + ui). compose-resources matches the folder against Locale language verbatim. On Desktop, LocalAppLocale.desktop.kt does Locale.setDefault(Locale.forLanguageTag("in")) and since JDK 17 Locale returns the NEW ISO code: Locale.forLanguageTag("in").getLanguage() == "id" (verified empirically with jshell on this machine: prints 'id'). compose-resources then looks for values-id, which does not exist, so Indonesian users on Desktop get English. On iOS, AppleLanguages is set to ["in"] but NSLocale canonicalizes the deprecated code to languageCode "id" (ResourceEnvironment.ios.kt reads locale.languageCode), so iOS very likely falls back to English too. Android is unaffected (its Locale.getLanguage() still returns the legacy 'in'). All values-in files in this shard (composeApp/values-in/strings.xml, ui/values-in/*) are dead weight on 2 of 3 platforms.
evidence: jshell: Locale.forLanguageTag("in").getLanguage() -> id (OpenJDK 21; JDK>=17 behavior). LocalAppLocale.desktop.kt:28-29; ResourceEnvironment.ios.kt uses locale.languageCode; no values-id dirs exist.
suggestedFix: Owner decision: either (a) duplicate/rename Indonesian dirs to values-id and keep values-in for Android compatibility (compose-resources reads the same folders on Android, where the language code is 'in', so BOTH dirs are needed), or (b) normalize the code in LocalAppLocale per platform (map 'in'->'id' before forLanguageTag/AppleLanguages is not enough because Android compose-resources needs 'in'). Simplest robust fix: ship both values-in and values-id copies.
verifierNote: Reproduced locally: Locale.forLanguageTag("in").getLanguage() == "id" on JDK 21 (JDK 17+ new-ISO-code default), and LocalAppLocale.desktop.kt:28-29 feeds exactly that into Locale.setDefault. compose-resources 1.11.0 sources confirm LanguageQualifier matching is raw string equality and the desktop/iOS environments derive "id" (Locale.getDefault / NSLocale.languageCode, which canonicalizes deprecated "in"), while only values-in dirs exist (no values-id) and the stored code is "in" (LanguageRepositoryImpl.kt:159) — Indonesian falls back to English on Desktop (proven) and iOS (canonicalization semantics). Android unaffected.

title: Turkish percent_completed '%%1$d tamamlandi' diverges from default placeholder signature
detail: Default is '%1$d%% completed'; the Turkish copy is '%%1$d tamamlandi' - the translator moved the percent sign before the number (correct for Turkish) but produced a different placeholder signature (%% + literal 1$d under aapt semantics). Under compose-resources the regex would coincidentally still substitute the inner %1$d but the leading % stays doubled ('%%42'). The key is currently unreferenced (see res-ac-6) so the defect is latent, but it is the only locale/default format-signature mismatch in the catalog and will bite if the key is revived.
evidence: values-tr/strings.xml:24 vs values/strings.xml:27; format-arg diff scan flagged only this key.
suggestedFix: Either delete with the unused-key sweep or correct to '%%%1$d tamamlandi' / restructure to positional-only '%1$d%% tamamlandi' per Turkish convention.
verifierNote: Core claim verified: values/strings.xml:27 '%1$d%% completed' vs values-tr/strings.xml:24 '%%1$d tamamlandı' is a real placeholder-signature divergence and the key has 0 code refs (latent). Rendering detail corrected: under compose-resources the regex consumes the second '%' so it renders '%42 tamamlandı' (single %, arguably correct Turkish), not '%%42'; under aapt/Formatter semantics it would render literal '%1$d tamamlandı'. Mismatch worth fixing either way.

title: Android-style \' and \" escapes are NOT unescaped by compose-resources — literal backslashes render in the UI in every locale
detail: The string values were copied verbatim from native Android res XML where AAPT requires apostrophes to be escaped (\'). Compose Multiplatform resources do not need or process this escape: the Gradle conversion step unescapes \n/\t but passes \' and \" through unchanged, and the runtime (components-resources 1.11.0 StringResourcesUtils.kt) only Base64-decodes and substitutes %N$s args. Verified empirically against the project's own build output: ui/build/.../preparedResources/.../values/strings.commonMain.cvr stores what_s_new as `What\'s new` while chapters_converted_successfully's \n IS converted to a real newline. Result: users see e.g. "What\'s new" in Settings/About (SettingsScreen.kt:1157, AboutScreen.kt:353), "You\'re on the last chapter" in the reader end-of-chapter card (ReaderScreen.kt:2115), "Yami Manga\'ya Hoş Geldiniz" on the Turkish Welcome screen, "Riavvia l\'app..." in the Italian language-restart hint, and `Search: \"x\"` in the admin filter summary — on all three platforms. 62 occurrences across ui/composeResources (all locales incl. ar/de/es/fr in other shards) and 66 more in composeApp/composeResources (out of this shard). Shard files/lines: values/strings.xml:24,62,64,137; values/strings_np_details_reader.xml:41; values/strings_np_settings_theme_lang.xml:29,42; values/strings_pfix_p3_complaint.xml:41; values/strings_pfix_p3_whatsnew.xml:17,18; values-it/strings.xml:69,70,73,76,111; values-it/strings_backfill_new.xml:158,182; values-it/strings_backfill_parity.xml:19; values-it/strings_pfix_lang_restart.xml:3; values-ja/strings_backfill_new.xml:158; values-pt/strings_backfill_new.xml:158; values-ru/strings_backfill_new.xml:158; values-tr/strings.xml:18,52,69,70,181; values-tr/strings_backfill_new.xml:86,158; values-tr/strings_backfill_parity.xml:71,90,135.
evidence: values/strings.xml:24 `<string name="what_s_new">What\'s new</string>`; decoded .cvr value is literally `What\'s new`; runtime StringResourcesUtils.kt does Base64.decode only — no escape handling for \' or \".
suggestedFix: Strip the backslash before ' and " in all compose-resources XML catalogs (XML needs no escaping for either character in element text): \' -> ' and \" -> " across ui/ and composeApp/ composeResources values*/ files. Add a lint/grep gate to keep AAPT-style escapes out of compose-resources catalogs.
verifierNote: Verified end-to-end: values/strings.xml:24 has What\'s new; the project's own prepared resource (ui/build/.../values/strings.commonMain.cvr) stores base64 V2hhdFwncyBuZXc= which decodes to What\'s new with the literal backslash; runtime decodeAsString (StringResourcesUtils.kt:41-43) is Base64.decode only and replaceWithArgs substitutes positional args only — no \' unescaping anywhere. title: Home feed scroll position is reset to top on EVERY re-entry (back from Details, tab return, rotation) — the KMP port dropped native's previousTabIndex guard
detail: HomeGrid (line 468) and HomeList (line 516) both run `LaunchedEffect(state.activeTabIndex) { gridState.scrollToItem(0) }` with no first-composition guard. LaunchedEffect bodies always run once when the composable (re-)enters composition, not only when the key CHANGES. The grid/list states are rememberLazyGridState/rememberLazyListState (rememberSaveable-backed), so when the user navigates Home -> Details -> back, the NavHost's SaveableStateHolder restores the scroll position — and this effect immediately wipes it back to item 0 (the HomeViewModel survives on the back stack, so state.feed is still populated and the jump is user-visible). Same loss on bottom-tab return and on Android configuration change. Native explicitly guards this: native-app/.../home/ui/screens/HomeScreen.kt:110-120 keeps `var previousTabIndex by remember { mutableStateOf(activeTabIndex) }` and only scrolls when `previousTabIndex != activeTabIndex`, so first composition / restore never resets. The KMP comment cites GAP-HOME-20 'legacy parity' but ports only the unguarded half of the legacy code.

title: Details parallax offset is read in the Scaffold content scope, not deferred to draw — every scroll frame over the header recomposes the whole Details content and re-runs the uncached DetailsState getters
detail: `val parallaxOffset by remember(headerBandHeightPx) { derivedStateOf { ... listState.firstVisibleItemScrollOffset ... } }` (line 466) changes on every scroll pixel while firstVisibleItemIndex == 0 (the tall details header). The delegate is read at line 569 (`DetailsParallaxBackdrop(coverUrl = ..., parallaxOffset = parallaxOffset)`) inside the Scaffold `padding ->` content lambda, so that entire content scope — including the `when` branch that calls DetailsBody with ~20 arguments — recomposes on every frame of header scrolling. The in-code comment claims the derivedStateOf means 'only this backdrop recomposes as the user scrolls', which is false: derivedStateOf only helps when the derived value changes less often than its inputs; here the derived Float changes per frame and the read site is the parent scope. Each of those per-frame recompositions re-evaluates `state.displayChapters` (the uncached get() that re-runs full dedup+filter+sort — see the existing DetailsState.kt:285 finding) plus firstUnreadChapter, and pays an O(n) list-equals for DetailsBody skipping — per frame on a screen whose chapter list can be 1000+ rows. DetailsParallaxBackdrop already applies the offset inside `graphicsLayer { translationY = -parallaxOffset }` (line 1319), so the value could be read there at draw time with zero recomposition.

suggestedFix: Change DetailsParallaxBackdrop to take `parallaxOffset: () -> Float` (or the State<Float> itself) and read it INSIDE the graphicsLayer block: `.graphicsLayer { translationY = -parallaxOffset() }`. Pass `{ parallaxOffset }` from the call site so composition never reads the per-frame value (the graphicsLayer lambda re-executes at draw, not composition). title: OnSelectLanguage launches an unwrapped suspend persistence chain with bare viewModelScope.launch — a throw escapes the MVI safety net (#29 crash class, missed in this VM)
detail: handle()'s OnSelectLanguage branch runs `viewModelScope.launch { setLanguage(intent.code) }`. SetLanguageUseCase -> LanguageRepositoryImpl.setLanguage is an unwrapped `suspend Unit` that performs a legacy DataStore write (`legacy.setLanguage(code)`, can throw IOException) followed by the platform `localeSwitcher.applyApplicationLocale(code)` facade call. There is no try/catch, no Result/AppResult wrapping, and the bare launch is a sibling coroutine outside submit()'s try/catch, so any throw escapes viewModelScope and crashes the process (Android routes it to the crash handler; iOS/Desktop terminate). This is exactly the #29 crash class already fixed in History/Updates and flagged for Sources (SourcesViewModel:154), Theme (ThemeViewModel:140) and WhatsNew — LanguageViewModel was missed. The sibling OnSubmitRequest launch is safe (its use case returns Result).

suggestedFix: Replace the bare launch with the base-class `launchSafely { setLanguage(intent.code) }` (routes throws to onUnhandledError), matching the crash-safety posture already applied to History/Updates.

title: Statistics init Room-flow collector has no .catch — inconsistent with the #17 crash-safety fix applied to HistoryViewModel for the identical posture

title: Locale.setDefault() mutates process-global state during composition — same bug class as the flagged Desktop sibling, Android actual was missed
detail: LocalAppLocale.provides (a @Composable) executes `if (default == null) default = Locale.getDefault()` and `Locale.setDefault(locale)` directly in the composition body rather than in a SideEffect. Composition must be side-effect free: Compose may re-execute, reorder, or discard compositions (speculative/failed compositions never apply), yet this mutates the JVM-global default locale and the object's captured `default` field on every (re)composition pass. The identical issue in the Desktop sibling was found (LocalAppLocale.desktop.kt:29 'Locale.setDefault() mutates process-global state during composition (not in a SideEffect)'); the Android actual carries the same pattern plus the extra `default` field write and was not flagged.
evidence: LocalAppLocale.android.kt:22-29 — `@Composable actual infix fun provides(value: String?)` body runs `default = Locale.getDefault()`, `Locale.setDefault(locale)` and builds a new Configuration, all during composition.
suggestedFix: Hoist the mutation into a SideEffect (mirror whatever resolution is chosen for the Desktop sibling finding) so the global-locale write only happens when the composition is applied; keep the Configuration override as the composition-time value.
verifierNote: LocalAppLocale.android.kt:25-28 mutates Locale.setDefault() and the captured `default` field directly in the @Composable provides body — a composition-time global side effect that re-fires on every recomposition and applies even for discarded compositions. Same class as the flagged Desktop sibling. Risky is right: the `current` getter and same-frame Locale.getDefault() readers are sensitive to when the write lands, so moving it to SideEffect changes first-frame ordering.

title: NSUserDefaults written during composition on every recomposition of the app root (side effect in @Composable provides)

title: Page-share PNG encode runs synchronously on the main thread in the legacy-args reader route (twin of the flagged sibling route)

title: Fire-and-forget CBZ-cache cleanup on the app-lifetime scope can race a concurrent re-extract of the same chapter (rapid Next->Prev or exit->reopen)
detail: clearExtractedPages launches `cbzReader.cleanupExtractedCache(...)` (a recursive delete of the chapter's extract dir) on the repository's app-lifetime cleanupScope, fire-and-forget. ReaderViewModel calls it on every chapter change (onEnter line 387, for the chapter being left) and in onCleared. Nothing serializes that delete against DefaultCbzReader.extractImages, which writes into the SAME directory (`cacheDir/cbz_extract/<mangaId>/<chapterId>`). If the user re-enters the just-left downloaded chapter while the cleanup is still in flight — tapping Next then immediately Prev, or closing and instantly reopening the reader — deleteRecursively can run concurrently with the new extraction: extracted page files are deleted after the page list is returned (Coil then fails on every file:// URL, all pages render broken) or the extraction throws mid-write (caught -> emptyList -> localPagesOrNull returns null and a downloaded chapter silently re-fetches from the network, which fails entirely when offline). The window is real because the cleanup does two Room reads before deleting up to ~200 files.
evidence: ChapterPagesRepositoryImpl.kt:211-215 `cleanupScope.launch { ... cbzReader.cleanupExtractedCache(entity.mangaId, chapterId) }` (no join/serialization); DefaultCbzReader.kt:94-129 extractImages writes into `fs.cacheDir / EXTRACT_ROOT / mangaId / chapterId` and `catch (e: Exception) { ... emptyList() }`; ReaderViewModel.kt:387 fires cleanup on every intra-manga chapter change.
suggestedFix: Serialize per-chapter cleanup and extraction (e.g. keep a per-chapter Mutex or a map of in-flight cleanup Jobs in ChapterPagesRepositoryImpl and have localPagesOrNull await/cancel the pending cleanup for that chapter before extracting).
verifierNote: Verified: clearExtractedPages (ChapterPagesRepositoryImpl.kt:211-215) is fire-and-forget on the app-lifetime cleanupScope with no serialization against DefaultCbzReader.extractImages, which writes the same cacheDir/cbz_extract/<mangaId>/<chapterId> dir (DefaultCbzReader.kt:94, deleteRecursively at :152); ReaderViewModel fires it on every chapter change (:387) and onCleared (:816). Rapid Next->Prev re-extract can interleave with the in-flight recursive delete -> broken file:// pages or a silent network re-fetch. Narrow window, degraded-not-crashed outcome: minor/risky as filed.

title: Reader list/pager keys use the bare page URL — duplicate page URLs crash the reader (native keys include the index)
detail: ReaderVerticalListBody keys image rows on item.page.url alone (line 1559-1563), and both pagers key pages on pages[index].url (lines 1681, 1764). Nothing dedups page URLs anywhere in the chain: ChapterPagesRepositoryImpl maps the scraped URL list 1:1 to Page objects and ReaderViewModel stores them verbatim. Scraped chapters routinely contain the same image URL twice (repeated credits/recruitment pages a scanlator appends to every chapter — fatal in the continuous appended feed where two chapters coexist in one LazyColumn; ad/banner images matched twice by loose selectors, e.g. Zazamanga's 'every img[data-src]' fallback). Two items with the same key composed in the same window throw IllegalArgumentException ('Key ... was already used') and crash the app mid-read. The native reader explicitly defends against this: WebToonReadingMode.kt keys ImagePage as "${item.chapterIndex}-${item.request.data}-${index}" — the rework dropped the index suffix and regressed the guarantee.
evidence: ReaderScreen.kt:1559 `is ReaderFeedItem.Image -> item.page.url`; :1681/:1764 `key = { index -> pages[index].url }`. Native WebToonReadingMode.kt:142 `key = { index, item -> ... "${item.chapterIndex}-${item.request.data}-${index}" }`. No distinct()/distinctBy on pages in ChapterPagesRepositoryImpl.fetchPages or ReaderViewModel.runFetch/appendChapterPages.
suggestedFix: Key by feed/page index combined with the URL (e.g. "$index:${item.page.url}" in ReaderVerticalListBody, "$index:${pages[index].url}" in both pagers), mirroring the native key shape. Alternatively dedup-preserving-order is NOT safe (pages may legitimately repeat), so the composite key is the right fix.

Duplicate co-composed URLs throw the duplicate-key IllegalArgumentException mid-read. Crash requires near-adjacent duplicates co-composed, so major. r2-comp-3 is a duplicate of this.

title: Loose-file downloaded chapters skip the stale-path re-derivation/existence check the CBZ branch got — broken pages with no network fallback after iOS container change
detail: localPagesOrNull's CBZ branch re-derives the archive location from the CURRENT filesDir because 'on iOS that path embeds the app sandbox container UUID, which changes across reinstall / backup-restore — leaving the stored path stale while isDownloaded stays true' (lines 170-191). The loose per-page branch (lines 194-197) has the exact same failure mode but no fix: it returns entity.localImagePaths verbatim with no existence check and no re-derivation under the live chapterDir. After an iOS reinstall/restore (or any event that moves the files), a chapter downloaded with the CBZ preference off yields N file:// URLs to nonexistent files — every page renders the per-page error pane and there is no fall-through to the network fetch (the list is non-empty so the function returns it). This is strictly worse than the pre-fix CBZ behavior, which at least degraded to a network re-fetch via the extractImages empty-list path.
evidence: Lines 194-197: `} else { // Loose per-page files, already in page order as the downloader stored them.\n entity.localImagePaths }` — contrast with lines 182-191 where the CBZ path calls cbzReader.cbzPath/cbzExists to re-derive. CoroutineDownloadRepositoryImpl.downloadOnePage persists absolute outPath strings (line 405), which embed the iOS container UUID.
suggestedFix: In the loose branch, re-derive each stored path's filename under the current appFileSystem chapter dir (the layout is fixed: chapterDir(mangaId, id)/image_<n>.<ext>), falling back to the stored path; if none of the resolved files exist, return null so the caller falls through to the network fetch.
verifierNote: Claim confirmed: the loose branch (ChapterPagesRepositoryImpl.kt:194-197) returns entity.localImagePaths verbatim — no existence check, no re-derivation — while the CBZ branch (:182-191) re-derives for exactly the iOS container-UUID staleness; the nonAndroid downloader persists absolute outPath strings (CoroutineDownloadRepositoryImpl.kt:399-405,343) and keeps loose pages when CBZ pref is off or archiving fails (:325-330). Adjusted fixSafety safe->risky: the suggested fix needs AppFileSystem injected into the repo (chapterDir is an AppFileSystem extension; CbzReader exposes no dir API) plus a DI change, and it alters the offline-read fallback behavior.

title: Android download flow has no terminal-state guarantee — a source flow that completes without Success/Error leaves the row stuck RUNNING forever
detail: downloadChapterFlowV2 flatMapConcats the legacy source's State flow into DownloadState and the doWork loop relies on a terminal Complete/Error emission to move the row out of RUNNING. But several legacy sources' chapter flows can complete after emitting only State.Loading (verified: ProMangaRepository/ProchanRepository chapter-load parse failure emits nothing after Loading — already-confirmed findings in those files). In that case the flow maps Loading -> InProgress(0,0) and completes; handleErrorSafely never runs, so the row set to RUNNING at line 140 is never updated. The chapter shows 'downloading' forever this session, and reconcileInterruptedDownloads re-queues it on every launch into the same dead loop, with no error ever surfaced. The iOS/Desktop sibling explicitly guards this case: CoroutineDownloadRepositoryImpl.collectImageUrls fails the row with 'No images for chapter' when the flow yields no terminal Success — the Android path is missing the equivalent guard (engine-twin drift).
evidence: DownloadWorkerV2.kt:135-154 — `chapterDownloadDao.updateStateChId(chapter.chapterId, DownloadingState.RUNNING)` then `downloadChapterFlowV2(...).collect { ... }` with no post-collect terminal check. flatMapConcat (lines 195-217) only emits Error for State.Error; a Loading-only flow produces no terminal state. Contrast CoroutineDownloadRepositoryImpl.kt:270-274 `if (imageUrls.isEmpty()) { dao.updateFailure(entity.chapterId, "No images for chapter"); return }`.
suggestedFix: After the collect in doWork (or inside downloadChapterFlowV2), verify the row reached a terminal state and mark it FAILED ('No images for chapter') if it is still RUNNING — mirroring the nonAndroid impl. Equivalently, track whether a Complete/Error state was seen during collect and call handleErrorSafely when none was.
verifierNote: Verified end-to-end: DownloadWorkerV2.kt:140-153 sets RUNNING then collects with no post-collect terminal check; flatMapConcat (195-217) maps Loading->InProgress only. Loading-only completion is real: ProMangaRepository.kt:165-170 (ImageCombinerState.Error with zero collected images emits nothing after Loading, flow completes) and ProchanRepository.kt:148-153 likewise. DownloadRepositoryImpl.kt:117-120 reEnqueueInterrupted() re-queues the stuck RUNNING row on every launch; the nonAndroid twin guards exactly this (CoroutineDownloadRepositoryImpl.kt:270-274 'No images for chapter').

title: An empty appended chapter silently dead-ends the continuous feed: it is retried forever and chapters beyond it are unreachable
detail: appendChapterPages skips an empty next chapter (`return@collect` at line 547) without adding it to loadedChapterUrls and without any user feedback. onAppendNextChapter derives the next chapter from loadedChapterUrls.lastOrNull(), so every subsequent scroll-to-end (and every tap on the boundary card) re-attempts the SAME empty chapter, re-fires markChapterRead(tailUrl) each time, and never advances — chapters after the empty one can never be reached in WEBTOON/CONTINUOUS_VERTICAL modes. Zero-page chapters are a real occurrence on scraped sources (locked chapters, parser misses). The replace-path (runFetch) deliberately classifies empty-as-error with a retry pane (#4 fix); the append path got no equivalent handling.
evidence: Lines 544-548: `if (newPages.isEmpty()) { FlowLog.log(...); return@collect // empty next chapter — skip, don't error the feed }` — loadedChapterUrls unchanged, no effect emitted. Lines 513-524: tail/next derivation from loadedChapterUrls means the same `next` is recomputed every time.
suggestedFix: On an empty append, emit ReaderEffect.ShowError (or a dedicated 'chapter has no pages' effect) and either record the chapter as skipped (so the next append targets tailIdx+2) or leave the boundary card in a visible error state — at minimum stop re-marking tailUrl read on every retrigger.
verifierNote: ReaderViewModel.kt:545-548 skips an empty append without recording it in loadedChapterUrls and without any effect; onAppendNextChapter (514-528) re-derives the same next from loadedChapterUrls.lastOrNull() and re-fires markChapterRead(tailUrl) on every retrigger, so the empty chapter is retried forever and later chapters are unreachable via the append path. Minor is right: explicit chapter selection / paged-mode next still works around it.

title: Append-path failures never auto-route Cloudflare challenges to the WebView solver — continuous-mode reading dead-ends with a snackbar
detail: runFetch's Failure branch implements the bounded 403/429/503/52x -> SolveCloudflareChallenge auto-recovery (GAP-RDR-01), but appendChapterPages' Failure branch only emits ReaderEffect.ShowError. In the continuous reader (WEBTOON/CONTINUOUS_VERTICAL), advancing chapters goes through the append path, so a Cloudflare-walled next chapter surfaces as a generic error snackbar on every scroll-to-end instead of the documented auto-solve round-trip. The user's only recovery is to switch to a paged mode or use the scrubber's next-chapter button (which routes through runFetch). This is the same recovery asymmetry GAP-RDR-01 closed between Details and Reader, re-opened between the reader's own replace and append paths.
evidence: Lines 570-573: `is AppResult.Failure -> { FlowLog.log(...); emit(ReaderEffect.ShowError(result.error)) }` — no CHALLENGE_STATUSES check, vs runFetch lines 716-733 which gate on `error is AppError.Network.Http && error.statusCode in CHALLENGE_STATUSES && cloudflareAttempts < MAX_CLOUDFLARE_ATTEMPTS`.
suggestedFix: Apply the same CHALLENGE_STATUSES + cloudflareAttempts gate in appendChapterPages' Failure branch and emit ReaderEffect.SolveCloudflareChallenge(next.url, manga.api) so the route adapter's solve-and-retry loop also covers continuous-mode chapter advances.
verifierNote: Claim verified: appendChapterPages Failure branch (ReaderViewModel.kt:570-573) emits only ShowError, vs runFetch's CHALLENGE_STATUSES gate (716-733). fixSafety corrected to risky: the solve-and-return loop (ChapterImagesReworkScreenRoute.kt:104-108, 196-210) re-dispatches OnRetry, which runs runFetch on the ANCHOR chapter and replaces the whole feed (loadedChapterUrls reset to one chapter) — the suggested fix triggers a disruptive feed reset it does not address, so it is a behavior change needing design.

title: Reader Cloudflare auto-route has no WebView-capability gate — macOS users are auto-navigated (up to 2x) into a dead WebView screen
detail: Same issue already confirmed for DetailsViewModel (Cloudflare-solver auto-routing has no WebView-capability gate), present independently in the Reader: on a 403/429/503/52x failure the VM unconditionally emits SolveCloudflareChallenge, and the route adapter navigates to Screen.WebView. On macOS Desktop KCEF is hard-skipped and the WebView screen shows an infinite loading spinner (separately confirmed finding), so a reader hitting a CF-walled source on macOS is bounced into a dead screen up to MAX_CLOUDFLARE_ATTEMPTS (2) times before finally seeing the error.
evidence: Lines 716-728: `if (error is AppError.Network.Http && error.statusCode in CHALLENGE_STATUSES && cloudflareAttempts < MAX_CLOUDFLARE_ATTEMPTS) { cloudflareAttempts++; emit(ReaderEffect.SolveCloudflareChallenge(...)) }` — no platform/WebView-availability check anywhere in the chain (VM, effect, ChapterImagesReworkScreenRoute).
suggestedFix: Gate the auto-route on a WebView-capability flag (e.g. a :platform facade or the existing KcefState) injected at the route-adapter level: when the platform has no working WebView, fall through to the plain ShowError path instead of navigating.
verifierNote: Verified: no capability gate in VM (ReaderViewModel.kt:716-728), effect, or adapter — rememberReaderCloudflareChallengeSolver (ChapterImagesReworkScreenRoute.kt:207-210) navigates unconditionally; Main.kt:162-187 hard-skips KCEF.init on macOS so KcefState.initialized stays false forever and the WebView screen renders only its placeholder. The accepted platform gap is the missing WebView, not auto-routing users into it twice; same class as the confirmed DetailsViewModel finding (not in this batch).

title: Bookmark observer collects a Room-backed flow with a bare viewModelScope.launch and no .catch (collector twin of the #29 writes finding)
detail: The already-confirmed ReaderViewModel finding covers fire-and-forget Room WRITES escaping the MVI safety net; the read-side collector has the same hole and would be missed by a fix that only wraps the writes: runObserveBookmark launches `observeChapterBookmark(chapterUrl).collect { ... }` in a bare viewModelScope.launch. The backing flow (ChapterBookmarkRepositoryImpl.observeBookmark) starts with a suspend Room query (chapterDao.getChapterIdByUrl) and then a Room flow — either can throw (DB closing/corruption), and MviViewModel's submit() try/catch does not cover coroutines launched inside handlers (its own KDoc says to use launchSafely for exactly this). A throw here crashes the process. HistoryViewModel got the #17 crash-safety .catch for the identical Room-flow-collector posture; the Reader's bookmark observer (and the init reading-mode collector at line 312, lower risk since settings-backed) did not.
evidence: Lines 457-462: `bookmarkJob = viewModelScope.launch { observeChapterBookmark(chapterUrl).collect { ... } }` — no catch, not launchSafely. MviViewModel.kt:151-156 documents that bare nested launches escape the submit() safety net.
suggestedFix: Use launchSafely (or append .catch logging) for the bookmark observer launched in runObserveBookmark, matching the #17 fix applied to HistoryViewModel.
verifierNote: ReaderViewModel.kt:457-462 is a bare viewModelScope.launch collecting a Room-backed flow (ChapterBookmarkRepositoryImpl.kt:42-49 starts with a suspend DAO query); MviViewModel.kt:148-158 KDoc explicitly warns that bare nested launches escape submit()'s safety net and provides launchSafely; HistoryViewModel.kt:121/130 got the .catch/launchSafely #17/#29 treatment for the identical posture. Distinct from the writes-side finding as claimed. Minor (rare trigger: DB closing/corruption), consistent with sibling crash-safety findings.

title: observeBookmark completes after a single false when the chapter row doesn't exist — bookmark state never re-binds if the row appears later
detail: Same flow-completes-instead-of-observing pattern already confirmed for SavedMangaDetailsRepositoryImpl.observeSavedDetails, here in the bookmark stream the Reader keeps collecting for the whole chapter session: observeBookmark resolves the chapter id ONCE; when getChapterIdByUrl returns null it emits `false` and the flow COMPLETES. If the saved_chapters row is created after the observer attached (manga saved to library / chapters persisted mid-session), the Reader's star stays permanently un-bookmarkable-looking: toggleBookmark succeeds (returns true, row now exists) but the dead observer never delivers the new state, contradicting the VM's design comment that 'the per-chapter observe collector re-emits with the new value'. ReaderViewModel's KDoc also claims the backing flow projects distinctUntilChanged — it does not (plain .map).
evidence: Lines 42-49: `override fun observeBookmark(chapterUrl: String): Flow<Boolean> = flow { val chapterId = chapterDao.getChapterIdByUrl(chapterUrl); if (chapterId == null) { emit(false) } else { emitAll(chapterDao.getChapterById(chapterId).map { it?.isBookmarked == true }) } }` — null branch emits once and the flow builder returns.
suggestedFix: Make the stream membership-reactive: observe a Room flow keyed on the URL (e.g. a `SELECT isBookmarked FROM saved_chapters WHERE url = ?` flow that emits null/false when absent and re-emits when the row is inserted), or re-resolve the id reactively as the saved-details fix will for the sibling finding.
verifierNote: ChapterBookmarkRepositoryImpl.kt:42-49: null chapterId emits false once and the flow builder returns (completes) — a row created later never re-binds, while the Reader keeps the dead collector for the whole chapter session and toggleBookmark (51-55) succeeds without the star updating. Both cited KDoc contradictions verified: ReaderViewModel.kt:455-456 claims a distinctUntilChanged backing projection (impl is plain .map) and the toggle comment relies on the observer re-emitting.

title: clearExtractedPages launches unguarded DAO reads on the app-lifetime cleanupScope — a DB throw is an uncaught coroutine exception (process crash)
detail: cleanupScope is `CoroutineScope(SupervisorJob() + dispatchers.io)` with no CoroutineExceptionHandler. clearExtractedPages launches two Room reads (getChapterIdByUrl, getChapterByIdSuspend) plus filesystem cleanup on it, fire-and-forget. The method is explicitly designed to be called from ReaderViewModel.onCleared() — i.e. during teardown, including app shutdown, exactly when the Room database may be closing — and a throw from either DAO call is unhandled: with a SupervisorJob and no handler it reaches the platform default handler and crashes on Android/iOS. The cbzReader.cleanupExtractedCache half catches internally; the DAO half does not.
evidence: Lines 92-95 scope construction; lines 211-215: `cleanupScope.launch { val chapterId = chapterDao.getChapterIdByUrl(chapter.url) ?: return@launch; val entity = chapterDao.getChapterByIdSuspend(chapterId) ?: return@launch; cbzReader.cleanupExtractedCache(...) }` — no try/catch, no exception handler on the scope.
suggestedFix: Wrap the launch body in runCatching (logging non-CancellationException failures) or add a logging CoroutineExceptionHandler to cleanupScope — best-effort cleanup must never crash the process.
verifierNote: ChapterPagesRepositoryImpl.kt:95 builds cleanupScope as SupervisorJob()+io with no CoroutineExceptionHandler; lines 211-215 launch two unguarded DAO reads on it, and the method is invoked from ReaderViewModel.onEnter/onCleared teardown paths (ReaderViewModel.kt:387). An uncaught throw reaches the platform default handler: process kill on Android/iOS (Desktop JVM only kills the thread). Wrap-in-runCatching fix is contained and behavior-preserving.

title: Stale KDoc: claims home/more/featured are 'each preceded by initSite() + getBaseUrl()' — only fetchHome calls initSite
detail: The 'Legacy method binding' KDoc states the three feed verbs are 'each preceded by initSite() + getBaseUrl() exactly as MangaViewModel.startHomeFetch / getMoreManga / getPopularManga do'. In the code only fetchHome calls repo.initSite(); fetchMore and fetchFeatured do not (fetchFeatured calls getBaseUrl only). That actually matches native (native's getPopularManga/getMoreManga also skip initSite — only startHomeFetch calls it), so the behavior is parity-correct, but the doc misdescribes both this implementation and the cited legacy reference, and could mislead a maintainer into 'restoring' initSite calls or assuming header hydration happens on the featured path.
