title: Paged modes auto-advance the chapter on ARRIVAL at the last page — the final page of every chapter is yanked away before it can be read
detail: Both pagers' end-of-chapter watchers fire onReachedEnd() when `page == pages.lastIndex && previous < page` — i.e. the moment the pager settles ON the last image after coming from a lower index (ReaderHorizontalPager L1647-1657, ReaderVerticalPager L1736-1746). For paged modes onReachedEnd dispatches ReaderIntent.OnNextChapter (L655-660), whose handler marks the chapter read and runs onEnter() for the next chapter, which synchronously clears `pages` — so the last page is replaced by the loading spinner within tens of milliseconds of appearing. Native is one swipe later: its ViewModel appends a ReaderItem.NextChapterOverlay AFTER each chapter's images (native ReaderViewModel.kt:203-214), so `allReaderItems.lastIndex` is the overlay card, not the final image, and the auto-advance (native ReaderScreen.kt:256-266) only fires after the user has read the last image and swiped once more. The rework's own comment even acknowledges this ('Native keeps a NextChapter overlay item inside the pager so its lastIndex is never the final image') and claims to fire 'only on a real swipe-PAST-the-last-page', but the implemented condition is arrival-at-last-page. Consequences: (a) users cannot dwell on or read the final page of any non-terminal chapter in the 4 paged modes — including DEFAULT, the default mode; (b) dragging the bottom scrubber to the end instantly skips the chapter (scrubber -> OnPageChanged(last) -> jump-loop scrollToPage(last) -> transition fires) and marks it read; (c) the NextChapterOverlay banner with its tap-to-advance affordance and loading spinner only ever flashes, defeating its design; (d) it defeats the VM's deliberate mark-read posture ('never on merely landing on the last image page' — ReaderViewModel.onPageChanged comment) because landing on the last page is converted into an advance.
evidence: ReaderScreen.kt L1647-1657: `LaunchedEffect(pagerState, pages.size) { ... snapshotFlow { pagerState.currentPage }.collect { page -> if (page == pages.lastIndex && previous < page) { onReachedEnd() } ... } }` + L655-659: `onReachedEnd = { onIntent(if (state.readingMode.isPaged) ReaderIntent.OnNextChapter else ...) }`. Native parity spec: ReaderItem.NextChapterOverlay appended after the images (native ReaderViewModel.kt:207-214); advance gate `pagerState.currentPage == allReaderItems.lastIndex` (native ReaderScreen.kt:257-266) only reachable one swipe past the last image.
suggestedFix: Restore the native one-extra-swipe semantics: append a terminal feed item to the paged layouts (mirror the continuous modes' NextChapterBoundaryCard — pageCount = pages.size + 1, last page renders NextChapterContent) and fire OnNextChapter only when the pager settles on that extra page; alternatively keep page count unchanged and require an explicit overscroll/tap on the existing NextChapterOverlay instead of auto-firing on arrival at lastIndex.
verifierNote: Claim fully confirmed: both pagers fire onReachedEnd on TRANSITION INTO pages.lastIndex (ReaderScreen.kt:1652, :1741 'page == pages.lastIndex && previous < page'), :ui routes paged modes to OnNextChapter (:655-659), and ReaderViewModel.onNextChapter→onEnter synchronously clears pages (ReaderViewModel.kt:415-435) — so the final page is yanked on arrival; the scrubber-jump path and the flash-only NextChapterOverlay also check out. Native parity verified: native appends ReaderItem.NextChapterOverlay after the images (native ReaderViewModel.kt:207-215) and advances only at allReaderItems.lastIndex (native ReaderScreen.kt:257-265), i.e. one swipe past the last image; the rework comment's 'swipe-PAST' intent contradicts its own implementation (not an owner-sanctioned divergence — the L652 owner-choice comment covers the clear-and-jump mechanism, not the trigger timing). Severity recalibrated critical→major per the rubric: severe user-visible incorrectness, but no crash/data-loss/security.

title: After Next/Prev chapter navigation, any composition restart (rotation, return from WebView) re-dispatches OnEnter with the stale nav-args chapter and resets the reader to the originally-opened chapter
detail: ReaderScreenContent dispatches `OnEnter(manga, chapter)` from `LaunchedEffect(manga.api, manga.language, manga.title, chapter.url)` where `manga`/`chapter` are reconstructed from static nav args in ChapterImagesReworkScreenRoute (L110-129). The ReaderViewModel is koinViewModel()-scoped to the NavBackStackEntry, so it survives (a) device rotation — MainActivity declares no android:configChanges, so the activity and composition are recreated — and (b) being covered by another destination (the Cloudflare-solve WebView via SolveCloudflareChallenge, or the per-page 'Open in WebView' Screen.WebView push). In both cases the reader composable re-enters composition and the LaunchedEffect runs again with the ANCHOR chapter from nav args. If the user has meanwhile navigated chapters via the prev/next pills or OnNextChapter auto-advance (VM state.chapter = chapterN != anchor), the OnEnter identity guard (`current.chapter?.url == chapter.url`, ReaderViewModel.kt:382) does NOT match, so onEnter() runs fully: pages cleared, appended feed reset, and the ANCHOR chapter is re-fetched — the user is silently yanked back to the chapter they originally opened, losing their reading position. The OnEnter KDoc ('a config change does NOT re-trigger the network fetch') only holds while no chapter navigation has occurred. Realistic triggers: rotate the device after advancing a chapter; hit a Cloudflare 403 mid-chapter-N (the auto-solve navigates to the WebView and back); tap 'Open in WebView' on a failed page after advancing.
evidence: ReaderScreen.kt L420-422 keys OnEnter on nav-args identity only; ChapterImagesReworkScreenRoute.kt L110-129 rebuilds Manga/Chapter from `backStackEntry.toRoute<Screen.ChapterImagesRework>()`; ReaderViewModel.kt L380-382: `if (current.manga?.matches(manga) == true && current.chapter?.url == chapter.url) return` — false after Next/Prev, so the full reset branch runs. app/src/main/AndroidManifest.xml MainActivity entry has no configChanges attribute.
suggestedFix: Make the intent-level OnEnter initialize-once per VM instance: in ReaderViewModel.handle, ignore OnEnter when `state.value.chapter != null` (VM-internal onEnter calls from onNextChapter/onPrevChapter bypass the intent path, and each push of the route gets a fresh entry-scoped VM, so a second intent-level OnEnter with different args can only be a stale re-composition). Process-death restore still works: a fresh VM has chapter == null and proceeds.
verifierNote: Traced: ReaderScreen.kt:420-422 re-dispatches OnEnter(navArgs) on every re-entry into composition (rotation — MainActivity has no configChanges in app/src/main/AndroidManifest.xml; pop-back from Screen.WebView / CF solver re-composes the route), VM survives via NavBackStackEntry scope, and the guard at ReaderViewModel.kt:382 fails after Next/Prev (chapter.url != anchor) so onEnter() fully resets to the anchor chapter. Fix is a VM behavior change → risky; CF retry uses OnRetry (ChapterImagesReworkScreenRoute.kt:107) so the initialize-once fix wouldn't break it.

title: Scrolling up across an appended-chapter boundary in WEBTOON/CONTINUOUS_VERTICAL teleports the list: boundary rows break the scrubber jump-loop's 'positions already match' guard
detail: buildReaderFeed maps a Boundary row's feedToPage entry to the FINISHED chapter's last page index p (ReaderFeedItem.kt:77-78), while pageToFeed[p] is the feed index of that page's Image row (one above the boundary). The jump-loop `LaunchedEffect(currentPageIndex)` guard compares feed indices: `if (listState.firstVisibleItemIndex != target) listState.scrollToItem(target)` (L1465-1471). When the user scrolls UP from an appended chapter and the full-screen-height boundary card becomes the first visible item, the snapshotFlow dispatches OnPageChanged(p) (feedToPage alias), currentPageIndex changes from p+1 to p, the jump-loop relaunches, and firstVisibleItemIndex (the boundary, b) != pageToFeed[p] (b-1) — so scrollToItem(b-1) fires: it cancels the user's fling (both run at MutatePriority.Default) and instantly snaps the viewport up by a full page-image height, skipping the boundary card entirely. The comment's assumption that 'the if-guard makes scroll-driven updates a no-op (positions already match)' is false exactly at boundary rows because feedToPage/pageToFeed are not inverse there. Downward crossings are safe (currentPageIndex is already p when the boundary becomes top-visible). During a finger-down drag the programmatic scroll is rejected by the higher-priority user mutation, so the symptom appears on flings and on settle — a jarring jump every time the user flings back across a chapter boundary in continuous reading.
evidence: ReaderFeedItem.kt L77-78: boundary `feedToPage.add(i)` aliases to the previous image's page index; ReaderScreen.kt L1465-1471: `LaunchedEffect(currentPageIndex) { val target = feed.pageToFeed.getOrNull(...) ...; if (listState.firstVisibleItemIndex != target) { listState.scrollToItem(target) } }` — with boundary b top-visible, target = b-1 != b.
suggestedFix: Compare in page space instead of feed space before scrolling: skip the scrollToItem when `feed.feedToPage.getOrNull(listState.firstVisibleItemIndex) == currentPageIndex` (the first visible row already represents the current page, boundary aliases included). Keep the feed-space comparison only as the actual scroll target.
verifierNote: Verified: ReaderFeedItem.kt:78 makes feedToPage[boundary b] = p while pageToFeed[p] = b-1, so when the boundary becomes top-visible on an upward fling, OnPageChanged(p) fires (ReaderScreen.kt:1458), currentPageIndex changes, and the jump-loop at L1465-1470 sees firstVisibleItemIndex (b) != target (b-1) → scrollToItem cancels the Default-priority fling and snaps a full image height. Downward crossings emit the already-current page (state value unchanged → no relaunch), so only up-crossings jump. Page-space guard fix compiles and preserves scrubber jumps.

title: Seekbar chapter pills are swapped relative to native: native puts NEXT chapter on the first (left) pill and PREVIOUS on the last, the rework reversed them
detail: Native SeekBarContainer.kt places the NEXT-chapter action on the FIRST pill in the Row (L50-62: `IconButton(enabled = hasNext, onClick = onNext)` with the `ic_previous` left-chevron glyph) and the PREVIOUS-chapter action on the LAST pill (L114-129: `onClick = onPrevious`) — i.e. left = forward, matching the right-to-left manga reading flow this Arabic-first app uses. The rework's ReaderPageScrubber puts Prev first (L1216-1224, YamiIcons.PrevChapter/NavigateBefore) and Next last (L1263-1271), despite the component KDoc claiming a 'faithful port of native SeekBarContainer'. The rework is self-consistent (icons match actions), but for users migrating from the native app the chapter-step buttons act in the opposite direction — tapping the left pill now goes BACK a chapter instead of forward. Given the campaign's 100% behavior-parity goal this is a deliberate-looking but undocumented divergence that needs an owner decision (keep logical LTR order, or restore native's left=next).
evidence: native SeekBarContainer.kt L50-52: first pill `IconButton(enabled = hasNext, onClick = onNext, ...)`; L114-117: last pill `IconButton(enabled = hasPrevious, onClick = onPrevious)`. Rework ReaderScreen.kt L1216-1224 first pill = onPrevChapter, L1263-1271 last pill = onNextChapter.
suggestedFix: Owner decision: either restore native's ordering (first pill = next chapter, last pill = previous) or document the intentional divergence in the component KDoc and parity tracker so it stops reading as a faithful port.
verifierNote: Verified against native SeekBarContainer.kt:50-52 (first pill IconButton(enabled=hasNext, onClick=onNext) with ic_previous glyph) + L114-117 (last pill onPrevious), wired to chapter nav in native ReaderScreen.kt:549-585; rework ReaderScreen.kt:1216-1224/1263-1271 puts Prev first, Next last despite the 'faithful port' KDoc at L1162. Real undocumented divergence from native ordering; fix needs owner decision → risky.

title: Reader top bar lives in the Scaffold topBar slot, so every chrome toggle (including the 3s auto-hide) resizes the page viewport and the 0.8-alpha translucency never shows the page beneath it
detail: Native overlays ControlOverlay INSIDE the same Box as the reading-mode layouts, so the page renders edge-to-edge under the translucent (background @ 0.8 alpha) bar and showing/hiding chrome never moves the page. The rework instead hosts ReaderTopBar in Scaffold's topBar slot (L524-563) wrapped in AnimatedVisibility; the content area is padded by the bar height (L576-579 `.padding(padding)`), so: (a) every tap-toggle and every 3-second auto-hide (L464-469) animates the whole page area up/down by the bar height — in webtoon/continuous modes this shifts the reading position the user's eyes are anchored on, and it also changes BoxWithConstraints.maxHeight (screenHeightDb), resizing loading placeholders and the full-viewport boundary cards mid-read; (b) the deliberately ported translucent containerColor (`background.copy(alpha = 0.8f)`, L856-858, 'so the page shows faintly through the bar') is ineffective — the page is laid out BELOW the bar, so the translucency only reveals the scaffold background, not the page. The bottom chrome stack already does this correctly (an Alignment.BottomCenter overlay inside the page Box).
evidence: ReaderScreen.kt L524-563 (topBar slot + AnimatedVisibility), L576-579 (`BoxWithConstraints(modifier = Modifier.fillMaxSize().padding(padding)...)`), L856-858 (translucent containerColor comment claims the page shows through). Native ReaderScreen.kt L359-615: reading modes and ControlOverlay are siblings in one Box — chrome floats over the page.
suggestedFix: Move the top bar out of the Scaffold slot and render it as a top-aligned overlay inside the page BoxWithConstraints (same pattern as the bottom chrome stack), keeping the page area at a constant size and making the translucent bar actually overlay the page.
verifierNote: Verified: ReaderTopBar lives in Scaffold topBar slot inside AnimatedVisibility (ReaderScreen.kt:524-563) and the page BoxWithConstraints is padded by it (L576-579), so every toggle/auto-hide (L464-469) resizes the viewport and changes screenHeightDb, while the 0.8-alpha containerColor (L856-858) only reveals the scaffold background, not the page. Bottom chrome is correctly an Alignment.BottomCenter overlay inside the same Box (L731-737). Layout restructure → risky.

title: OnNextChapter/OnPrevChapter lack the isLoading re-entrance guard their intent KDoc documents — rapid double-dispatch can skip a chapter
detail: ReaderIntent.OnNextChapter's KDoc states 'Re-entrance guard: dropped when state.isLoading == true (initial fetch in progress) or when !state.canGoNext' (ReaderIntent.kt:146-149). The implementation only checks canGoNext (ReaderViewModel.kt:465-481; onPrevChapter likewise L483-496) — there is no isLoading drop. Because each submit() runs in its own coroutine and onEnter recomputes state quickly, a second OnNextChapter arriving while chapter N+1 is still loading (double-tap on the next pill, or a user tap on the NextChapterOverlay racing the paged auto-advance) sees state.chapter == N+1, canGoNext true, and advances again to N+2 — skipping a chapter the user never saw, and marking N+1 read via markChapterRead. The documented isLoading guard would drop the second dispatch.
evidence: ReaderViewModel.kt L465-468: `private suspend fun onNextChapter() { val current = state.value; if (!current.canGoNext) return; ... }` — no isLoading check, contradicting ReaderIntent.kt L146-149 ('dropped when state.isLoading == true').
suggestedFix: Add `if (current.isLoading) return` at the top of onNextChapter()/onPrevChapter() to match the documented contract (or update the KDoc if the guard is intentionally absent — but the guard also closes the real double-advance race, so adding it is preferable).
verifierNote: Verified: ReaderIntent.kt:146-149 documents an isLoading drop that ReaderViewModel.kt:465-467/483-485 never implements (only canGoNext/canGoPrev), and ReaderState.kt:312-313 derives canGoNext purely from chapters indices (no isLoading term), so a second OnNextChapter landing after onEnter's state swap but during the N+1 fetch advances to N+2 and marks N+1 read. Adding the documented guard is a small, contract-matching change.

title: Horizontal reading modes invert under RTL layout (Arabic UI): RIGHT_TO_LEFT pages left-to-right and vice versa
detail: HorizontalPager's reverseLayout is relative to LocalLayoutDirection, and the app root (App.kt:424-431) provides LayoutDirection.Rtl whenever Arabic is the app/device locale. The reader never pins a layout direction around its pager, so under an Arabic UI the two horizontal modes are functionally swapped: ReadingMode.RIGHT_TO_LEFT (reverseLayout=true, line 1339) gets double-mirrored into left-to-right paging, and ReadingMode.LEFT_TO_RIGHT (reverseLayout=false) pages right-to-left. The mode labels in ReadingModeDialog and Settings therefore describe the opposite of what happens for the app's largest (Arabic) audience. Native has the same code shape (HorizontalReadingMode.kt reverseLayout + supportsRtl=true), so this matches native — but it is harmful per the ground rules: a core-reading-flow control does the opposite of its label for the primary locale. Every other manga reader pins the pager to Ltr and expresses direction purely via reverseLayout.
evidence: ReaderPageLayout: `ReadingMode.RIGHT_TO_LEFT -> ReaderHorizontalPager(..., reverseLayout = true, ...)`; ReaderHorizontalPager: `HorizontalPager(state = pagerState, reverseLayout = reverseLayout, ...)` with no CompositionLocalProvider(LocalLayoutDirection provides LayoutDirection.Ltr) anywhere in the reader. App.kt: `isRtlLanguageTag(appLanguage) -> LayoutDirection.Rtl` provided app-wide (and on Android an Arabic device locale yields Rtl even with no in-app pick). In RTL + reverseLayout=true the pager lays page 0 at the left edge (LTR reading); in RTL + reverseLayout=false it reads right-to-left.
suggestedFix: Wrap the reader's HorizontalPager (or the whole ReaderPageLayout horizontal branch) in CompositionLocalProvider(LocalLayoutDirection provides LayoutDirection.Ltr) { ... } so reverseLayout=true always means manga-style right-to-left regardless of UI locale. Note this intentionally diverges from (and fixes) native's behavior — owner sign-off needed; the page scrubber Slider can stay in the ambient direction.
verifierNote: Mechanics confirmed (reverseLayout is LocalLayoutDirection-relative; App.kt:424-431 provides Rtl for Arabic; no direction pin anywhere in ReaderScreen.kt), but native has the identical shape (native ReaderScreen.kt:435 reverseLayout=(mode==RIGHT_TO_LEFT) + supportsRtl=true in its manifest), so Arabic users see exactly the native behavior — per the APP_MAP parity rule this is a label-vs-behavior defect inherited from native, both directions stay reachable via the swapped labels. Downgraded major→minor; fixing it deliberately diverges from native → risky, owner sign-off.

title: iOS: layout direction flips immediately on language pick while strings only change after relaunch — mixed RTL-layout/LTR-text session
detail: The root layoutDirection override is derived in common code from the persisted appLanguage and applies on all platforms instantly. But on iOS isLiveLocaleSwitchSupported=false: compose-resources keeps resolving the old NSLocale until the app is relaunched (LocalAppLocale.ios only writes AppleLanguages for the next launch, and the Language screen shows a restart hint). So picking Arabic on iOS mirrors the whole UI to RTL immediately while every string stays English for the rest of the session; switching from Arabic back to English yields Arabic text in an LTR layout. The direction flip and the language flip are out of sync for the entire session on the one platform where the switch is not live.
evidence: App.kt: `isRtlLanguageTag(appLanguage) -> LayoutDirection.Rtl` (no platform gating) vs LocalAppLocale.ios.kt: `actual val isLiveLocaleSwitchSupported: Boolean = false` and the comment 'iOS does NOT re-resolve compose-resources strings in-session'. LanguageScreenRoute passes `restartHintVisible = !LocalAppLocale.isLiveLocaleSwitchSupported`, confirming strings are known not to switch live on iOS.
suggestedFix: Gate the explicit-selection direction override on LocalAppLocale.isLiveLocaleSwitchSupported (keep the platform's current direction when the locale can't move mid-session, so direction and strings flip together on next launch), e.g. `appLanguage.isBlank() || !LocalAppLocale.isLiveLocaleSwitchSupported -> LocalLayoutDirection.current`. On iOS after relaunch the persisted Arabic pick still resolves to Rtl via the same branch.
verifierNote: Verified: App.kt:424-431 flips LocalLayoutDirection instantly from the persisted pick on all platforms, while LocalAppLocale.ios.kt:62-66 (isLiveLocaleSwitchSupported=false) only writes AppleLanguages for the next launch — so an iOS session runs RTL layout with old-language strings until relaunch (restart hint confirmed in LanguageScreenRoute.kt:200). Gating fix changes direction behavior on iOS and its post-relaunch ambient-direction assumption is unproven → risky.

title: Two remaining non-AutoMirrored directional glyphs bypass the RTL-clean YamiIcons set (Outlined.List, Filled.PlaylistAddCheck)

title: Numeric stringResource args render Latin digits in the Arabic UI where native renders Arabic-Indic digits (systemic compose-resources divergence)
detail: compose-resources interpolates format args with plain toString() (positional %1$d replacement, no locale digit shaping), so every numeric template in the Arabic UI renders Western digits: 'منذ 3 أيام' (days_ago/weeks_ago/months_ago/years_ago in History rows and group headers, Library 'last updated' and items-count header, Details date template, Statistics h_m duration, downloads counts). Native resolves the same values-ar templates through Context.getString → java.util.Formatter under the ar default locale, which emits Arabic-Indic digits ('منذ ٣ أيام'). The campaign already fixed the same class of divergence for thousands-grouping (StatisticsScreen formatCount GAP-STAT-01 routes through a locale-aware platform formatter precisely because '%,d is LOCALE-AWARE — Arabic-Indic digits'), but every other numeric placeholder still bypasses that. This is a visible native-parity divergence on most list rows for the primary locale, not just cosmetics-by-choice.
evidence: HistoryScreen.kt:387/403-406 `stringResource(Res.string.days_ago, days.toInt())` etc.; values-ar 'منذ %1$d أيام'; compose-resources replaces %1$d with arg.toString() (corroborated by the known-finding that non-positional %d specifiers are no-ops — replacement is regex-based, not Formatter-based). Native HistoryItem.kt:133-136 uses Android stringResource(R.string.days_ago, ...) which localizes digits under ar. StatisticsScreen.kt:459-465 KDoc documents the same divergence class and its fix for grouping.
suggestedFix: Route numeric args through a locale-aware digit formatter before interpolation (e.g. reuse/extend the existing formatGroupedNumber expect/actual, or a formatLocalizedInt helper) at the stringResource call sites that feed the Arabic-visible templates — or record an explicit owner decision that Latin digits are acceptable KMP-wide and note it as accepted divergence in the parity docs.
verifierNote: Claim confirmed: HistoryScreen.kt:387/403-406 (and siblings) interpolate ints via compose-resources' plain positional replacement while native's Context.getString renders Arabic-Indic digits under ar — the project's own StatisticsScreen.kt:461-465 KDoc acknowledges this exact divergence class and fixed it only for %,d grouping. fixSafety corrected report-only→risky: the files are editable (not forbidden paths) and the suggested digit-shaping fix is a cross-screen rendering behavior change needing owner decision.

title: Orphaned setting 'new_sources_added': written true on every app-version bump, but nothing in the KMP app ever reads it or clears it (native used it for the Home 'NEW' sources badge)
detail: checkIfShouldShowWhatsNew() calls ds.setNewSources(true) whenever a new version is detected — the only write site for StorageKeys.NEW_SOURCES ("new_sources_added"). title: ActiveRepoProvider is dead (zero consumers) and its 'repo_enabled_${API}' preference read is orphaned — no code anywhere writes that key; source enablement actually lives in Room sources.isEnabled
detail: ActiveRepoProvider filters the repo set by prefs.getBoolean("repo_enabled_${repo.API}", true) and snapshots prefs.getInt("active_tab", 0) once at construction into never-updated StateFlows. Two problems: (1) the 'repo_enabled_*' keys are read-only orphans — no writer exists in the KMP codebase (the real enable/disable path is SourcesRepositoryImpl.setSourceEnabled → legacy enableDisAbleSource → Room sourcesDao.setEnabledByName, a completely different cell), so the filter always evaluates to the default true; native shares this quirk, but in native the class at least had live consumers. (2) In KMP the class itself is dead: its KDoc-claimed consumer WebViewViewModel no longer takes it (WebViewViewModel.kt:43-45 takes only SourcesRepository), and the only remaining reference is the Koin binding single { ActiveRepoProvider(...) } at SharedModule.kt:285. A maintainer reading 'repo_enabled_*' here could reasonably conclude per-source enablement is prefs-backed and write to the wrong store. The live active-tab/enabled-source state is owned by repo_settings/SourcesRepository (Room + StorageKeys.ACTIVE_TAB), which Home consumes via HomeFeedRepositoryImpl.observeActiveTabIndex.
evidence: Repo-wide grep for 'repo_enabled' → single hit (the read at ActiveRepoProvider.kt:37). Grep for ActiveRepoProvider consumers → only SharedModule.kt:285 binding + KDoc mentions; WebViewViewModel ctor verified to take only SourcesRepository.
suggestedFix: Delete ActiveRepoProvider and its SharedModule binding (no behavior change — nothing resolves it). If kept for a future slice, replace the inert repo_enabled_* prefs filter with the Room-backed enabled state so it cannot drift from the real source-enablement cell.
verifierNote: Verified: 'repo_enabled' appears exactly once in KMP code (ActiveRepoProvider.kt:37, read with default true, no writer anywhere), and ActiveRepoProvider's only references are its own file and the never-resolved lazy single at SharedModule.kt:285 — no consumer injects it, so the class is dead and its prefs-backed filter is misleading next to the real Room-backed isEnabled cell. Deleting a never-resolved lazy binding is behavior-neutral.

title: Piloted sources never hydrate the legacy header cache the Coil interceptor reads — covers on captured-header pilot sources load with no Cookie/UA despite valid saved headers
detail: CoilSourceHeaderInterceptor sources its headers exclusively from the matched legacy repo's in-memory `defaultHeaders` (`val headers = match.defaultHeaders; if (headers.isEmpty()) return chain.proceed()`). For the 12 piloted sources, every feed/search/details/pages fetch is served by GenericSourceClient, which reads captured headers directly from DataStoreHeaderStore per request — and the :data pilot branches return BEFORE the legacy hydration runs (HomeFeedRepositoryImpl.kt:131-139 hits `sourceRegistry.get(...)` and returns before the `repo.initSite()` on line 139; the legacy `LegacyKotlinSourceClient.home()` fallback that does call `repo.initSite()` only executes when the generic primary FAILS). Piloted legacy repos like MangaLekRepositoryv2 (line 364-365) and TeamXRepositoryv2 (line 110-111) implement `defaultHeaders get() = _cachedHeaders ?: emptyMap()`, hydrated only inside `initSite()`/`refreshHeaders()`. Net effect after a cold start with previously-captured Cloudflare headers: the generic engine sends the saved Cookie+User-Agent and the FEED succeeds, but the legacy repo's `_cachedHeaders` stays null all session, so the interceptor finds an EMPTY map and skips injection — every plain-URL image load (Home grid covers, search-result covers, details cover; HomeReworkScreenRoute.kt:62-70 explicitly documents that Home covers rely solely on this interceptor because the :ui cover slot coerces to String) goes out with no Cookie and no User-Agent. On the captured-header pilots that are Cloudflare-gated (Lekmanga, Team X, 3asq, DilarV2 — exactly the sources whose `usesCapturedHeaders: true` exists because bare requests 403), covers 403 even though the user already solved the challenge — the documented Bug-4-layer-3 recovery silently regressed for piloted sources. Library covers escape only because LibraryScreenRoute uses rememberSourceImageRequest(url, api), which calls ensureSiteInitialized() itself.
evidence: App.kt:300-303 `val headers = match.defaultHeaders / if (headers.isEmpty()) { return chain.proceed() }`; HomeFeedRepositoryImpl.kt:131-137 `if (sourceRegistry.isPiloted(repo.API)) { sourceRegistry.get(repo.API)?.let { ... return@withContext result } }` precedes `repo.initSite()`; MangaLekRepositoryv2.kt:364-365 `override val defaultHeaders get() = _cachedHeaders ?: emptyMap()`; GenericSourceClient.kt:213-214 reads `headerStore.headersFor(config.api)` per request (feed works, proving valid headers exist in the store that images never get).
suggestedFix: In CoilSourceHeaderInterceptor, when `match.defaultHeaders` is empty, fall back to the persisted headers: either call `(match as? BaseManga)?.ensureSiteInitialized()` (intercept is suspend) and re-read defaultHeaders, or inject DataStoreHelper and use `getHeadersForApi(match.API)`. Alternatively (narrower): have the :data pilot branches (HomeFeed/Search/MangaDetails/ChapterPages RepositoryImpl) call `repo.initSite()` before delegating to the registry so the interceptor's source of truth stays hydrated.
verifierNote: All links verified: App.kt:300-303 skips injection on empty defaultHeaders; HomeFeedRepositoryImpl.kt:131-137 pilot branch returns before repo.initSite(); MangaLekRepositoryv2.kt:362-365 defaultHeaders = _cachedHeaders ?: emptyMap(); GenericSourceClient requestHeaders reads headerStore per request so the feed succeeds while legacy stays unhydrated; HomeReworkScreenRoute.kt:91 passes raw coverUrl (interceptor-only) while LibraryScreenRoute.kt:231 escapes via rememberSourceImageRequest's ensureSiteInitialized. 8 of 12 pilots have usesCapturedHeaders=true (BundledSourcesConfig.kt:219-505); only LegacyKotlinSourceClient.kt:44/50 (failure fallback) calls initSite.

title: DataStoreHeaderStore/SourcesGenericModule KDocs claim the generic Azora client reuses captured Cloudflare headers — Azora's config sets usesCapturedHeaders=false (engine KDoc calls Azora 'header-free')
detail: DataStoreHeaderStore's KDoc says wiring the real store 'is what lets the generic engine reuse headers a user already captured for a Cloudflare-gated source like Azora, so the generic path can actually succeed live', and SourcesGenericModule.kt:42 repeats 'The real [DataStoreHeaderStore] lets the generic Azora client reuse captured Cloudflare headers.' But the shipped pilot config sets `"usesCapturedHeaders": false` for Azora (BundledSourcesConfig.kt:45), and GenericSourceClient.requestHeaders' KDoc (GenericSourceClient.kt:208-211) documents the opposite: 'A header-free source (e.g. Azora) skips the header-store read entirely.' So the generic Azora client never reads the store. A maintainer debugging an Azora Cloudflare wall would be told by two KDocs that captured headers are replayed when they are not (only the legacy fallback path replays them via AzoraRepositoryv2.initSite). One of the two stories is stale — most likely the store/module KDocs, which predate the per-source usesCapturedHeaders flag.
evidence: DataStoreHeaderStore.kt:7-11 'Wiring this ... is what lets the generic engine reuse headers a user already captured for a Cloudflare-gated source like Azora'; BundledSourcesConfig.kt:39-45 '"api": "Azora" ... "usesCapturedHeaders": false'; GenericSourceClient.kt:209-211 'A header-free source (e.g. Azora) skips the header-store read entirely'.
suggestedFix: Reword the DataStoreHeaderStore and SourcesGenericModule KDocs to cite a source that actually has usesCapturedHeaders=true (e.g. Lekmanga, Team X, 3asq, DilarV2), or note that Azora's generic descriptor deliberately opts out of captured headers. If Azora's API host is in fact Cloudflare-gated, flipping its usesCapturedHeaders to true is the behavioral alternative (owner decision).
verifierNote: DataStoreHeaderStore.kt:7-11 and SourcesGenericModule.kt:42 both cite Azora as the captured-header beneficiary, but BundledSourcesConfig.kt:45 sets Azora usesCapturedHeaders=false and GenericSourceClient's requestHeaders KDoc explicitly calls Azora 'header-free' — the generic Azora client never reads the store. Doc-only contradiction, suggested reword is safe.

title: Admin (and iOS/Desktop user) complaint mutations misreport every transient fetch failure as 'Complaint <id> not found'
detail: All four admin mutations (changeStatus / addClosureReason / editComplaint via fetchLegacyById -> legacyGetAll()) depend on a re-fetch whose underlying implementations NEVER throw on failure: ComplaintFirestoreDataSource.getAllComplaints (androidMain, lines 152-155) and ComplaintFirestoreRestDataSource.getAllComplaints (lines 107-110) both catch everything and coerce to emptyList(). So on any network failure / Firestore outage, fetchLegacyById gets an empty list and throws IllegalStateException("Complaint <id> not found") — which the AdminComplaintViewModel.completeAction renders verbatim in the snackbar. The admin is told the complaint no longer exists when in fact the network blipped (and cannot distinguish that from a genuine concurrent delete). The same misdiagnosis hits the user-side edit/reply path on iOS/Desktop (ComplaintActionRepositoryImpl.fetchLegacyById:129-131 over the REST getComplaintsByUser, which also coerces failures to emptyList; Android's SDK getComplaintsByUser throws properly so Android user-side is correct). This is not native parity: the native AdminComplaintViewModel mutates the in-memory complaint object directly (complaint.copy(...)) and never re-fetches, so the re-fetch failure mode is a KMP-introduced regression. Distinct from known finding #350 (empty list state on read screens): even after that read-path fix, this write-path helper still conflates 'fetch failed' with 'document missing'.
evidence: AdminComplaintActionRepositoryImpl.kt:180-182 `legacyGetAll().firstOrNull { it.id == id } ?: error("Complaint $id not found")`; ComplaintFirestoreDataSource.kt:152-155 `catch (e: Exception) { ...; emptyList() }`; ComplaintFirestoreRestDataSource.kt:107-110 `catch (t: Throwable) { ...; emptyList() }`; AdminComplaintViewModel.kt:251-255 surfaces `e.message` verbatim.
suggestedFix: Make the mutation-path re-fetch failure-transparent: either add a throwing fetch (e.g. a getAllComplaintsOrThrow / getComplaintByIdOrThrow on the legacy repository) used by fetchLegacyById in both action repos, or have the existing getAll/getByUser rethrow (fixing known #350 at the source) so 'not found' is only raised when the fetch genuinely succeeded without the document.
verifierNote: AdminComplaintActionRepositoryImpl.kt:180-182 raises error("Complaint $id not found") whenever legacyGetAll() is empty; both fetchers coerce all failures to emptyList (ComplaintFirestoreDataSource.kt:152-155 catch→emptyList, ComplaintFirestoreRestDataSource.kt:97-110 non-2xx and catch→emptyList; REST getComplaintsByUser:122-125 same, hitting the user-side iOS/Desktop path at ComplaintActionRepositoryImpl.kt:129-131). AdminComplaintViewModel.completeAction (251-256) shows e.message verbatim. Not parity: native admin VM mutates complaint.copy(...) in memory with no re-fetch (native AdminComplaintViewModel.kt:74, 162-165).

title: AdminComplaintViewModel.loadList has no in-flight guard or cancel-before-relaunch — concurrent loads race and stale data (incl. statistics) wins
detail: Same defect class as known finding #252 on the user-side ComplaintViewModel, but in the admin VM (different file, not indexed): loadList() launches an unguarded viewModelScope coroutine per call. Retry-button spam (OnRetry) or a post-mutation refire racing a user-initiated retry runs multiple collection-wide fetches concurrently; whichever response lands last overwrites state.all, state.filtered AND state.statistics — potentially with the older snapshot. The house pattern for ordering-sensitive loads is the cancel-before-relaunch Job (see ReaderViewModel per CLAUDE.md).
evidence: AdminComplaintViewModel.kt:259-289 — `private fun loadList() { updateState { ... }; viewModelScope.launch { val result = observeAllComplaints() ... } }` with no Job field, no isLoading short-circuit.
suggestedFix: Add a `private var loadJob: Job? = null` and `loadJob?.cancel(); loadJob = viewModelScope.launch { ... }` in loadList() (mirror whatever fix lands for #252 on the user-side VM).
verifierNote: AdminComplaintViewModel.kt:259-289 — loadList launches an unguarded viewModelScope coroutine (no Job field, no isLoading short-circuit; OnRetry at line 98 and post-mutation refire at line 249 both call it), so concurrent one-shot fetches race and last-writer-wins on all/filtered/statistics. Cancel-before-relaunch is the documented house pattern.

title: Stale KDoc: claims the rework search has 'no id-match', but ComplaintViewModel.applyFilter matches complaint.id
detail: The `id = "admin"` rationale paragraph states: "the rework's search pattern matches subject/body only (no id-match), so this is purely a label-style identifier, not a search hit anchor." The live rework filter does match ids: ComplaintViewModel.applyFilter (line 289) includes `complaint.id.contains(query, ignoreCase = true)` (and the admin VM additionally matches userId). Typing 'admin' in the Feedback Manager search DOES surface the pinned entries by id-match, exactly the legacy behaviour the KDoc says was dropped. title: Download-all re-enqueues every already-downloaded chapter — native filters !isDownloaded, so the whole manga re-downloads over the network
detail: The use case loops details.chapters.forEach with no isDownloaded filter, and its own KDoc ('Already-downloaded chapters are NOT pre-filtered, mirroring ... the legacy behaviour') misstates the native spec: native-app's download-all handler explicitly filters first — LibraryMangaRoute.kt:180 'val notDownloadedChapters = chapters.filter { !it.isDownloaded }' (and again at :220 for the custom-download path) — before calling downloadViewModel.downloadChapters. Because ChapterDownloadDao.insert is OnConflictStrategy.REPLACE against the unique chapterId index, each re-enqueue REPLACEs the SUCCESS row with a fresh QUEUED row (progress 0, sizeBytes 0), so tapping 'Download all' on a manga with hundreds of downloaded chapters (a) moves them all out of the Completed tab back into Active, (b) re-downloads every page of every chapter over the network, overwriting perfectly good files, and (c) on iOS/Desktop additionally aborts any in-flight chapter via the per-page state check. The domain Chapter model carries isDownloaded (onDeleteAllDownloads in DetailsViewModel already filters on it), so the filter is one line.
evidence: details.chapters.forEach { chapter -> val chapterId = chapterIdResolver.resolveChapterId(chapter.url) ?: return@forEach; enqueueDownload(...) } — vs native LibraryMangaRoute.kt downloadAllManga: 'val notDownloadedChapters = chapters.filter { !it.isDownloaded }; downloadViewModel.downloadChapters(notDownloadedChapters, manga)'
suggestedFix: Filter before the loop: details.chapters.filter { !it.isDownloaded }.forEach { ... } (restores native behaviour); also correct the KDoc paragraph that claims native does not pre-filter.
verifierNote: EnqueueAllChaptersDownloadUseCase.kt:63-70 loops all chapters with no isDownloaded filter and its KDoc (line 30-34) misstates the spec — native filters first (native LibraryMangaRoute.kt:184 'chapters.filter { !it.isDownloaded }'). Downstream has no guard either (DownloadsActionRepositoryImpl.enqueueDownload:135-147), and ChapterDownloadDao.insert is OnConflictStrategy.REPLACE on a unique chapterId index, so SUCCESS rows demote to QUEUED and everything re-downloads. Fix compiles: domain Chapter.isDownloaded exists (Chapter.kt:72).

title: Multi-select 'download' skips both the !isDownloaded filter and the offline gate that native and the sibling Details download paths apply
detail: onDownloadSelected enqueues every selected url unconditionally. Native's equivalent (LibraryMangaRoute.kt onCustomDownload, lines 204-222) does two things this handler omits: (1) gates on connectivity with a 'no internet' snackbar and early return, and (2) filters 'chapters.filter { !it.isDownloaded }' before enqueueing. The KMP handler has neither, while its own siblings onDownloadChapter (line 796) and onDownloadAllClick (line 674) DO apply the state.value.isOnline gate — so the offline UX is inconsistent across the three Details download actions (offline multi-select downloads silently enqueue, then on iOS/Desktop immediately land in the Failed tab with a network error instead of the native snackbar). And because the selection bar always shows the download action (DetailsScreen.kt:664, even when isSelectionAllDownloaded), selecting a range that includes downloaded chapters re-downloads them: the REPLACE insert demotes each SUCCESS row to QUEUED and the files are re-fetched over the network.
evidence: private fun onDownloadSelected() { ... viewModelScope.launch { selected.forEach { url -> enqueueChapterDownload(...) ... } } } — no isOnline check, no isDownloaded filter; compare onDownloadChapter lines 793-799 (isOnline gate present) and native LibraryMangaRoute.kt:206-222 (gate + filter).
suggestedFix: Mirror the sibling paths: early-return with DetailsEffect.ShowError(AppError.Network.NoConnectivity()) when !state.value.isOnline, and resolve the selected urls against displayChapters to drop chapters whose isDownloaded is true before enqueueing.
verifierNote: DetailsViewModel.kt:873-886 onDownloadSelected has neither the isOnline gate (present in siblings onDownloadChapter:796 and onDownloadAllClick:674) nor the !isDownloaded filter; native onCustomDownload (LibraryMangaRoute.kt:206-222) has both. DetailsScreen.kt:664 always exposes the download action in selection mode, so downloaded chapters get REPLACE-demoted and re-fetched. Distinct root from r5-dl-1 (different handler/layer, separate fix).

title: Removing a manga from the library never cancels its in-flight download — on Android the running chapter completes anyway and writes a permanently orphaned CBZ into the just-purged manga directory
detail: purgeManga deletes all rows (removeMangaWithChapters cascades chapter_downloads + saved_chapters) and the on-disk manga/<id> directory, but nothing stops the download engine if one of this manga's chapters is RUNNING/COMPRESSING at that moment. On Android, ChapterDownloadService has no per-page DB-state cooperative check (only ensureActive/isStopped), so the worker keeps downloading the full chapter after the purge: each downloadImage call does mkdirs() and recreates manga/<id>/chapter_<id>/, OptimizedCbzManager then writes chapter_<id>.cbz there, and the terminal DAO/chapterDao writes are silent no-ops because the rows are gone. The result is a complete downloaded chapter on disk referenced by nothing — and it can never be cleaned up: the queue row, chapter row and manga row are deleted, and re-adding the manga generates a NEW autoGenerate saved_manga.id, so deleteMangaFiles will never target the old directory again. Permanent storage leak (a full chapter, potentially tens of MB) plus the wasted bandwidth of finishing a download the user just discarded. On iOS/Desktop the per-page state check (CoroutineDownloadRepositoryImpl.processJob) aborts after at most one more page, so the leak there is bounded to a page or two. Native shares the no-cancel posture, but the leak is real user harm (the campaign's storage-size displays make stale storage visible), so it is reported despite the parity caveat.
evidence: purgeManga: libraryDeo.removeMangaWithChapters(id); fileService.deleteMangaFiles(id) — no interaction with DownloadRepository. Android engine: ChapterDownloadService.downloadImage does File(context.filesDir, "manga/$mangaId/chapter_$chapterId").apply { mkdirs() } per page and never re-reads the chapter_downloads row state; DownloadWorkerV2.handleCompleteSafely's updateStateAndProgress/markChapterDownloaded silently no-op on the deleted rows.
suggestedFix: Before purging, look up chapter_downloads rows for the mangaId in RUNNING/COMPRESSING and route them through legacy cancelARunningChapter (which cancels the Android worker / iOS-Desktop active job and deletes partial files), then purge; alternatively re-run fileService.deleteMangaFiles(id) after the engine confirms termination. Owner decision on exact mechanism.
verifierNote: Mechanics confirmed: LibraryRepositoryImpl.purgeManga (281-291) never touches the download engine; DownloadWorkerV2's loop has no per-page DB-state re-check (only isStopped, line 143), ChapterDownloadService.downloadImage mkdirs() recreates the purged dir (lines 124/274), and terminal UPDATE writes no-op on deleted rows, so a full orphan chapter (unreachable after the autoGenerate id changes) can be written. Downgraded major→minor: requires the narrow race of an in-flight chapter at purge time, harm is hidden storage/bandwidth (bounded to one chapter), and the finding itself concedes native shares the no-cancel posture.

title: cancelARunningChapter deletes the chapter's files and force-fails the row without re-checking it is still active — a cancel tap racing completion destroys a just-completed download while saved_chapters.isDownloaded stays true
detail: Both engines' cancel-running paths act unconditionally on a chapterId captured from a UI snapshot: Android's cancelARunningChapter does cancelUniqueWork → deleteChapterFiles(mangaId, chapterId) → onCancel(chapterId)=FAILED; the iOS/Desktop twin (CoroutineDownloadRepositoryImpl.cancelARunningChapter, line 171) checks activeChapterId only to decide whether to cancel the Job, then likewise unconditionally deleteChapterFiles + onCancel. If the chapter completes in the window between the UI rendering the RUNNING/COMPRESSING affordance and the cancel executing (Room-flow latency plus, on Details, the COMPRESSING tail where users tap cancel as compression finishes), the handler deletes the freshly written CBZ/pages and flips the SUCCESS row to FAILED — but DownloadWorkerV2.handleCompleteSafely / processJob already set saved_chapters.isDownloaded=true and localImagePaths, and nothing un-sets them. The chapter then claims 'Downloaded' in Details/Library and opens to missing files offline (the loose-file read path has no existence fallback per the known finding on ChapterPagesRepositoryImpl:196, compounding the breakage).
evidence: override suspend fun cancelARunningChapter(chapterId: Long, mangaId: Long) { workManager.cancelUniqueWork(WORK_NAME); chapterDownloadService.deleteChapterFiles(mangaId, chapterId); onCancel(chapterId); enqueueRequest() } — no check that the row is still RUNNING/COMPRESSING. Same shape in CoroutineDownloadRepositoryImpl lines 171-185.
suggestedFix: In both impls, read dao.getDownloadByChapter(chapterId)?.state first and only delete files + mark FAILED when it is RUNNING/COMPRESSING/QUEUED; when it is already SUCCESS, return without side effects (the cancel raced completion).
verifierNote: Both impls act unconditionally on a UI-snapshot chapterId: androidMain DownloadRepositoryImpl.kt:93-98 (cancelUniqueWork → deleteChapterFiles → onCancel=FAILED) and CoroutineDownloadRepositoryImpl.kt:171-185 (activeChapterId checked only for the Job, then unconditional deleteChapterFiles + onCancel). Completion path sets saved_chapters.isDownloaded + localImagePaths (DownloadWorkerV2:287-288; CoroutineDownloadRepositoryImpl:343-349) and nothing un-sets them, so a cancel racing completion deletes the CBZ while the chapter still claims Downloaded.

title: enqueueChapterDownload still posts the unique work with ExistingWorkPolicy.KEEP — the exact dropped-enqueue race the reconcile fix in the same file documents and fixed with APPEND_OR_REPLACE
detail: reconcileInterruptedDownloads (lines 108-120, same file) was deliberately switched to APPEND_OR_REPLACE with a comment explaining why KEEP is wrong: 'if that prior run already passed its final getNextQueuedChapter()==null it finishes without ever seeing the row we just re-QUEUED'. The ordinary user enqueue path has the identical race and still uses the KEEP default: dao.insert lands after the running worker's final getNextQueuedChapter() returned null but before WorkManager marks the chain terminal → enqueueUniqueWork(KEEP) drops the request → the new row sits QUEUED with no worker, until the next enqueue of any chapter or the next app launch's reconcile. Most likely trigger: enqueueing chapter B just as chapter A's download finishes. The iOS/Desktop twin is immune (Channel.UNLIMITED wake-ups are buffered).
evidence: private fun enqueueRequest(policy: ExistingWorkPolicy = ExistingWorkPolicy.KEEP) ... override suspend fun enqueueChapterDownload(...) { val id = dao.insert(...); if (id >= 0L) enqueueRequest() } — vs reconcileInterruptedDownloads() { dao.reEnqueueInterrupted(); enqueueRequest(ExistingWorkPolicy.APPEND_OR_REPLACE) } and its comment block describing the KEEP drop.
suggestedFix: Use ExistingWorkPolicy.APPEND_OR_REPLACE for the enqueue path too (or make it the enqueueRequest default) — the worker drains the Room queue regardless, so an appended no-op pass is harmless.
verifierNote: DownloadRepositoryImpl.kt:64 enqueueRequest defaults to ExistingWorkPolicy.KEEP and enqueueChapterDownload (74-83) uses that default, while reconcileInterruptedDownloads (117-120) in the same file was switched to APPEND_OR_REPLACE with a comment (108-116) describing exactly this KEEP-drop race (insert after the worker's final getNextQueuedChapter()==null, before the chain goes terminal → row sits QUEUED with no worker). Same race applies to the ordinary enqueue; iOS/Desktop twin is immune via the UNLIMITED wake-up channel.

title: cancelAllDownloads on iOS/Desktop never deletes the active chapter's partial pages — asymmetric with the single-chapter cancel and with Android, and the orphans are unreachable after a row delete
detail: cancelAllDownloads cancels the active Job and bulk-flips rows to FAILED, but unlike cancelARunningChapter (which calls deleteChapterFiles) and unlike Android (whose worker catch runs chapterDownloadService.deleteChapterFiles for currentChapter on cancellation), no file cleanup happens for the chapter that was mid-download — its partial image_N files stay in chapterDir. The engine's failure policy deliberately keeps partial pages 'for the next retry', but the FAILED row's two user affordances diverge: Retry overwrites them, while Delete (DownloadsActionRepositoryImpl.deleteDownload, intentionally row-only per #10) removes the row and orphans the partial pages until the whole manga is purged. The same leak applies to per-page failure → FAILED → user deletes the row instead of retrying.
evidence: override suspend fun cancelAllDownloads() { activeJobMutex.withLock { toCancel = activeJob; ... }; toCancel?.cancelAndJoin(); dao.markAllRunningOrQueuedAsFailed() } — no deleteChapterFiles; workerLoop's CancellationException catch (line 237-240) also only does dao.updateFailure. Contrast cancelARunningChapter line 181: deleteChapterFiles(mangaId, chapterId).
suggestedFix: Capture the active (chapterId, mangaId) under the mutex in cancelAllDownloads and call deleteChapterFiles for it after cancelAndJoin (mirroring cancelARunningChapter); alternatively delete partial files when a FAILED row is deleted.
verifierNote: CoroutineDownloadRepositoryImpl.cancelAllDownloads (193-202) cancels the job and bulk-FAILs rows with no deleteChapterFiles, and the workerLoop CancellationException catch (237-240) only writes updateFailure — vs cancelARunningChapter:181 which deletes files, and the Android worker catch which runs deleteChapterFiles for currentChapter. deleteDownload (163-165) is row-only, so partial pages orphan until the whole manga purge. Asymmetry confirmed.

title: Re-enqueueing a chapter that is already RUNNING/COMPRESSING aborts it and restarts from page 0 on iOS/Desktop — the REPLACE insert demotes the live row to QUEUED
detail: enqueueChapterDownload unconditionally dao.insert()s; with OnConflictStrategy.REPLACE on the unique chapterId index, enqueueing a chapter that is currently downloading rewrites its row to state=QUEUED/progress=0. The engine's per-page cooperative check (processJob: 'state != RUNNING → abort') then treats the in-flight job as cancelled mid-chapter, leaves its partial pages, and the worker loop re-pulls the same chapter and downloads it again from page 0. Triggers are easy: double-tapping the Details/Updates download button before the first Room emission flips the affordance, enqueueing the same chapter from Updates while Details queued it, or download-all over a queue with an active chapter (compounded by r5-dl-1's missing filter and the dead isDownloadingAll guard on the header button). Android self-heals because its engine never re-reads the row state mid-chapter, so only iOS/Desktop pays the full restart. There is no enqueue-time dedup anywhere in the chain (DownloadsActionRepositoryImpl.enqueueDownload does a chapter-row lookup, never a downloads-row state check).
evidence: override suspend fun enqueueChapterDownload(...) { val id = dao.insert(chapter.toChapterDownloadEntity(...)); if (id >= 0L) wakeups.trySend(Unit) } + ChapterDownloadDao.insert @Insert(onConflict = OnConflictStrategy.REPLACE) + ChapterDownloadEntity Index(value=["chapterId"], unique=true) + processJob lines 284-291 abort when state != RUNNING.
suggestedFix: In enqueueChapterDownload (or DownloadsActionRepositoryImpl.enqueueDownload), read getDownloadByChapter(chapterId) first and no-op when the existing row is QUEUED/RUNNING/COMPRESSING, only REPLACE for SUCCESS/FAILED/absent rows.
verifierNote: CoroutineDownloadRepositoryImpl.enqueueChapterDownload (154-161) does an unconditional dao.insert; ChapterDownloadDao.insert is OnConflictStrategy.REPLACE (ChapterDownloadDao.kt:106) against the unique chapterId index (ChapterDownloadEntity.kt:23), demoting a live RUNNING row to QUEUED; processJob's cooperative check (284-291) then aborts mid-chapter and the worker re-pulls it from page 0. No dedup anywhere in the chain (DownloadsActionRepositoryImpl.enqueueDownload does no downloads-row state check). iOS/Desktop-only full restart, as claimed.

title: iOS/Desktop persist the cancel reason as hardcoded English 'Cancelled by user' — shown verbatim in the Failed tab on localized devices, while Android localizes the same path
detail: The Failed tab renders the persisted errorMsg ('Failed: %s', DownloadsScreen.kt:591). Android's single-chapter cancel writes the localized string (DownloadRepositoryImpl.onCancel uses context.getString(R.string.cancelled_by_user), and native ships that key in all 10 locales), but the iOS/Desktop engine writes the raw companion constant CANCELLED_BY_USER = "Cancelled by user" from onCancel and the workerLoop cancellation catch — so an Arabic/Russian/Japanese user on iOS/Desktop sees English text in the Failed list for every cancelled download. (The bulk markAllRunningOrQueuedAsFailed SQL literal is English on all platforms, matching native verbatim — parity; the per-chapter iOS/Desktop path has no such parity constraint since native is Android-only.)
evidence: const val CANCELLED_BY_USER = "Cancelled by user" used at onCancel (line 168) and the workerLoop catch (line 239); Android twin: dao.updateFailure(chapterId, context.getString(me.manga.yamiapk.shared.R.string.cancelled_by_user)).

title: Desktop/iOS inline library refresh skips the cover-image-change propagation the Android worker performs — saved covers go permanently stale on those platforms
detail: The Android LibraryRefreshWorker (app/src/main/java/me/manga/yamiapk/work/LibraryRefreshWorker.kt:243-245) checks `mangaInfo.imageUrl != manga.imageUrl` on every per-manga fetch and calls `libraryRepository.updateMangaImageUrlEverywhere(...)` to rewrite the cover URL in saved_manga, notifications and history. The cross-platform inline refresh (#1) — RefreshAllLibraryChaptersUseCase.refreshOne — fetches the same details but only calls persistAndNotify(manga, chapters); the fetched details' coverUrl is dropped. The class KDoc claims 'both converge on the same ... persist semantics', but the cover-propagation step exists only on Android. Manga sites rotate cover/CDN URLs constantly (APP_MAP domain risk #1), and Desktop/iOS have no worker, so a library cover that rots after add is never repaired there (only the unrelated source-registry version-bump propagation can fix it). The Details refresh path (persistNewChapters) has the same omission.
evidence: refreshOne: `when (val details = fetchDetails(manga)) { is AppResult.Success -> (persistAndNotify(manga, details.value.chapters) ...) }` — details.value.coverUrl unused. Worker: `if (mangaInfo.imageUrl != manga.imageUrl) { libraryRepository.updateMangaImageUrlEverywhere(manga.id, mangaInfo.imageUrl) }`.
suggestedFix: Add a cover-reconcile step to the shared persist path: extend LibraryRepository (rework) with an updateCoverIfChanged(key, newCoverUrl) verb that mirrors the legacy updateMangaImageUrlEverywhere transaction, and call it from refreshOne (and optionally from the Details persistNewChapters path) when details.coverUrl differs from the saved row's imageUrl.
verifierNote: RefreshAllLibraryChaptersUseCase.kt:69-74 uses only details.value.chapters; PersistNewChaptersAndNotifyUseCase/LibraryRepositoryImpl.persistNewChaptersAndNotify (LibraryRepositoryImpl.kt:191-214) never touch the cover, while the Android worker does propagate (LibraryRefreshWorker.kt:243-245 updateMangaImageUrlEverywhere). Desktop/iOS run only the inline path, so rotated covers are never repaired there; the KDoc 'both converge on the same persist semantics' overstates convergence.

title: Android offline pull-to-refresh gives zero feedback: the refresh job is enqueued with a CONNECTED network constraint (native enqueued unconstrained) and ENQUEUED maps to Idle, so nothing visible happens until the work fires later unexpectedly
detail: refresh() builds BackgroundJob(tag/workerClass/uniqueWorkName) without overriding requiresNetwork, which defaults to true (BackgroundJobScheduler.kt BackgroundJob: `val requiresNetwork: Boolean = true`), so AndroidBackgroundJobScheduler adds Constraints NetworkType.CONNECTED. Native's RefreshViewModel.refreshLibrary enqueued a plain OneTimeWorkRequestBuilder<LibraryRefreshWorker>() with no constraints — offline, the worker started immediately and its foreground notification reported per-manga failures. In the KMP app, an offline pull-to-refresh leaves the work ENQUEUED; observeUniqueWork maps ENQUEUED → JobState.Idle → spinner false, so the user sees no spinner, no error, no notification — the gesture appears dead — and the refresh then runs as a surprise background job (with its foreground notification) whenever connectivity returns.
evidence: LibraryRefreshRepositoryImpl.refresh(): `BackgroundJob(tag = REFRESH_WORK_NAME, workerClass = ..., uniqueWorkName = REFRESH_WORK_NAME)` — requiresNetwork default true; AndroidBackgroundJobScheduler.toJobState(): 'ENQUEUED / BLOCKED / CANCELLED / null collapse to Idle'.
suggestedFix: Either pass requiresNetwork = false for the user-initiated refresh (restoring native immediate-run-and-report behavior), or surface the ENQUEUED state (e.g. map ENQUEUED of the unique chain to a 'waiting for network' UI signal) so the gesture has visible feedback offline.
verifierNote: Verified end-to-end: BackgroundJob.requiresNetwork defaults true (BackgroundJobScheduler.kt:92), LibraryRefreshRepositoryImpl.refresh() (lines 115-121) never overrides it, AndroidBackgroundJobScheduler.toConstraints adds NetworkType.CONNECTED (line 136) and toJobState collapses ENQUEUED to Idle (lines 124-131), so observeIsRefreshing maps to spinner=false. Native RefreshViewModel.refreshLibrary (native-app RefreshViewModel.kt:88-99) enqueued a constraint-free OneTimeWorkRequest that ran immediately offline. Offline pull-to-refresh therefore gives zero feedback and fires later as a surprise — a real parity/UX divergence.

title: Rework history rows are written with mangaId=0, so the Android worker's cover-change propagation (history UPDATE keyed by mangaId) never matches them — History covers stay stale
detail: record() inserts HistoryItemD(mangaId = 0L, ...) — documented as safe because the upsert keys on mangaUrl. But the legacy LibraryRepository.updateMangaImageUrlEverywhere (shared/.../library/domain/LibraryRepository.kt:202-203), invoked by LibraryRefreshWorker when a manga's cover URL changes, propagates the new cover to history via `historyDao.updateMangaImageUrl(mangaId, newImageUrl)` (UPDATE history_items ... WHERE mangaId = :mangaId). With every rework-written history row carrying mangaId=0, that UPDATE matches nothing, so after a source rotates a cover URL the Library/Details/Updates covers refresh on Android but the History screen keeps rendering the dead URL (broken image). The purge path already grew url-keyed belt-and-braces twins (removeHistoryByUrl) for exactly this mangaId=0 posture; the image-propagation path was not given the same treatment.
evidence: HistoryRepositoryImpl.record(): `HistoryItemD(api = ..., mangaId = 0L, mangaUrl = manga.url, ...)`; legacy LibraryRepository.updateMangaImageUrlEverywhere: `historyDao.updateMangaImageUrl(mangaId, newImageUrl)` keyed on the real Room id.
suggestedFix: Add a url-keyed variant (`UPDATE history_items SET mangaImageUrl = :newImageUrl WHERE mangaUrl = :mangaUrl`) and call it from updateMangaImageUrlEverywhere alongside the mangaId-keyed one (mirroring the removeHistoryByUrl belt-and-braces pattern), or resolve and store the real mangaId in record() when the manga is in-library.
verifierNote: HistoryRepositoryImpl.record() (line 99) writes HistoryItemD(mangaId = 0L); insertOrUpdateHistory upserts by mangaUrl, so rework-created rows keep mangaId=0 forever. Legacy LibraryRepository.updateMangaImageUrlEverywhere (shared library/domain/LibraryRepository.kt:198-204) propagates cover changes to history via historyDao.updateMangaImageUrl(mangaId,...) — `UPDATE history_items ... WHERE mangaId = :mangaId` (HistoryDao.kt:53) — which matches nothing for mangaId=0 rows. History covers stay stale after a cover-URL rotation while library/notifications update. Not a duplicate of r5-lib-1 (different propagation gap: worker-side history miss vs no inline propagation at all).

title: Statistics read-duration is formatted as hardcoded English "${h}h ${m}m" in :shared — native localizes h_m in 11 locales (Arabic, Japanese, Russian...), so all non-English users see an untranslated duration
detail: readDurationFlow maps the persisted minute counter to the literal string `"${h}h ${m}m"` (with a 'TODO Phase 10: stringResource(R.string.h_m, h, m)' comment). Native resolves R.string.h_m, which is translated in every shipped locale (values-ar: '%1$dس %2$dد', values-ja: '%1$d時 %2$d分', values-ru: '%1$dч %2$dм', etc.). The rework Statistics screen renders this pre-formatted string verbatim (ReadingStatistics.readDuration: String flows through ReadingStatisticsRepositoryImpl → StatisticsViewModel → StatisticsScreen), so an Arabic/Japanese/Russian UI shows an English-format duration — a visible i18n parity regression on the Statistics screen. It also violates the rework rule that user-facing text is localized at the :ui call site, not produced in :data/:shared.

suggestedFix: Expose the raw minutes (Int) through ReadingStatistics instead of a pre-formatted string, and format in :ui StatisticsScreen via a compose-resources np_* string with the native h_m translations ported across the 10 locales.

Native localizes h_m in all shipped locales (e.g. values-ar:800 '%1$dس %2$dد', values-ja '%1$d時 %2$d分', values-ru '%1$dч %2$dм').
