title: Stale param KDoc: 'Home/Library quick-toggle pass the default emptyList()' — no production add-path passes empty chapters anymore, and the default is a latent Updates-flood hazard
detail: The invoke() param doc claims callers with no chapter context (Home/Library quick-toggle) add with emptyList() and 'chapters fill in on the first Details open'. In the live code, HomeViewModel.onSaveToggle (HomeViewModel.kt:310-316) deliberately fetches the FULL chapter list first and short-circuits on fetch failure precisely so a half-saved 0-chapter row can never be created; the Library screen has no add affordance; Details always passes the fetched chapters (the body that hosts the bookmark button only renders when details != null). The doc therefore describes a retired design. Worth noting because the emptyList() default it advertises is hazardous: a 0-chapter library row makes the next refresh treat the manga's ENTIRE backlist as newly-discovered — persistNewChaptersAndNotify writes a notifications row per chapter (hundreds for popular titles), flooding the Updates feed and (on Android) posting system notifications, plus stamping isNew=true on every chapter for 4 days.
evidence: KDoc: 'Callers with no chapter context (Home/Library quick-toggle) pass the default `emptyList()`; the add still succeeds and chapters fill in on the first Details open.' vs HomeViewModel.kt:312 comment 'toggleInLibrary never runs on a failed fetch (no half-saved 0-chapter row)'.
suggestedFix: Rewrite the param KDoc to state that add-paths must supply the fetched chapter list (Home fetches before toggling; remove ignores it), and document the Updates-flood consequence of a 0-chapter add — or drop the emptyList() default entirely so future callers must opt in explicitly.
verifierNote: KDoc at ToggleInLibraryUseCase.kt:56-59 claims Home/Library quick-toggle ADDs with the default emptyList() and 'chapters fill in on the first Details open' — contradicted by HomeViewModel.onSaveToggle (HomeViewModel.kt:310-316), which deliberately fetches the full chapter list and short-circuits on failure ('no half-saved 0-chapter row'); the only other caller (DetailsViewModel.kt:727) passes the fetched chapters. Only the remove branch (which ignores chapters) uses the default. Stale param doc describing a retired design; the flood-hazard framing of a 0-chapter add is accurate (persistNewChaptersAndNotify would notify the whole backlist).

title: Coil ImageLoader has no explicit diskCache — on iOS/Desktop the image cache (up to 250MB) lands in the system temp dir, invisible to Settings' cache size and never cleared by Clear Cache
detail: The singleton ImageLoader in App.kt configures components and maxBitmapSize but never sets .diskCache(...), so Coil 3.4.0's default singletonDiskCache() is used: DiskCache.Builder().directory(FileSystem.SYSTEM_TEMPORARY_DIRECTORY / "coil3_disk_cache") with maxSize = 2% of free disk clamped to [10MB, 250MB] (verified in coil-core-3.4.0 sources, nonJsCommonMain/coil3/disk/utils.kt). On Android this accidentally works out (java.io.tmpdir == context.cacheDir, so the cache lives under the app cache dir that the Settings cache-size walk measures and clearFilesLargerThan1MB clears). On iOS SYSTEM_TEMPORARY_DIRECTORY = NSTemporaryDirectory() (the sandbox tmp/ dir) while IosAppFileSystem.cacheDir = NSCachesDirectory; on Desktop it is the system-wide $TMPDIR while DesktopAppFileSystem.cacheDir = ~/.yami-manga/cache. Consequences on iOS/Desktop: (1) the Settings screen's displayed cache size (SettingsRepositoryImpl.observeSettings -> legacy.getCacheFolderSize() which walks fs.cacheDir) never includes the largest cache in the app — every cover and chapter page ever viewed; (2) 'Clear cache' (legacy.clearFilesLargerThan1MB over fs.cacheDir) can never reclaim it — up to 250MB of images a user explicitly tried to delete stay on disk; (3) on Desktop the directory is shared machine-wide with every other Coil3-based JVM app and with a second instance of this app — Coil's own source comments that the singleton exists because two DiskCache instances must never share a directory, but that guard is per-process only (okio DiskLruCache has no cross-process file locking), so concurrent instances can corrupt the journal.
evidence: App.kt:359-377 builds ImageLoader.Builder(ctx).components{...}.maxBitmapSize(Size.ORIGINAL).build() — no .diskCache(). coil-core 3.4.0 nonJsCommonMain/coil3/disk/utils.kt: 'DiskCache.Builder().directory(FileSystem.SYSTEM_TEMPORARY_DIRECTORY / "coil3_disk_cache")'. IosAppFileSystem.kt:29 'cacheDir = resolveDir(NSCachesDirectory)'; DesktopAppFileSystem.kt:22+31 cacheDir = ~/.yami-manga/cache. SettingsRepositoryImpl.kt:183-186 cache size = legacy.getCacheFolderSize() (walks fs.cacheDir only).
suggestedFix: In the setSingletonImageLoaderFactory block, set an explicit disk cache rooted under the app's own cache dir on every platform, e.g. .diskCache { DiskCache.Builder().directory(appFileSystem.cacheDir / "image_cache").build() } (inject AppFileSystem/the path via Koin like sourcesRepository already is). That makes the Settings cache size/clear feature actually cover the image cache on iOS/Desktop and gives the Desktop app a per-user, per-app directory.
verifierNote: Verified against coil-core 3.4.0 sources (nonJsCommonMain/coil3/disk/utils.kt: SYSTEM_TEMPORARY_DIRECTORY/'coil3_disk_cache'; DiskCache.Builder defaults 2% free, clamped 10MB-250MB) and App.kt:359-377 (no .diskCache()). okio iOS SYSTEM_TEMPORARY_DIRECTORY resolves $TMPDIR (sandbox tmp/), while IosAppFileSystem.cacheDir=NSCachesDirectory (IosAppFileSystem.kt:29) and DesktopAppFileSystem.cacheDir=~/.yami-manga/cache (line 22); Settings size/clear walk only fs.cacheDir (SettingsRepository.kt:106-116, SettingsRepositoryImpl.kt:183-186). So on iOS/Desktop the largest cache is invisible to and unclearable by Settings, and Desktop shares a machine-wide temp dir across processes. Major: user-facing cache management is factually wrong on 2 of 3 platforms.

title: Coil header interceptor runs a fresh Room getAllSources query (plus ~150 Ktor Url parses) for every image request whose host misses the in-memory scan — per-cover/per-page on hot scroll paths, never memoized
detail: CoilSourceHeaderInterceptor (App.kt:296) calls SourcesRepository.findRepoByHost(host) on EVERY Coil image request (Coil interceptors run before the engine's memory-cache service, on the main dispatcher). findRepoByHost first scans all ~50 registered repos parsing up to 3 URLs each with Ktor's Url() inside runCatching (~150 allocating parses per request, on the main thread), and when no repo matches — which is the steady state for every image from a host unrelated to a source's baseUrl/imgBaseUrl: Firestore/complaint screenshots, What's-New gallery images, and sources whose page/cover CDN is a different apex domain (e.g. wasabisys S3, comick pictures CDN) — it falls through to sourcesDao.getAllSources().first(), executing a fresh Room full-table query per image. The result is never cached, so a fling through a 3-column library grid or a 200-page chapter from an unrelated-CDN source issues one DB query + ~150 Url parses per image, every time. The KDoc's justification ('Room/SQLDelight is in-memory cached after the first query, cheap enough to run per image') is incorrect — Room flows re-run the query on each collection; nothing here is cached.
evidence: SourcesRepository.kt:193-204: fast path 'repos.firstOrNull { sequenceOf(repo.baseUrl, repo.BASE_URL, repo.imgBaseUrl).mapNotNull(::parseHostOrNull)... }' then 'val entities = sourcesDao.getAllSources().first()' on miss. App.kt:296 'val match = sourcesRepository.findRepoByHost(host)' inside Interceptor.intercept, which runs per request.
suggestedFix: Memoize per host: keep a Map<String, BaseMangaRepository?> (with negative entries) invalidated when the sources table changes (the repo already has allSources Flow to hook), and pre-parse each repo's three candidate hosts once instead of per request. Also stop re-querying Room per miss — collect getAllSources() into a cached snapshot.
verifierNote: SourcesRepository.findRepoByHost (SourcesRepository.kt:191-211): fast path parses up to 3 Urls per repo across ~50 repos per call, and every miss runs sourcesDao.getAllSources().first() — a fresh Room query per image request (Room flows re-execute the query per collection; nothing is memoized). Called from CoilSourceHeaderInterceptor on every Coil request (App.kt:296), including memory-cache hits (user interceptors precede EngineInterceptor). The KDoc's 'in-memory cached after the first query' justification is wrong. Real hot-path waste; minor (perf, not correctness).

title: iOS AVIF pages are decoded at full resolution TWICE with a full-res lossless PNG buffer in between — multi-hundred-MB transient spikes when the reader decodes several tall AVIF strips concurrently
detail: IosAvifDecoder.decode() materializes, per page: (1) the full encoded AVIF ByteArray; (2) a full-resolution UIImage/CGImage raster (W*H*4 bytes — ~45MB for a typical 800x14000 webtoon strip); (3) a full-resolution lossless PNG re-encode via UIImagePNGRepresentation (NSData, typically tens of MB and CPU-expensive at this size); (4) a Kotlin ByteArray COPY of that PNG (NSData and copy alive simultaneously); (5) a SECOND full-resolution raster when decodeEncodedImageWithSkia calls Image.makeFromEncoded(png) and draws it; (6) the downsampled dst bitmap. Peak transient native memory is roughly 2 full rasters + 2 PNG buffers per page, and Coil decodes multiple pages concurrently while the reader scrolls/preloads, multiplying the spike. The ObjC-side UIImage/NSData are additionally released only when Kotlin/Native's GC collects their wrappers, so the pressure is not promptly relieved. On AVIF-heavy sources (the Bug-5 Cloudflare AVIF CDNs this decoder exists for) this is a realistic jetsam/OOM-kill risk on tall strips, plus a large per-page CPU cost (full-res PNG encode) on the reader's hottest path. The size hint (options.size) is only applied at step 5/6 — after all full-res work is done.
evidence: IosAvifDecoder.kt:51-56 'val avif = source.source().use { it.readByteArray() }; val png = decodeAvifToPngBytes(avif)...; return decodeEncodedImageWithSkia(png, options)'; :69-77 UIImage.imageWithData -> UIImagePNGRepresentation -> NSData.toByteArray() (memcpy copy). decodeEncodedImageWithSkia then calls Image.makeFromEncoded(png) and rasterizes the whole source before downsampling (HighQualitySkiaImageDecoder.kt:89-135).
suggestedFix: Decode directly at target size with ImageIO instead of the PNG round-trip: CGImageSourceCreateWithData + CGImageSourceCreateThumbnailAtIndex with kCGImageSourceThumbnailMaxPixelSize derived from options.size (and kCGImageSourceShouldCacheImmediately), then copy the downsampled CGImage pixels straight into a Skia Bitmap. That removes one full raster, both PNG buffers, and the full-res encode. At minimum, wrap the ObjC work in an autoreleasepool and downscale the UIImage before re-encoding.
verifierNote: IosAvifDecoder.kt:51-56 + 69-86: full AVIF bytes -> UIImage -> full-res lossless UIImagePNGRepresentation NSData -> memcpy'd Kotlin ByteArray -> decodeEncodedImageWithSkia (HighQualitySkiaImageDecoder.kt:89-135) re-decodes the PNG full-res via Image.makeFromEncoded + drawImageRect before downsampling; options.size is only applied at the last step. For ~800x14000 strips that is ~45MB raster + tens-of-MB PNG x2 per page, with ObjC buffers freed only on K/N GC and Coil decoding pages concurrently — realistic jetsam risk on the AVIF sources this decoder exists for, squarely in the APP_MAP huge-images/memory risk profile. Major (crash risk), confidence medium stands.

title: Kermit release log floor exists only on Android — iOS/Desktop production builds emit the full VERBOSE/DEBUG stream, including the per-page-flip Reader trace with chapter URLs, into OS logs
detail: Only the Android host sets a production log floor (MyApp.kt:160 Logger.setMinSeverity(Severity.Warn) in release builds). Neither the Desktop entry point (Main.kt) nor the iOS host configures Kermit, so production iOS/Desktop builds run at Kermit's default Verbose floor. Concretely: FlowLog (core/logging/FlowLog.kt) explicitly relies on 'the Android-release Logger.setMinSeverity(Severity.Warn) floor... suppresses it in release builds with no extra wiring' — but on iOS/Desktop it fires on EVERY reader page change (ReaderViewModel.onPageChanged:603 logs flatIndex + activeChapter=<full chapter URL>), writing the user's page-by-page reading history into the persistent OS log (Console/os_log on macOS/iOS); SourcesRepository.getSiteStateFlow logs at .v per emission; and the many per-source request/header logs already flagged individually all stay live. Besides the privacy leak of reading-history URLs in system logs, this is sustained string-building and os_log I/O on the reader's hottest path.
evidence: Grep across desktopApp/, iosApp/, composeApp/iosMain for setMinSeverity/minSeverity: only app/src/main/java/me/manga/yamiapk/MyApp.kt:160 hit. FlowLog.kt:19-21 KDoc states release suppression comes solely from the Android host's floor. ReaderViewModel.kt:603 FlowLog.log("Reader", "page", "flatIndex=... activeChapter=$activeUrl...") on every page change.
suggestedFix: Set the same release floor at the other two entry points: in desktop Main.kt before startKoin (gate on a build flag or System property), and in the iOS app init (e.g. MainViewController/Koin bootstrap) — Logger.setMinSeverity(Severity.Warn) for non-debug builds.
verifierNote: Core confirmed: the only setMinSeverity site repo-wide is app/MyApp.kt:160 (Android release); Kermit defaults to Verbose elsewhere, and FlowLog.kt:19-21 explicitly relies on the Android-only floor, so iOS/Desktop production builds emit the per-page-flip Reader trace incl. full chapter URLs (ReaderViewModel.kt:603-607). Adjusted detail: the persistent-OS-log privacy exposure applies to iOS (Kermit's Apple writer goes to os_log); on Desktop the JVM default writer is stdout/console, not a persistent OS log — overhead yes, persisted reading history no.

title: regex-replace/regex-extract transforms recompile Regex(pattern) for every field of every item — the bundled chapter.number regex-extract recompiles once per chapter row on piloted sources
detail: Transforms.applyOne constructs Regex(spec.args["pattern"]) inline on each invocation for both 'regex-replace' (line 68) and 'regex-extract' (line 79). Transforms run per extracted field per item, so a chapters fetch on a piloted source whose config uses a regex transform — the bundled PILOT_SOURCES_CONFIG_JSON does, for chapter.number (BundledSourcesConfig.kt:372 regex-extract '\\d+(\\.\\d+)?') — recompiles the identical pattern once per chapter row (hundreds of compiles per details/chapters load, repeated on every refetch). Patterns come from the validated, bounded config document, so a tiny memoization map is safe and bounded; the engine already memoizes its static regexes (STRIP_HTML/WHITESPACE) the right way.
evidence: Transforms.kt:68 'runCatching { Regex(pattern).replace(value, replacement) }' and :79 'val matches = Regex(pattern).findAll(value).toList()' — both inside applyOne, called from apply(value, specs) per field per item. BundledSourcesConfig.kt:372 ships a live regex-extract on chapter.number.
suggestedFix: Cache compiled patterns, e.g. a private val regexCache = mutableMapOf<String, Regex>() guarded by the engine's single-threaded use (or atomicfu lock), keyed by pattern: regexCache.getOrPut(pattern) { Regex(pattern) }. Bounded by the number of distinct patterns in the active config.
verifierNote: Transforms.kt:68 and :79 construct Regex(pattern) inline inside applyOne, invoked per field per item from GenericSourceClient (lines 396/429/460/486); the bundled pilot config ships a live regex-extract on chapter.number (BundledSourcesConfig.kt:372), so a chapters fetch recompiles the same pattern once per row. STRIP_HTML/WHITESPACE (Transforms.kt:97-98) show the engine already memoizes static regexes. Bounded, validated pattern set makes a memo map safe.

title: Adult hard-block gate is bypassed on cache-first opens: classification only uses nav-arg genres and the cache-only path never re-classifies, while History/Updates pass genres=emptyList()
detail: The P0-ADULT gate is armed in onEnter() solely from the nav-arg manga.genres (line 302), and the only re-classification site is runFetch().onSuccess (fetched genres). Since the 2026-06-01 cache-first change, shouldOpenFromCache() suppresses runFetch entirely for an in-library manga with a saved chapter list — and the saved-details collector (startObservingSavedDetails) renders the full cover + chapter list from Room without ever calling isAdultContent on the saved genres. HistoryReworkScreenRoute.kt:96 and UpdatesReworkScreenRoute.kt:134 both navigate with `genres = emptyList()` and a comment saying 'Details re-fetches them' — stale since cache-first: for in-library manga (Updates rows are by definition in-library; History rows usually are) there is no fetch, so tentativeAdult=false, adultGateStep=None, and an adult title renders fully ungated. The same hole applies to Home/Search entries whose feed parsers don't populate genres. This directly contradicts the VM's own INTENTIONALLY-DIFFERENT decision (lines 313-319: gate ALL entry points incl. library) and DetailsState.adultGateStep's 'compliance-critical: ... an adult manga can never momentarily render its content' contract — and it is also a native-parity break for Home/Search entries, where native always fetched and classified from the fetched genres before rendering.
evidence: DetailsViewModel.onEnter: `val tentativeAdult = isAdultContent(manga)` (nav-arg genres only) ... `if (!shouldOpenFromCache(manga)) { runFetch(manga) }` — cache branch never re-classifies; startObservingSavedDetails onEach only does `current.copy(details = merged, ...)`. Saved genres ARE available: SavedMangaEntity.toDomainDetails maps `genres = genres` (MangaDetailsMappers.kt:128). HistoryReworkScreenRoute.kt:96 / UpdatesReworkScreenRoute.kt:134: `genres = emptyList()` with stale 'Details re-fetches them' comments.
suggestedFix: In startObservingSavedDetails' onEach (and/or shouldOpenFromCache), re-run the classifier against the saved/merged details genres — e.g. `val refreshedAdult = isAdultContent(manga.copy(genres = merged.genres))` — and arm adultGateStep exactly as runFetch.onSuccess does (None->AdultWarning when adult, preserve advanced steps). Also update the stale route-adapter comments.

title: Disabling/enabling a source while Home is cached desyncs feed, highlighted tab and siteState: the tabs collector never resets or refetches the feed when the enabled set shifts under a fixed activeTabIndex
detail: Home -> edit-tabs -> Sources -> toggle a source -> back is a primary flow. The observeSourceTabs() collector only does `updateState { it.copy(sourceTabs = tabs) }` + restartSiteStateObservation(); activeIndexFlow is a StateFlow whose value does not change when the enabled list shrinks/grows, so nothing resets the feed or re-fetches. Consequences after disabling the active source or any source ordered before it: (1) the feed still shows the old (possibly now-disabled) source's items while the tab strip highlights whichever source shifted into that index — or no tab at all when the index is now out of bounds (activeTab=null); (2) restartSiteStateObservation rebinds the maintenance/stopped/adult gate to the WRONG source's siteState relative to the displayed feed (or keeps the previous source's state when activeTab is null, since it early-returns); (3) a later pull-to-refresh silently calls activeRepo (enabled[idx]) and replaces the feed with a source the user never selected — or EmptyMangaRepository (blank Home) when the index is out of range. The VM/route/Sources screen contain no compensating logic (SourcesViewModel toggle handlers never touch the active index; OnEnter is `started`-guarded on return).
evidence: HomeViewModel.kt:116-121: `observeSourceTabs().onEach { tabs -> updateState { it.copy(sourceTabs = tabs) }; restartSiteStateObservation() }` — feed/page/featured untouched. restartSiteStateObservation(): `val api = state.value.activeTab?.api ?: return` (out-of-bounds index keeps stale siteState). SourcesRepository.activeRepo: `.getOrElse(_activeIndex.value) { EmptyMangaRepository }` — index never clamped/remapped on enabled-set change.
suggestedFix: Track the api the current feed was fetched for; in the tabs collector, when state.activeTab?.api differs from the fetched-feed api (or activeTab becomes null), clamp the index (selectSourceTab) and reset+refetch the feed/featured like onTabSelected does.
verifierNote: Verified: HomeViewModel.kt:116-121 tabs collector only copies sourceTabs + restarts siteState; restartSiteStateObservation (:264-265) early-returns on null activeTab; legacy SourcesRepository.kt:111/131 keeps a raw stored index with getOrElse{EmptyMangaRepository} and never remaps on enabled-set change; HomeFeedRepositoryImpl fetches via sourcesRepository.activeRepo.first() (:213-214), so refresh after a toggle hits the index-shifted source. Home VM survives the Sources round-trip (koinViewModel on a retained back-stack entry, OnEnter started-guarded).

title: Zero-result genre/sort browse renders a completely blank results pane: isIdle is derived from query.isBlank(), but genre browse runs with a deliberately blank query

title: setForeground() from a background-started worker throws on Android 12+, aborting the entire library refresh as 'failed'
detail: doWork() unconditionally calls setForeground(getForegroundInfo()) as its first statement. On API 31+ (targetSdk is 35), setForeground() throws ForegroundServiceStartNotAllowedException whenever the worker starts while the app is NOT in the foreground — and this app's refresh work is exactly the kind that starts in the background: LibraryRefreshRepositoryImpl enqueues the one-off with a CONNECTED network constraint (known finding: offline pull-to-refresh defers until connectivity returns, typically after the user has left the app), and the EXPONENTIAL/30s backoff retry path also re-runs the worker later. When that deferred/retried start happens in the background, the exception is swallowed by doWork's catch (e: Exception), which posts the 'Library refresh failed' error notification and returns Result.failure() — the refresh never runs, and the user gets a spurious failure notification for a refresh they requested while offline. Native never hit this because it enqueued the worker unconstrained from a foregrounded Activity, so the worker always started while the app was visible. The worker is not enqueued as expedited work, so no FGS-restriction exemption applies.
evidence: LibraryRefreshWorker.kt:116-144: `override suspend fun doWork(): Result = supervisorScope { try { setForeground(getForegroundInfo()) ... } catch (e: Exception) { updateNotification(...isError = true); Result.failure() } ... }`. Enqueue path: AndroidBackgroundJobScheduler.scheduleOneOff builds a plain OneTimeWorkRequest (no setExpedited) with Constraints from BackgroundJob.requiresNetwork -> NetworkType.CONNECTED (AndroidBackgroundJobScheduler.kt:50-70, 133-139); LibraryRefreshRepositoryImpl passes requiresNetwork (existing finding at LibraryRefreshRepositoryImpl.kt:115 confirms the CONNECTED constraint). app/build.gradle.kts: targetSdk = 35.
suggestedFix: Wrap the setForeground call in its own try/catch for ForegroundServiceStartNotAllowedException (and the safety net IllegalStateException) and continue the refresh as ordinary background work when foreground promotion is rejected — the supervisorScope body does not require foreground to function. Optionally also mark the request expedited with OutOfQuotaPolicy.RUN_AS_NON_EXPEDITED_WORK_REQUEST for the user-initiated path.

title: Windows/Linux first launch blocks on a ~150-200 MB KCEF download with zero UI — the app shows no window for minutes and looks dead
detail: On Windows/Linux, main() runs the entire KCEF init inside runBlocking(Dispatchers.IO) BEFORE application{} opens the Compose window. The file's own KDoc states first-run init 'downloads ~150-200 MB of CEF + JetBrains Runtime binaries (slow but cached)'. The result: a user double-clicking the freshly installed .msi/.deb build gets NO window, NO splash, NO progress for however long a 150-200 MB download takes on their connection (minutes; indefinitely on a slow/captive network) — only stderr output they will never see in a packaged app. Users will assume the app is broken, force-kill it mid-download, or launch it repeatedly. KCEF's init builder exposes download/extract progress callbacks, and the codebase already contains the exact alternative pattern: the macOS branch lets application{} open immediately while WebViewHost degrades gracefully via the KcefState.initialized handshake — the same late-init recovery would work on Windows/Linux with a visible window during download. This was missed by all prior desktop findings (which covered markInitialized-on-error, macOS spinner, and stale KDoc, but not the first-run blocking window-less download).
evidence: Main.kt:94-161: `if (!isMac) { kcefInitAttempted = true; runBlocking(Dispatchers.IO) { runCatching { KCEF.init(...) } ... } }` executes before `application { ... Window(...) { App() } }` at line 189; KDoc lines 28-29 admit the 150-200 MB first-run download happens inside this blocking call.
suggestedFix: Open the window first and run KCEF.init on a background coroutine on all OSes (the KcefState handshake already makes WebViewHost re-key when init completes), or at minimum show a native splash/progress window during the blocking download using KCEF's onDownloading/onExtracted progress callbacks.
verifierNote: Verified: Main.kt:94-161 runs KCEF.init inside runBlocking(Dispatchers.IO) before application{} at line 189 on non-mac; KDoc lines 28-29 confirm the ~150-200 MB first-run download happens inside that blocking call; desktopApp/build.gradle.kts nativeDistributions (lines 95-99) sets no appResourcesRootDir, so packaged .msi/.deb installs do NOT ship a bundled CEF and really hit the windowless download. The KcefState.markInitialized handshake (Main.kt:153) + WebViewHost re-key already exist, so the suggested async-init fix is feasible; it changes WebView-readiness ordering on Win/Linux, hence risky.

title: Duplicate-binding guard is ineffective on all 3 platforms: Koin 4.2.0 allows definition override by default, so the registration tests cannot fail on the hazard they document
detail: The strangler-fig migration's central DI hazard is the same type being bound in both the legacy graph (SharedModule/platformModule) and a rework module. Three tests (app KoinGraphRegistrationTest:26-31, composeApp DesktopKoinGraphRegistrationTest:20-25, composeApp IosKoinGraphRegistrationTest:19-25) and two production KDocs (KoinInitializer.kt:12-13 'registered in one startKoin call so duplicate-binding diagnostics fire at startup', AppKoinModule.kt postscript 'collisions with SharedModule surface as duplicate-binding diagnostics') all claim a type bound twice surfaces as a registration failure. It does not: Koin 4.2.0's KoinApplication has `private var allowOverride = true` (verified in the 4.2.0 sources, KoinApplication.kt:40), so a duplicate definition silently overrides — last-loaded module wins, behavior depends on module list order, and neither the tests nor app startup report anything. No call to allowOverride(false)/strictOverride() exists anywhere in the repo. Today's graph has no same-platform duplicates (verified by scanning every single<T>/factory/viewModel binding across SharedModule, the 3 PlatformModule actuals, all 17 rework modules and appKoinModule), so nothing is currently broken — but the documented safety net for future slices is a no-op, which is exactly when it is needed (each new rework slice re-binds repository types that have legacy counterparts). Extends shard finding code-aa-12 (which covered only the :app test) to the Desktop/iOS tests and the production bootstrap docs.
evidence: KoinGraphRegistrationTest.kt:17-18 'a type bound twice ... surfaces here as a registration failure' vs Koin 4.2.0 KoinApplication.kt:40 `private var allowOverride = true`; `koinApplication { modules(...) }` in all three tests sets no override policy.
suggestedFix: In all three graph tests, set strict mode before loading modules: `koinApplication { allowOverride(false); modules(...) }`. Optionally do the same in production `initKoin` (KoinInitializer.kt) and `doInitKoin` (KoinHelper.kt) once the tests are green, and correct the KoinInitializer/AppKoinModule KDoc claims if strictness is not adopted in production.
verifierNote: Claim verified against the actual Koin 4.2.0 sources jar: KoinApplication.kt:40 `private var allowOverride = true`, and InstanceRegistry.saveMapping only logs a warning and overwrites when override is allowed — so all three graph tests (app/KoinGraphRegistrationTest.kt:27, composeApp Desktop/Ios twins) cannot fail on a duplicate binding, and no allowOverride(false)/strictOverride exists anywhere in the repo. Severity downgraded major->minor: by the finding's own scan no duplicate exists today, so this is an ineffective test guard plus stale KDoc (KoinInitializer.kt:13), not user-visible incorrectness.

title: Systemic MVI-contract violation across 4 features: effects carry hardcoded English display text and raw exception messages that :ui renders verbatim in all 10 locales
detail: CLAUDE.md's MVI contract: 'Effects carry only trigger data, never rendering data or i18n text' and 'Errors are typed AppError, never String — :ui translates them to localized text'. Four rework features violate both, and their :ui screens pipe the string straight into a snackbar: (1) AdminComplaintViewModel:236 emit(ShowSuccessMessage("Copied to clipboard")), :232/:other call sites pass successMessage literals ("Complaint updated", etc.), :250-255 builds the error from `e.message ?: e::class.simpleName ?: "Unknown error"` — rendered at AdminComplaintScreen.kt:214-215. (2) ComplaintViewModel:168 ("Copied to clipboard"), :227 ("Complaint deleted"), :240-247 same raw-throwable pattern — rendered at ComplaintScreen.kt:193-194. (3) UpdatesViewModel:227 emit(ShowError(throwable.message ?: "Download failed")) — rendered at UpdatesScreen.kt:268. (4) DownloadsViewModel:237-243 emitOnFailure builds `e.message ?: ... ?: "Unknown error"` — rendered at DownloadsScreen.kt:211. Consequences: Arabic/RTL users (the app's primary audience) get English snackbars in core flows, and raw exception/Firestore messages leak to end users. The codebase itself treats this as a bug elsewhere: SettingsViewModel:255-268 (SET-PFIX-P3) explicitly removed this exact pattern as 'embedded unlocalized English in the VM', and SourcesEffect.RequestFailed(body) (SourcesEffect.kt:80-92) demonstrates the sanctioned pattern (effect carries trigger data; :ui resolves Res.string.request_failed). Consolidates and systematizes shard findings code-as-3/6/12 and code-au-5: this is one contract violation repeated across 4 feature slices, best fixed with one shared pattern.

title: Download image-header twins drifted: Android's MangamelloPlus imgsHeader special-case never made it into the iOS/Desktop download engine, which sends `host: plus.mangamello.com` + API headers to the cdn.mangamello.com image host
detail: Two parallel download pipelines attach per-source headers differently. Android ChapterDownloadService.downloadImage (ChapterDownloadService.kt:251-263) special-cases `repo is MangamelloPlusRepository`: image URLs containing mangamello/mello/cdn.mangamello.com get `repo.imgsHeader` (host: cdn.mangamello.com, referer: plus.mangamello.com, UA Dart/3.3) and everything else for that repo gets NO headers; all other repos get repo.defaultHeaders. The iOS/Desktop twin CoroutineDownloadRepositoryImpl.downloadOnePage (lines 386-390) applies `repo.defaultHeaders` unconditionally - for MangamelloPlus that map (MangamelloPlusRepository.kt:102-119) includes `host: plus.mangamello.com`, `authorization: Bearer null`, `content-type: application/json` and UA `Dart/3.8`, i.e. exactly the headers the Android author deemed wrong for the image CDN (an explicit Host header naming a different vhost than the request URL is a classic 403/404 trigger). Result: downloading a Mangamello Plus chapter can succeed on Android and fail (or behave differently) on iOS/Desktop - platform-divergent behavior in a core flow. The audit postscript in ChapterDownloadService.kt (lines 493-502) even marks the special case 'PRESERVE during any future header-' work, but the nonAndroid port predates/ignores it.
evidence: ChapterDownloadService.kt:253-262 `if (repo is MangamelloPlusRepository) { ... repo.imgsHeader ... } else { repo.defaultHeaders... }` vs CoroutineDownloadRepositoryImpl.kt:387-389 `headers { repo.defaultHeaders.forEach { (name, value) -> append(name, value) } }` with no special case.
suggestedFix: Port the image-host header selection to the nonAndroid engine - ideally as a single shared helper (e.g. `BaseMangaRepository.imageHeadersFor(url)` defaulting to defaultHeaders, overridden by MangamelloPlus) consumed by BOTH download pipelines and the reader/Coil paths, so the rule lives once. Needs owner verification of CDN behavior (sources_repositry types involved are read-only).
verifierNote: Verified both pipelines: ChapterDownloadService.kt:251-263 special-cases 'repo is MangamelloPlusRepository' (imgsHeader with host: cdn.mangamello.com / Dart/3.3 for mangamello image URLs, no headers otherwise) while CoroutineDownloadRepositoryImpl.kt:386-389 sends repo.defaultHeaders unconditionally — for MangamelloPlus that includes 'host' to 'plus.mangamello.com', 'authorization' to 'Bearer null' (MangamelloPlusRepository.kt:104-108) aimed at the wrong vhost. Real platform-divergent download behavior; minimal fix is confinable to the non-frozen nonAndroid file but is behavior-changing on iOS/Desktop, so 'risky' is correct.

title: Both download pipelines bypass the SourceRegistry and always use the legacy parser for page URLs, while the reader uses the generic engine for 12 piloted sources - reading and downloading the same chapter can use different parsers and diverge
detail: ChapterPagesRepositoryImpl.fetchPages routes piloted sources (12 PILOT_APIS) through sourceRegistry.get(api).pages() (generic engine primary, legacy fallback). The download pipelines never consult the registry: Android DownloadWorkerV2.kt:190 and nonAndroid CoroutineDownloadRepositoryImpl.kt:370 both call `repo.fetchChapterDataF(url)` (legacy scraper) directly. Today both parsers work, so output matches; but the precise scenario the pilot subsystem exists for - legacy parser rot or a domain move breaking the legacy path while the generic config keeps working (Lekmanga already moved domains mid-flight) - produces 'chapter reads fine but its download fails' with no fallback, silently and per-platform. The two verb paths also diverge in header provenance (generic: config.headers + captured DataStore headers; download: repo.defaultHeaders) and page ordering/filtering (engine's page.order sort vs each legacy parser).
evidence: ChapterPagesRepositoryImpl.kt:112-121 `if (sourceRegistry.isPiloted(manga.api)) { ... emitAll(client.pages(manga, chapter)) }` vs DownloadWorkerV2.kt:190 and CoroutineDownloadRepositoryImpl.kt:370 `repo.fetchChapterDataF(...)` with no registry reference in either download file.
suggestedFix: Resolve page URLs for downloads through the same seam the reader uses (inject SourceRegistry, or better: reuse ChapterPagesRepository/the registry's pages() flow) in both download engines, so read and download can never disagree on the URL set or headers.
verifierNote: Facts verified: DownloadWorkerV2.kt:190 and CoroutineDownloadRepositoryImpl.kt:370 call repo.fetchChapterDataF directly with no SourceRegistry reference, while ChapterPagesRepositoryImpl.kt:112-118 routes piloted apis through the registry. But the finding itself concedes no user-visible divergence today ('both parsers work, so output matches'), the documented Stage-0 pilot scope is exactly the 4 read repos (sources-subsystem map), and legacy is actually MORE domain-move-resilient than generic (it follows the DB-refreshed base URL — see xcut-dup-4), so the rot scenario is speculative. Latent architecture drift, not current incorrectness -> minor. Suggested fix also under-specified: :shared has no dependency on :sources:contracts (registry is wired in :composeApp), so injecting it into both download engines needs build-graph changes — risky stands.

title: Two base-URL resolution twins drifted: legacy sources follow the server-pushed/user-edited base URL from the sources DB on every launch, but the generic engine's {baseUrl} is frozen at compile time in PILOT_SOURCES_CONFIG_JSON
detail: Legacy BaseManga.getBaseUrl() (BaseManga.kt:57-66) reads `sourcesRepository.getBaseUrlFor(API)` from the Room sources table, which RefreshSourcesUseCase updates from the remote source list on EVERY app launch (App.kt:320-348, SourceRegistryRefreshRepositoryImpl also rewrites stored manga/history/notification image URLs via replaceBaseUrl) and which the repo-settings screen lets users edit. The generic engine has no equivalent: `{baseUrl}` template var and all relative-link absolutization use the static `config.baseUrl` (GenericSourceClient.kt:438, 519; vars() at 513-520), the bundled config is a compile-time string constant (BundledSourcesConfig.kt), and remote config is disabled (DenyRemoteSignatureVerifier). Consequence: after any domain move (this app's #1 documented risk; Lekmanga lekmanga.net -> lek-manga.net already happened mid-development), every verb on all 12 piloted sources first issues a doomed request to the dead host (paying up to the 30s connect timeout before FallbackSourceClient falls back to legacy), and the generic path is silently lost until an app-store release updates the baked-in JSON. User-edited base URLs in repo settings are likewise ignored by the generic path while honored by legacy.
evidence: GenericSourceClient.kt:519 `"baseUrl" to config.baseUrl.trimEnd('/')` (no DB/registry input anywhere in :sources:engine); DefaultSourceRegistry.kt:53-54 builds configs solely from updateManager.activeDocument(); BaseManga.kt:60 `sourcesRepository.getBaseUrlFor(API) ?: BASE_URL`.
suggestedFix: Feed the DB-resolved base URL into the generic path - e.g. have the composition root overlay `config.copy(baseUrl = sourcesDao.getBaseUrlFor(api) ?: config.baseUrl)` when building the GenericSourceClient (with imageBase handled analogously), or add a BaseUrlProvider port to :sources:contracts. Until then the pilot system quietly degrades after every domain move.
verifierNote: All evidence verified: BaseManga.kt getBaseUrl() = sourcesRepository.getBaseUrlFor(API) ?: BASE_URL; App.kt:329-352 refreshes the sources DB every launch explicitly 'so source base URLs follow server-side domain changes'; GenericSourceClient.kt:438/519 uses only static config.baseUrl; DefaultSourceRegistry.kt:54 builds from the bundled-only activeDocument (remote disabled). Worse than latency: FallbackSourceClient falls back on Failure only (pages additionally on empty) — a parked old domain returning 200 garbage yields Success(empty) on home/search and the source silently goes empty with no fallback. Domain moves are the app's documented #1 risk and already happened once (Lekmanga). Not in the documented Stage-1/2 deferral list.

title: formatBytes twins drifted: the round-half-up fix documented in :core's copy was never backported to :platform's copy, so the same byte count renders differently on different screens
detail: :core/util/ByteSizeFormat.formatBytes (lines 18-34) rounds half-up via `(value * 10).roundToLong()` and its KDoc explicitly calls out 'the truncation bias of (v*10).toLong() (which would render 1.945 MB as "1.9 MB" vs native "2.0 MB")' while claiming the logic 'mirrors the internal formatBytes in :platform/filesystem/FileSizeFormatter'. The :platform copy (lines 95-108) still uses the truncating `(value * 10).toLong() / 10.0` and renders via Double.toString. So Details/downloads sizes formatted through :core (DetailsState.kt:71,357) and folder sizes formatted through the :platform FileSizeFormatter actuals can disagree by a tenth (and the :platform copy is also exposed to Double.toString artifacts). Both KDocs claim the copies match - one is now wrong.
evidence: :core `val tenths = (value * 10).roundToLong(); return "${tenths / 10}.${tenths % 10} $unit"` vs :platform `val rounded = (value * 10).toLong() / 10.0; return "$rounded $unit"`.
suggestedFix: :platform already depends on :core - delete the :platform-internal formatBytes and have the three FileSizeFormatter impls call me.manga.yamiapk.core.util.formatBytes.
verifierNote: Verified divergence: core/util/ByteSizeFormat.kt:31-33 rounds half-up ((value*10).roundToLong()) and its KDoc claims to 'mirror' the :platform copy; platform FileSizeFormatter.kt:106 still truncates ((value*10).toLong()/10.0). Both are live (:core via DetailsState.kt:71, :platform via the 3 formatter actuals) so the same byte count can render differently across screens. :platform depends on :core, so the delegation fix compiles and is safe.

title: AppError->localized-message mapping copy-pasted across 5 :ui screens; NetworkErrorMessages is byte-identical in Home and Library, with diverging variants in Details/Reader/Search
detail: HomeScreen.kt:643-688 and LibraryScreen.kt:1646-1700 contain a byte-identical private `NetworkErrorMessages` class + `rememberNetworkErrorMessages()` (11 pre-resolved strings, same statusCode `when`). DetailsScreen.kt:2322-2392 has a superset variant (`AppErrorMessages`, 18 strings) using details_error_* keys where Library uses error_*/library_* keys; ReaderScreen and SearchScreen carry further variants (all resolve error_network_no_connectivity etc.). The pattern (pre-resolve in composable scope because snackbar collectors can't call stringResource) is sound and per-screen translation is the documented convention, but the holder class + status-code table being maintained 5x is drift bait: none of the copies names the challenge statuses the VMs special-case (429, 520-524), and any future code added to one table will miss the others - exactly how the month-abbreviation drift (xcut-dup-6) happened.
evidence: Identical class bodies at HomeScreen.kt:658-688 and LibraryScreen.kt:1663-1700 (same fields, same `messageFor(error, fallback)` when-table 400/401/403/404/408/500/502/503/504).
suggestedFix: Move NetworkErrorMessages + rememberNetworkErrorMessages() into one internal :ui shared file (e.g. components/AppErrorMessages.kt) parameterized on the per-screen fallback string; keep per-screen overrides only where the strings genuinely differ.
verifierNote: Duplication verified: NetworkErrorMessages + rememberNetworkErrorMessages are byte-identical at HomeScreen.kt:643-688 and LibraryScreen.kt:1646-1691, with variant holders in Details/Reader/Search. fixSafety corrected to report-only: the canonical dedup must delete the copy in HomeScreen.kt, which is an owner-WIP forbidden path; partial dedup leaves the Home twin in place.

title: Native's global browser User-Agent was never wired into the KMP Ktor clients: installBrowserHeaders() and DEFAULT_USER_AGENT have zero call sites, while their audit postscripts claim they are live
detail: Native applied a Chrome-114 UA (plus Referer) to every request via an OkHttp interceptor. The KMP port created two artifacts for this - `installBrowserHeaders(referer)` (BrowserHeadersInterceptor.kt:20) and `DEFAULT_USER_AGENT` (HttpClientFactory.kt:22) - but neither is referenced anywhere (verified by repo-wide grep), and none of the three createHttpClient actuals (android/ios/desktop) installs DefaultRequest/UserAgent. So requests from sources that don't set their own UA in defaultHeaders go out with the Ktor engine default UA instead of a browser UA - a per-source-variable UA rule, unlike native's uniform one, and a plausible contributor to source-specific 403s. Both files carry audit postscripts asserting the symbols are 'LIVE-NOT-STALE... consumed by per-source repo HttpClient configurations' / 'consumed by ApiClient-wrapped requests' - false on both counts (stale-KDoc finding per ground rules).
evidence: grep for `installBrowserHeaders` across the repo matches only its own file; grep for `DEFAULT_USER_AGENT` matches only its declaration; HttpClientFactory.{android,ios,desktop}.kt install only ContentNegotiation/Logging/HttpTimeout/HttpCache.
suggestedFix: Owner decision: either install a default browser UA on the shared client (DefaultRequest with DEFAULT_USER_AGENT, matching native posture - per-request appended headers still win) or delete both dead artifacts and correct the postscripts.
verifierNote: Dead-code + stale-postscript halves confirmed: installBrowserHeaders and DEFAULT_USER_AGENT have zero call sites (grep), no createHttpClient actual installs DefaultRequest/UserAgent, and both postscripts claim live consumers that don't exist. But the native-parity premise is wrong: native-app's BrowserHeadersInterceptor is itself dead — defined but never added to any OkHttpClient (AppModule.provideOkHttpClient adds only logging/forceCacheForDados/offlineCache; zero references repo-wide) — so there is no 'uniform native UA' to restore and no parity regression. Correct fix is delete-both + fix postscripts (safe), not installing a default UA.

title: Two image-header mechanisms disagree on precedence: CoilSourceHeaderInterceptor unconditionally overwrites per-request headers that rememberSourceImageRequest already attached
detail: Per-source image headers are attached in two places: (1) request-level by rememberSourceImageRequest (SourceImageRequest.kt) - the reader passes Page.headers captured at fetch time, and the KDoc says this 'bypasses the Coil ImageLoader interceptor host-match'; (2) loader-level by CoilSourceHeaderInterceptor (App.kt:285-310), which runs on EVERY request and, on a host-match with non-empty repo.defaultHeaders, does `req.newBuilder().httpHeaders(networkHeaders)` - REPLACING whatever NetworkHeaders the request already carried. So the 'bypass' only works when the host-match misses or the matched repo is un-hydrated. Today the two maps are usually the same object (legacy repo defaultHeaders), so the clobber is invisible; but for the 12 generic-piloted sources the reader's Page.headers come from `config.headers + DataStore captured headers` (GenericSourceClient.requestHeaders) which can differ from the matched legacy repo's defaultHeaders (e.g. config Referer vs legacy static map; MangamelloPlus's `host:` headers) - the interceptor silently swaps verified-working fetch-time headers for the legacy set.
evidence: App.kt:300-308: no check of existing request headers before `.httpHeaders(networkHeaders)`; SourceImageRequest.kt:25-29 KDoc claims direct attachment bypasses the interceptor path.
suggestedFix: In CoilSourceHeaderInterceptor, skip injection when the incoming request already carries non-empty httpHeaders (`req.httpHeaders.asMap().isNotEmpty() -> proceed()`), making request-level attachment authoritative.
verifierNote: Verified: CoilSourceHeaderInterceptor (App.kt ~300-310) does req.newBuilder().httpHeaders(networkHeaders) with no check of existing request headers — Coil 3's httpHeaders setter REPLACES the NetworkHeaders extra, so a host-match with non-empty legacy repo.defaultHeaders clobbers what rememberSourceImageRequest attached (SourceImageRequest.kt:47/103), contradicting that file's 'bypasses the interceptor' KDoc (lines 25-29). Real precedence bug for piloted sources whose GenericSourceClient headers differ from the legacy repo's; fix changes live image-auth behavior -> risky correct.

title: Generic engine maps transport and parse failures to AppError.Unexpected while every other rework boundary classifies them as Network.Timeout/NoConnectivity/Serialization - FallbackSourceClient even sniffs cause names to compensate
detail: GenericSourceClient.runRequest's catch-all (lines 203-205) wraps any non-cancellation Throwable in `AppError.Unexpected(t.message ?: "generic source error", t)`. Every other classifier in the codebase (MangaDetailsRepositoryImpl, ChapterPagesRepositoryImpl, HomeMappers, LegacyKotlinSourceClient, SourceRegistryRefreshRepositoryImpl) buckets DNS-failure messages into Network.NoConnectivity, timeouts into Network.Timeout, and SourceConfigParser maps malformed JSON to Network.Serialization. FallbackSourceClient.categorise (lines 126-131) acknowledges the gap by string-sniffing `cause::class.simpleName` for 'Serialization'/'Json' to relabel Unexpected as a parse error in diagnostics. Today the legacy fallback masks this (the fallback's well-classified error is what surfaces when both fail), but in generic-only debug mode and for any future generic-only source, offline/timeout failures will render as the generic 'unexpected error' string instead of the no-connectivity/timeout messages, and :ui's per-status messages never apply.
evidence: GenericSourceClient.kt:203-204 `catch (t: Throwable) { AppResult.Failure(AppError.Unexpected(...)) }` vs e.g. HomeMappers.classifyHomeThrowable's connectivity/timeout buckets; FallbackSourceClient.kt:126-131 `val looksLikeParse = causeName.contains("Serialization")...`.
suggestedFix: Apply the same message-heuristic classification (connectivity/timeout -> Network.NoConnectivity/Timeout; serialization causes -> Network.Serialization) in runRequest's catch - ideally the same shared classifier extracted for xcut-dup-1 (it is dependency-free and could live in :core).
verifierNote: Verified: runRequest's catch-all wraps every non-cancellation Throwable in AppError.Unexpected (GenericSourceClient.kt:203-204) while :data classifiers bucket NoConnectivity/Timeout (HomeMappers.kt:167-190) and FallbackSourceClient.categorise compensates by sniffing cause::class.simpleName for Serialization/Json (FallbackSourceClient.kt:126-131). Masked in production because the fallback's well-classified error surfaces when both fail; real for generic-only debug mode.

title: Updates recency-bucketing + chapter-number sort is implemented twice (:data UpdatesRepositoryImpl.groupByDate and :ui UpdatesScreen.groupByRecency) and kept aligned by hand - it has already drifted once
detail: UpdatesRepositoryImpl sorts/buckets updates in :data (sortedByDescending chapterNumber.toDoubleOrNull at line 188) and UpdatesScreen re-derives the identical grouping in :ui (groupByRecency/bucketFor, lines 730-760, including the same `chapterNumber.toDoubleOrNull() ?: 0.0` sort at 743). The :ui KDoc itself records that an earlier audit 'flagged divergent boundary logic' (the exactly-7-days-ago drop) and that the fix was to synchronize the duplicate so 'the two grouping layers are now provably identical at the boundary' - i.e. the twin has already drifted once and was re-aligned by hand rather than de-duplicated. Business grouping logic living in a composable file is also a layering smell (the VM/state layer should deliver display-ready groups).
evidence: UpdatesScreen.kt:718-725 KDoc: 'matches native AND the :data UpdatesRepositoryImpl.groupByDate exactly - the two grouping layers are now provably identical at the boundary... eliminating the divergent boundary logic the audit flagged.'
suggestedFix: Make one layer authoritative: have the presentation state expose the already-bucketed structure produced by :data (or move grouping into the ViewModel/State), and delete the :ui re-implementation.
verifierNote: Verified twin logic: UpdatesRepositoryImpl.groupByDate (data/.../UpdatesRepositoryImpl.kt:180-200) and UpdatesScreen.groupByRecency/bucketFor (:730-763) implement the same bucketing + chapterNumber.toDoubleOrNull sort; the :ui KDoc (:717-724) itself records the prior boundary drift that was hand-re-aligned. Risky is right: consolidating changes emitted wire shape across layers.

title: Systemic token bypass in :ui - 125 inline RoundedCornerShape(...) vs 3 MaterialTheme.shapes reads, and LocalSpacing appears in only 25/52 files with dp literals outnumbering token reads 5-30x in the largest screens
detail: Pattern-level (individual literals were the shard reviewers' scope): the design system defines both an 8-pt Spacing scale (LocalSpacing, theme/Spacing.kt) and a shape scale (YamiShapes 4/8/12/16dp, wired into MaterialTheme), and CLAUDE.md mandates 'Screens read the 8-pt LocalSpacing.current, not dp literals'. Measured adoption: RoundedCornerShape is constructed inline 125 times across :ui (vs 3 MaterialTheme.shapes reads), and per-screen dp-literal counts dwarf LocalSpacing reads (WhatsNew 92:3, Details 79:7, Settings 69:12, Reader 65:8, Search 47:4, About 41:4, Library 37:4). Many literals are deliberate native-parity values, but the corner radii used inline are overwhelmingly the same 4/8/12/16 values the theme already names - meaning a future theme-level radius/spacing change will not propagate, and new screens copy the literal style. This is the drift mechanism, not any single offending dp.
evidence: grep counts: 125 `RoundedCornerShape(` in :ui commonMain outside theme/ vs 3 `MaterialTheme.shapes`; LocalSpacing referenced in 25 of 52 :ui kotlin files.
suggestedFix: Adopt-on-touch policy: when a screen is edited, replace 4/8/12/16dp inline radii with MaterialTheme.shapes.{extraSmall,small,medium,large} and grid paddings with LocalSpacing; optionally add a lint/detekt rule for new code. Bulk rewrite is not recommended (parity risk).
verifierNote: Counts re-measured: 135 inline RoundedCornerShape( in :ui commonMain outside theme/ vs 3 MaterialTheme.shapes reads; LocalSpacing in 25/52 files - matches the finding's magnitude. YamiShapes.kt:36-42 names exactly the 4/8/12/16 values being inlined. Adopt-on-touch recommendation and risky label (bulk rewrite = parity risk) are correct.

title: Cloudflare 403->WebView auto-retry latch uses remember, so it is lost when Details/Reader leaves composition and the auto-retry never fires
detail: rememberCloudflareChallengeSolver (Details, line 259) and rememberReaderCloudflareChallengeSolver (ChapterImagesReworkScreenRoute.kt:191, shared by the legacy-args Reader adapter too) arm a one-shot 'pendingRetry' latch with plain remember { mutableStateOf(false) }, then navigate to Screen.WebView. In Compose Navigation, the outgoing destination's composition is disposed once the forward transition completes; plain remember state does NOT survive that (only rememberSaveable does, via the NavBackStackEntry's SaveableStateHolder). So when the user solves the challenge and the WebView pops, the route adapter recomposes fresh with pendingRetry=false, the currentBackStackEntryFlow replay (replay=1) emits the Details/Reader entry, the condition is false, and onRetry() is never invoked. The masking path doesn't exist either: DetailsViewModel.onEnter (line 294) and ReaderViewModel.onEnter (line 382) early-return on same-identity re-entry, so the re-dispatched OnEnter from the screen's LaunchedEffect does not re-fetch. Net effect: the flagship 'AUTO 403->WebView recovery + auto-retry-on-return' (Reader parity item #6 / Details bug #2) is broken on every entry path — the user returns from the WebView to the same error pane and must tap Retry manually. For the Reader the VM additionally burns its cloudflareAttempts budget (ReaderViewModel.kt:718-724) on solves that never auto-retry. The inline comment 'Survives recomposition (remember) but not process death' is wrong about the actual failure mode (leaving composition, not process death).
evidence: MangaDetailsReworkScreenRoute.kt:259 'var pendingRetry by remember { mutableStateOf(false) }' + :264-273 LaunchedEffect(detailsEntry) { currentBackStackEntryFlow.filter { it == detailsEntry }.collect { if (pendingRetry) { pendingRetry = false; onRetry() } } }; ChapterImagesReworkScreenRoute.kt:191 identical; DetailsViewModel.kt:294 'if (state.value.manga?.matches(manga) == true) return'; ReaderViewModel.kt:382 same-identity early return.
suggestedFix: Change 'remember { mutableStateOf(false) }' to 'rememberSaveable { mutableStateOf(false) }' in both helpers (Boolean is natively saveable). Keep the rest of the choreography unchanged.
verifierNote: Verified end-to-end: MangaDetailsReworkScreenRoute.kt:259 and ChapterImagesReworkScreenRoute.kt (rememberReaderCloudflareChallengeSolver) both use plain remember{mutableStateOf(false)}; Screen.WebView is a regular composable<> destination (App.kt:666), so the Details/Reader content leaves composition after the forward transition and only rememberSaveable state survives via the entry's SaveableStateHolder — on pop-back the latch re-initializes false and the replay-1 currentBackStackEntryFlow emission finds pendingRetry=false. DetailsViewModel.kt:294 and ReaderViewModel.kt:~381 same-identity early returns block the masking refetch; ReaderViewModel.kt:~718-724 increments cloudflareAttempts per emit, so the budget burns on solves that never auto-retry. rememberSaveable fix is correct, multiplatform, and the restarted LaunchedEffect replay fires the retry exactly once. Kept as primary for the group (covers both helpers + the budget-burn consequence).

title: Bottom-nav popUpTo(findStartDestination()) is a no-op for the whole first session after onboarding — tab switches stack up unboundedly and back walks through every visited tab
detail: On first launch the NavHost startDestination is Screen.Welcome (App.kt:533). The onboarding Finish (SourcesScreenRoute.kt:180-185, and the dead RepoSettingsScreenRoute equivalent) navigates to Library with popUpTo(graph.startDestinationId){inclusive=true}, removing Welcome from the back stack. The graph's start destination, however, is still Welcome for the rest of the process. From then on every BottomNavigationBar tab click runs navigate(screen){ popUpTo(navController.graph.findStartDestination().id){ saveState=true }; launchSingleTop; restoreState }, and popUpTo silently pops nothing because Welcome is not on the back stack. Result for the entire first session: each tab switch pushes a NEW entry (launchSingleTop only dedups consecutive same-destination), the stack grows without bound (Library, Home, Library, Home, ...), saveState/restoreState never engage (fresh VM + lost scroll state per visit), and the system back button walks backwards through the full tab-visit history instead of returning to the start tab / exiting. Behaviour self-heals only after process restart (first_launch=false -> start=Library). safePopBackStack's navigateToLibrary fallback has the same inert popUpTo in that session (harmless there). Native/standard expectation is a flat single-entry-per-tab stack.
evidence: BottomNavigationBar.kt:137-143 popUpTo(navController.graph.findStartDestination().id){saveState=true}; SourcesScreenRoute.kt:179-185 prefs.putBoolean("first_launch", false) + navigate(Screen.Library){ popUpTo(startDestinationId){inclusive=true} }; App.kt:532-533 startDestination chosen once from first_launch. androidx semantics: popUpTo to a destination absent from the back stack pops nothing and navigation proceeds.
suggestedFix: Make the post-onboarding stack root coincide with the popUpTo anchor. Simplest: in BottomNavigationBar use popUpTo(Screen.Library.route) (Library is the root both in normal sessions, as start destination, and in the first session after the wizard clear). Alternative: always start the graph at Library and conditionally redirect to Welcome on first launch, keeping the standard findStartDestination() pattern valid. Needs an owner decision on approach.
verifierNote: Verified: App.kt:532-537 picks startDestination=Welcome on first launch; SourcesScreenRoute.kt:179-185 pops Welcome inclusively but the graph's startDestination stays Welcome, so BottomNavigationBar.kt:137-143 popUpTo(findStartDestination().id) pops nothing for the rest of the first session (androidx popUpTo on an absent destination is a silent no-op) — stack grows per tab tap, saveState/restoreState never engage, back walks the tab history. Self-heals on restart as claimed.

title: WhatsNew Get-Started uses raw popBackStack() — a double-tap can pop two entries and leave an empty NavHost (blank app)
detail: Both WhatsNew adapters wire onGetStarted = { navController.popBackStack() } (WhatsNewScreenRoute.kt:227, WhatsNewReworkScreenRoute.kt:93), bypassing the project's safePopBackStack double-tap guard. The first-launch flow is Library -> WhatsNewScreen(true); the stack is [Library, WhatsNew]. A double-tap on the Get-Started CTA executes two synchronous pops: the first pops WhatsNew, the second pops Library, leaving the NavHost with no destination — a blank screen until process restart (a manual popBackStack does not finish the Activity). This is exactly the bug class the 2026-06-02 'regression fix' guard in safePopBackStack.kt was added for, and every other adapter routes back-presses through safePopBackStack. The About -> WhatsNewRework path has the same raw pop but a deeper stack (no blank screen, just a double pop back to Settings).
evidence: WhatsNewScreenRoute.kt:227 / WhatsNewReworkScreenRoute.kt:93 'onGetStarted = { navController.popBackStack() }'; safePopBackStack.kt:19-29 lifecycle-RESUMED guard documented as 'regression fix, 2026-06-02'; LibraryScreenRoute.kt:184 is the inbound edge that makes WhatsNew the top of a 2-entry stack.
suggestedFix: Replace navController.popBackStack() with navController.safePopBackStack() in both adapters (also restores the empty-stack -> Library fallback).
verifierNote: Verified: WhatsNewScreenRoute.kt:227 and WhatsNewReworkScreenRoute.kt:93 both wire onGetStarted={navController.popBackStack()} with no debounce in :ui (WhatsNewScreen.kt:254,267,271,285-287 — header X and Get-Started both call straight through). LibraryScreenRoute redirects via safeNavigate(Screen.WhatsNewScreen(true)) on top of Library (the non-first-launch rootStart, App.kt:533), so the stack is [Library, WhatsNew]; a double-tap performs two synchronous pops, the second popping Library and leaving the NavHost with no destination (programmatic popBackStack does not finish the Activity). safePopBackStack.kt's RESUMED guard ('regression fix, 2026-06-02') exists for exactly this; swapping both call sites to safePopBackStack() is a compile-clean, behavior-preserving fix (single pop unchanged, plus Library fallback).

title: Raw navController.navigate() without the double-tap guard at 4 nav sites — duplicate destinations can be pushed

title: Push notifications have no contentIntent — tapping them neither opens the app nor dismisses them; no deep-link surface exists at all
detail: The FCM notification is built without setContentIntent, so a tap does nothing (and setAutoCancel(true) is inert without a contentIntent, so the notification is only dismissible by swipe). There are zero deep links / nav-graph entry points from external intents anywhere (MainActivity has only MAIN/LAUNCHER, no onNewIntent, no nav arguments from extras; grep for PendingIntent.getActivity across :app/:shared/:platform returns nothing), so for brief item 4: no external entry can ever land on an invalid route — but equally a data-payload push (the admin 'message' use case) cannot bring the user into the app. Native parity caveat: native-app's NotificationHelper/MyFirebaseMessagingService also never call setContentIntent, so this matches native; flagged because a tap-dead push is harmful UX regardless of parity.
evidence: MyFirebaseMessagingService.kt:62-67 builder has setSmallIcon/setContentTitle/setContentText/setAutoCancel only; grep 'setContentIntent|PendingIntent.getActivity' in app/, shared/, platform/ and native-app/ returns no hits.
suggestedFix: Add a PendingIntent.getActivity(MainActivity, FLAG_IMMUTABLE) contentIntent so the tap opens the app at the start destination (Library). Deviates from native; needs owner sign-off.
verifierNote: MyFirebaseMessagingService.kt:62-67 builds the notification with no setContentIntent; grep confirms zero setContentIntent/PendingIntent.getActivity hits in app/shared/platform/composeApp and native-app (only PendingIntent.getBroadcast cancel actions in DownloadWorkerV2). Matches native, but tap-dead push is harmful UX so the parity rule permits flagging; fix deviates from native -> risky is correct.

title: System back while the Search overlay is open pops the Home entry instead of closing the overlay
detail: Search is an overlay-swap on the Home back-stack entry (rendered when HomeState.isSearching), not a destination. There is no BackHandler interception (the commonMain BackHandler shim is a documented App.kt KDoc point-4 TODO), so pressing system back while searching pops Screen.Home itself: in the common case Home is the only/last entry, so back exits the app (or, in the first-session stacked state of xcut-nav-2, returns to a stale previous tab) — the user expects back to close the search overlay and land on the Home grid. The adapter KDoc acknowledges the deferral; recorded so it is tracked as a user-visible back-nav gap, since the canonical exit (Search top-bar close button) is non-obvious on Android where back-to-dismiss is the platform convention.
evidence: HomeReworkScreenRoute.kt:93-133 'if (homeState.isSearching) { SearchScreen(... onClose = { homeViewModel.submit(HomeIntent.OnToggleSearch) }) }' with no back interception; App.kt KDoc item 4 documents the missing commonMain BackHandler.
suggestedFix: Add the expect/actual BackHandler shim (Android actual = androidx.activity.compose.BackHandler) and intercept back in this adapter when homeState.isSearching, submitting HomeIntent.OnToggleSearch instead of popping.
verifierNote: User-visible behavior claim holds, but the mechanism is wrong: a commonMain BackHandler shim ALREADY exists (ui/src/commonMain/.../ui/util/BackHandler.kt + android/ios/desktop actuals) and HomeScreen.kt:201 already has BackHandler(enabled = state.isSearching){ OnToggleSearch } — it never fires because HomeReworkScreenRoute.kt:93 swaps HomeScreen OUT of composition (renders SearchScreen instead) when isSearching, and SearchScreen has no BackHandler. Fix is to add the existing :ui BackHandler to SearchScreen (or stop the adapter-level swap), not to 'add the shim'.

title: WebView host sandbox allows suffix-spoofed hosts via bare endsWith(host)
detail: The main-frame gate allows targetHost == host || targetHost.endsWith(".$host") || targetHost.endsWith(host). The third clause subsumes the first two and additionally admits unrelated registrable domains that merely end with the pinned host string (e.g. pinned 'lekmanga.net' admits 'evil-lekmanga.net'; pinned 'azoramoon.com' admits 'notazoramoon.com'). The sandbox exists to keep the captured Cloudflare cf_clearance cookie bound to the source host, and a malicious in-page redirect to a suffix-spoofed domain defeats the pin. The KDoc says the bare endsWith reproduces the legacy Android rule verbatim (parity-intentional), so this is a report-only hardening note: dropping the third clause strictly tightens the gate with no legitimate-traffic loss (equal host and true subdomains are already covered by the first two clauses).
evidence: WebViewUrlSandbox.kt:51 'return targetHost == host || targetHost.endsWith(".$host") || targetHost.endsWith(host)'.
suggestedFix: Remove the trailing '|| targetHost.endsWith(host)' clause (owner decision — documented as verbatim legacy parity).
verifierNote: WebViewUrlSandbox.kt:51 verified: the bare endsWith(host) third clause subsumes the first two and admits e.g. 'evil-lekmanga.net' for pinned 'lekmanga.net'. KDoc (lines 23-25) documents verbatim legacy parity, so owner-decision/report-only framing is correct; dropping the clause strictly tightens with no legitimate loss.

title: System back while the Search overlay is open exits the Home screen instead of closing search — the intended BackHandler is unreachable
detail: Search is an overlay-swap on the Home back-stack entry: HomeReworkScreenRoute renders SearchScreen INSTEAD OF HomeScreen when `HomeState.isSearching` is true. The native-parity back intercept (`BackHandler(enabled = state.isSearching) { OnToggleSearch }`, ported into HomeScreen.kt:198-201 citing native HomeRoute.kt:289-294) can therefore never fire: while searching, HomeScreen is not in composition (SearchScreen is), and when HomeScreen IS composed, `state.isSearching` is false so the handler is disabled. SearchScreen itself registers no BackHandler (the shared :ui expect/actual exists and is already used by Downloads/Library/Details). Net effect on Android: open search from Home, press the back button/gesture → the NavHost pops the Home entry (to Library or out of the app) with the search overlay and its results silently discarded — a back-stack parity break with native that users hit on every search session.

On Android, system back while searching pops the Home entry. Suggested fix touches only SearchScreen (editable) — safe; the dead HomeScreen handler is owner-WIP/report-only as noted.

title: macOS WebView degraded state shows an infinite loading spinner instead of the documented 'unavailable' placeholder
detail: Main.kt's macOS branch hard-skips KCEF init entirely (Main.kt:162-187) and never calls KcefState.markInitialized(), so `KcefState.initialized` stays false for the whole process lifetime. WebViewHost.desktop.kt's null-client branch interprets `!kcefInitialized` as 'init still in flight' and renders an eternal CircularProgressIndicator (line 106-109); the 'Embedded WebView unavailable on this Desktop runtime.' placeholder (line 114) is unreachable on macOS because the else branch requires `kcefInitialized == true`. So every WebView entry on macOS — including the AUTOMATIC Cloudflare-solver routing from Details/Reader on a 403 — presents a spinner that implies the page will load, and the user has no signal to give up and use open-in-browser. PLATFORM_FEATURE_MATRIX footnote 14 and REMAINING_PROBLEMS §D document the accepted macOS gap as 'always shows an "Embedded WebView unavailable" placeholder' — the current behavior regressed from that documented degraded state when the late-init-recovery handshake was added (the two states were designed for the async-init path that Main.kt does not actually run on macOS).
evidence: Main.kt:162-187 macOS branch: only System.err.println, no KCEF.init, no KcefState.markInitialized(). WebViewHost.desktop.kt:101-117: `if (client == null) { if (!kcefInitialized) { CircularProgressIndicator() } else { Text("Embedded WebView unavailable...") } }` — on macOS kcefInitialized is permanently false.
suggestedFix: Add a third KcefState value (e.g. `markUnavailable()` / sealed status SKIPPED) set in Main.kt's macOS skip branch, and have WebViewHost.desktop.kt render the 'unavailable' placeholder (ideally with an 'Open in external browser' action and a localized string) for that state, keeping the spinner only for a genuinely in-flight async init.
verifierNote: Verified: Main.kt:162-187 macOS branch never calls KCEF.init/markInitialized, so KcefState.initialized is false for the process lifetime and WebViewHost.desktop.kt:106-109 renders an eternal CircularProgressIndicator; the 'unavailable' placeholder (line 114) is unreachable on macOS. Contradicts the documented degraded state (PLATFORM_FEATURE_MATRIX.md footnote 14, REMAINING_PROBLEMS.md:126, and Main.kt:165-166's own comment all claim the placeholder is shown). Affects the automatic 403->solver routing — user gets a spinner that never resolves.

title: Cloudflare-solver auto-routing has no WebView-capability gate — on macOS the user is auto-navigated (up to 2x) into a dead WebView screen
detail: On a challenge-status failure (403/429/503/520-524) DetailsViewModel (line 615-621) and ReaderViewModel (line 717-728) AUTO-emit SolveCloudflareChallenge, which the route adapters translate into navigation to Screen.WebView. There is no platform-capability check, so on Desktop-macOS (embedded WebView unsupported, accepted gap REMAINING_PROBLEMS §D) the user is involuntarily navigated into the degraded WebView screen up to MAX_CLOUDFLARE_ATTEMPTS=2 times per surface before the normal error pane with its open-in-browser fallback is finally shown. Combined with xcut-ux-4's infinite spinner this reads as a hang. Reported as minor because the underlying capability gap is accepted/report-only; the flow-level annoyance (auto-routing into a screen known to be non-functional) is new information.
evidence: DetailsViewModel.kt:615-621 / ReaderViewModel.kt:717-728 emit SolveCloudflareChallenge purely on statusCode + attempts; no platform flag is consulted. Desktop WebViewHost degrades only after navigation.
suggestedFix: Expose an `isEmbeddedWebViewAvailable` flag from :platform (false on macOS when KCEF init is skipped), inject it into the two VMs (or check in the route adapters), and fall back to the ShowError path (error pane already offers Open-in-WebView/browser actions) when unavailable.
verifierNote: Verified: DetailsViewModel.kt:615-621 / ReaderViewModel.kt:717-728 emit SolveCloudflareChallenge on statusCode+attempts only; MangaDetailsReworkScreenRoute navigates to Screen.WebView with no capability check. Main.kt:162-187 hard-skips KCEF init on macOS, so KcefState.initialized stays false and WebViewHost.desktop.kt:106-109 shows an indefinite CircularProgressIndicator — user is auto-routed into it up to MAX_CLOUDFLARE_ATTEMPTS=2 times. The capability gap itself is accepted (report the flow, not the gap).

title: User-facing snackbar text hardcoded in English inside :presentation effects (Downloads, Updates, Complaint, AdminComplaint) — bypasses i18n and the typed-AppError rule
detail: Several rework VMs put raw user-facing strings (including raw exception messages) into effect payloads, violating the project MVI contract ('Effects carry only trigger data, never rendering data or i18n text' / 'Errors are typed AppError, never String'): DownloadsViewModel.emitOnFailure (line 237-244) surfaces `e.message ?: e::class.simpleName ?: "Unknown error"`; UpdatesViewModel uses `throwable.message ?: "Download failed"` (line 227) and `"Failed to load updates"` (line 169, state.errorMessage); ComplaintViewModel uses "Reply sent"/"Complaint updated"/"Complaint deleted"/"Copied to clipboard"/"Unknown error" (lines 168-247); AdminComplaintViewModel mirrors the same (lines 198-255). On the 9 non-English locales (incl. RTL Arabic — the app's main audience) these snackbars render untranslated English or technical exception text. The Phase-10 i18n backfill covered :ui resources but these VM-side strings were missed.
evidence: DownloadsViewModel.kt:237-244: `val message = result.exceptionOrNull()?.let { e -> e.message ?: e::class.simpleName } ?: "Unknown error"; emit(DownloadsEffect.ShowError(message))`.
suggestedFix: Convert these effects to carry typed payloads (AppError or a sealed success-kind enum) and let :ui map them to Res.string.* at the call site, as DetailsScreen/ReaderScreen already do with their errorMessages vocabularies.
verifierNote: All cited sites verified: DownloadsViewModel.kt:237-242, UpdatesViewModel.kt:227/:169, ComplaintViewModel.kt:168/205/216/227/245 hardcoded English / raw Throwable.message in effect payloads, violating the contract's 'Effects never carry i18n text / errors are typed AppError'. title: Onboarding notification-permission 'denied' toast fires immediately on auto-request, before the user has answered the system dialog
detail: The denial toast is keyed on `LaunchedEffect(hasPermission, autoRequested.value) { if (autoRequested.value && !hasPermission) toast }`. On first composition `autoRequested` flips to true and `permissionRequester.request()` launches the ASYNC system dialog; `hasPermission` is still false at that instant, so the effect re-runs with (false, true) and shows 'you need to enable notifications' while the permission dialog is still on screen (Android 13+). A user who then GRANTS still saw a denial nag during onboarding. The toast should only fire after the request actually completes with a denial.
evidence: ThemeSelectionScreenRoute.kt:155-166: the toast effect keys on the request *flag*, not on request *completion*; permissionRequester.request() is asynchronous and hasPermission's StateFlow only updates after the user responds.
suggestedFix: Surface a completion signal from NotificationPermissionRequester (e.g. suspend request() returning the result, or a requestCompleted flow) and show the denial toast only on an actual post-response denial.
verifierNote: ThemeSelectionScreenRoute.kt:155-166: LaunchedEffect(Unit) flips autoRequested=true and fires the async request(); the toast effect is keyed on (hasPermission, autoRequested.value), so it re-runs with (false,true) immediately — hasPermission's StateFlow can't have updated yet — showing the denial toast while the Android 13+ system dialog is still pending, even for users who then grant.
